INTRODUCTION

介绍

We live in an age of unprecedented wealth, yet our prosperity hangs by a thread. I watch with growing concern as some of our politicians erode its foundations. Even worse, they do so with impunity: most journalists do not call them out, nor do most voters, who, after all, elected them.

我们生活在一个前所未有的财富时代，然而我们的繁荣却岌岌可危。我越来越担忧地看到，一些政客正在侵蚀繁荣的根基。更糟糕的是，他们这样做却逍遥法外：大多数记者没有谴责他们，大多数选民也没有，毕竟是选民把他们选了上台。

Why? Because we take prosperity for granted. But history teaches us that prosperity is not the norm; poverty is, and we are always a few bad decisions away from regressing into it. Consider Venezuela : once the wealthiest country in South America , it is now the poorest.

为什么？因为我们把繁荣视为理所当然。但历史告诉我们，繁荣并非常态；贫困才是，而且我们往往只需几个错误的决定就会再次陷入贫困。以委内瑞拉为例：它曾经是南美洲最富有的国家，如今却成了最贫穷的国家。

We have lost track of how we arrived at our current position and what it takes to maintain it. Instead of celebrating those who create prosperity, we elect those who redistribute it, until only crumbs remain. We optimize the present while neglecting to build the future.

我们已经忘记了如何走到今天这一步，以及维持现状需要付出怎样的努力。我们非但没有赞扬那些创造繁荣的人，反而选举那些重新分配财富的人，直到最后只剩下残羹剩饭。我们只顾眼前利益，却忽视了建设未来。

I wrote this book as both a warning and a guide. For readers in wealthy countries, it is a wake-up call: here are the policy mistakes that can undo decades of progress, and here is how to spot them before it is too late. For those in developing nations, it serves as a roadmap to prosperity, illustrating which strategies are effective and which are not.

我写这本书既是为了发出警示，也是为了提供指导。对于富裕国家的读者来说，这是一记警钟：书中列举了可能使数十年进步付诸东流的政策失误，并阐述了如何在为时过晚之前发现这些失误。对于发展中国家的读者来说，这本书则是一份通往繁荣的路线图，阐明了哪些策略行之有效，哪些无效。

Most importantly, it provides everyone with the tools to advocate for better policies, whether at the dinner table or the voting booth. The goal is to help build countries that are wealthier, cleaner, safer, and freer.

最重要的是，它为每个人提供了倡导更佳政策的工具，无论是在餐桌上还是在投票站。其目标是帮助建设更富裕、更清洁、更安全、更自由的国家。

# ↩

Book overview

书籍概述

This book comprises three parts and twenty-six chapters.

本书共分为三部分，二十六章。

The Prologue examines a recent environmental preservation project in Great Britain to explain why the efficiency of public spending matters. Through the lens of two fictional countries, Moralia and Pragmatia , it shows how practical approaches to public spending often yield better results than purely moral ones.

序言以英国近期一项环境保护项目为例，阐释了公共支出效率的重要性。文章通过虚构的两个国家——莫拉利亚和普拉格玛提亚——的视角，展现了务实的公共支出方式往往比纯粹的道德方式更能取得成效。

Part I , “ Scarcity and Abundance ,” explores the choices that lead nations to prosperity or poverty. It argues that prosperity arises from creating abundance through efficiency and accountability. A society needs surplus production to provide a decent life for all and sustain institutions that uphold fairness, health, and sustainability. We need not maximize productivity, but must keep it above a critical threshold. Productive nations share prosperity, unproductive ones share poverty.

第一部分“稀缺与富足”探讨了国家走向繁荣或贫困的选择。它认为，繁荣源于通过效率和问责制创造富足。一个社会需要剩余产品来保障所有人的体面生活，并维持维护公平、健康和可持续性的制度。我们不必追求生产力最大化，但必须将其保持在临界阈值之上。生产力高的国家共享繁荣，生产力低下的国家共享贫困。

How can we, however, boost national productivity without cutting corners or exhausting ourselves? One key is letting wages signal which jobs society values most, allowing unproductive jobs to fade naturally while helping affected workers transition. Nations prosper when they treat low wages and high prices as structural issues, and decline when they rely on superficial fixes.

然而，我们如何在不偷工减料或过度消耗自身资源的情况下提高国家生产力呢？关键在于让工资水平反映社会最重视的职业，让低效的职业自然消亡，同时帮助受影响的劳动者顺利过渡。国家若将低工资和高物价视为结构性问题，就能繁荣发展；而若仅仅依赖表面功夫，则会走向衰落。

Examining policy missteps around the world, we uncover another path to poverty: swelling opportunity costs. Nations grow poorer when they focus on the wrong priorities or spend tax money inefficiently. Instead of debating tax rates, we should concentrate on spending current tax receipts more wisely. Part I concludes with a review of principles and policies that promote prosperity and prevent poverty.

通过审视世界各地的政策失误，我们发现了通往贫困的另一条途径：机会成本不断攀升。当国家把精力放在错误的优先事项上或低效使用税款时，它们就会变得更加贫穷。与其争论税率，我们不如集中精力更明智地使用当前的税收收入。第一部分最后回顾了促进繁荣和预防贫困的原则和政策。

But why do nations so often make poor choices that lead to decline? This question drives Part II .

但为什么国家常常做出导致衰落的糟糕选择？这个问题将在第二部分展开。

Part II , “ Virtue and Decadence ,” investigates the cultural factors behind good and bad policy decisions. Using examples from around the world, it shows how nations decline when they pursue luxuries before securing basic needs. Rushing to solve problems can mean overlooking stronger, long-term solutions.

第二部分“美德与颓废”探讨了良好和不良政策决策背后的文化因素。它以世界各地的案例为例，揭示了当国家在满足基本需求之前追求奢侈品时，是如何走向衰落的。仓促解决问题往往意味着忽略了更有效、更长远的解决方案。

The dangers of groupthink deserve special attention, especially in identity politics, where the urge to protect "our own" can sometimes excuse poor behavior. As the saying goes, the road to hell is paved with good intentions; therefore, intentions must be subordinate to outcomes.

群体思维的危害尤其值得关注，尤其是在身份政治中，维护“自己人”的冲动有时会成为不良行为的借口。正如俗语所说，通往地狱的路是由善意铺成的；因此，意图必须服从于结果。

We also examine the critical role of journalism in preserving democracy and prosperity. Nations thrive when truth circulates and falter when it is obscured. Better scientific peer review, falsifiable policies, and journalists who resist short-term political pressures are essential.

我们还探讨了新闻业在维护民主和繁荣方面发挥的关键作用。国家繁荣昌盛离不开真相的传播，而真相一旦被掩盖，国家就会衰落。更完善的科学同行评审、可证伪的政策以及能够抵制短期政治压力的记者都至关重要。

While Part I offered economic solutions and Part II presented cultural ones, implementing them is not simple. It is essential to avoid becoming tyrants while we pursue prosperity.

第一部分提出了经济解决方案，第二部分提出了文化解决方案，但实施起来并非易事。在追求繁荣的同时，我们必须避免成为暴君。

Part III , “ Utopia and Dystopia ,” addresses this challenge. It shows how good intentions can lead to disastrous outcomes and offers safeguards.

第三部分“乌托邦与反乌托邦”探讨了这一挑战。它揭示了良好的初衷如何导致灾难性的后果，并提出了相应的保障措施。

We explore democracy's paradox: although democratic systems are superior to dictatorships, many autocracies emerged from democracies. What warning signs indicate we are sliding toward autocracy, and how can we reverse it before it is too late?

我们探讨民主的悖论：尽管民主制度优于独裁制度，但许多专制政权却从民主制度中演变而来。有哪些预警信号表明我们正在滑向专制？我们又该如何在为时已晚之前扭转局面？

We also examine the foundations of civilization and how to prevent its decline into barbarism. One key principle stands out: to preserve our rights, we must guarantee them even to our enemies.

我们还探讨了文明的根基以及如何防止文明堕入野蛮状态。其中一个关键原则尤为突出：为了维护我们的权利，我们必须保障即使是敌人的权利。

Finally, we discuss the thin line between utopias and dystopias: the dangerous belief that the end justifies the means. Coercion can never achieve utopia, for it instantly turns into dystopia. Does this make utopia impossible? I offer an optimistic perspective and a possible way forward.

最后，我们探讨乌托邦与反乌托邦之间那条微妙的界限：那种认为目的可以为手段辩护的危险信念。强制永远无法实现乌托邦，因为它会立即演变成反乌托邦。这是否意味着乌托邦根本不可能实现？我提出了一种乐观的观点和一条可能的未来之路。

A guide to more constructive discussions

如何开展更具建设性的讨论

The true test of a nonfiction book is not its comprehensiveness or scholarly complexity, but what stays with the reader after they close the cover. Therefore , rather than trying to cover everything about poverty and prosperity, this book focuses on a few key principles, explained clearly enough that you can think about them independently and discuss them with others.

衡量一本非虚构类书籍的真正标准，并非其内容的全面性或学术的复杂性，而是读者合上书页后能留下的印象。因此，本书并非试图涵盖贫困与繁荣的方方面面，而是聚焦于几个关键原则，并以清晰易懂的方式加以阐释，使读者能够独立思考并与他人展开讨论。

As we will see in the chapter “ The Quality of the Discourse ,” nations thrive when citizens keep political discussions focused on what truly matters. Good leaders emerge, and smart policies follow. Conversely , when public debate degenerates into weak arguments or distractions, nations tend to drift toward poverty. At its core, this book is a guide to more constructive political conversations.

正如我们将在“话语质量”一章中看到的那样，当公民将政治讨论聚焦于真正重要的事情时，国家才能繁荣昌盛。优秀的领导者会涌现，明智的政策也会随之而来。反之，当公共辩论沦为薄弱的论点或无关紧要的干扰时，国家往往会走向贫困。本书的核心在于指导人们如何进行更具建设性的政治对话。

I offer fresh perspectives on vital issues, supported by historical facts, clear examples, and straightforward logic. You will gain the tools and language to engage meaningfully in debates about how societies can prosper.

我将以历史事实、清晰的例证和简洁的逻辑，为重要议题提供全新的视角。您将获得参与有关社会如何繁荣发展的辩论所需的工具和语言。

PROLOGUE

序幕

THE RATIONAL ENVIRONMENTALIST

理性环保主义者

I n 2024, the UK government spent $129 million on a one-kilometer-long shelter to protect about 300 bats during the construction of a high-speed rail line. That’s roughly $380,000 per bat. ⁠ 1

2024年，英国政府斥资1.29亿美元建造了一条长达一公里的蝙蝠庇护所，以在高铁建设期间保护约300只蝙蝠。这相当于每只蝙蝠约38万美元。

Bats are vital for the ecosystem, and protecting them is important. However , this astronomical cost should give any environmentalist pause. With $129 million, how many more bats or other endangered species could we have protected? How many wetlands could we have restored, or acres of forest preserved?

蝙蝠对生态系统至关重要，保护它们意义重大。然而，如此天文数字般的费用应该让所有环保人士深思。1.29亿美元，我们本可以保护多少蝙蝠或其他濒危物种？我们本可以修复多少湿地，或者保护多少英亩的森林？

Some environmentalists celebrate any win, regardless of cost. That is understandable, but it ignores the undeniable fact that resources are limited. Every dollar spent inefficiently is a dollar unavailable for other environmental projects. Overspending on one initiative forces a lose-lose choice: work harder to generate more resources or accept that we accomplish less overall. Neither is desirable.

有些环保主义者不计代价地庆祝任何胜利。这可以理解，但却忽略了一个不容置疑的事实：资源是有限的。每一美元的低效使用，就意味着其他环保项目少了一美元可用。过度投入某一项举措，会让我们陷入两难境地：要么更加努力地创造更多资源，要么接受整体成果减少的现实。这两种选择都不可取。

A rational environmentalist aiming to maximize positive impact must care about using resources efficiently.

理性环保主义者若想最大限度地发挥积极作用，就必须重视资源的有效利用。

Finite and infinite resources

有限资源和无限资源

I’m not saying we should always ruthlessly prioritize everything or run a cost-benefit analysis on every action. After all, we all care about different things. If someone wants to spend their free time on a cause they care about, well, the world runs on such acts of care.

我并不是说我们应该总是冷酷无情地对所有事情进行优先级排序，或者对每项行动都进行成本效益分析。毕竟，我们每个人关心的事情都不一样。如果有人想把空闲时间花在自己关心的事业上，那么，世界正是靠着这样的奉献精神运转的。

But when it comes to public spending, where resources are scarce, we must use them efficiently. Whenever a project or agency delivers less than its budget and staff allow, society ends up worse off. This applies not only to environmental protection but also to education, healthcare, social support, and other areas.

但公共支出资源有限，我们必须高效利用。任何项目或机构如果未能达到预算和人员配置要求，最终都会损害社会利益。这不仅适用于环境保护，也适用于教育、医疗、社会保障等其他领域。

I know this might sound counterintuitive. If we care about the environment, shouldn’t we spend as much as possible on it? More spending does produce more results, usually, but that’s not the full story.

我知道这听起来可能有点反直觉。如果我们关心环境，难道不应该尽可能多地投入资金吗？通常来说，投入越多，效果就越好，但这并非全部真相。

To explain what’s really going on, let me introduce two fictional countries: Moralia and Pragmatia .

为了解释事情的真相，让我介绍两个虚构的国家：莫拉利亚和普拉格马蒂亚。

Moralia and Pragmatia

道德与实用主义

Moralia and Pragmatia are two nations identical in every way except one. Moralia's government prides itself on making the most ethical choices, while Pragmatia focuses on efficient spending.

莫拉利亚和普拉格玛提亚这两个国家除了一个区别外，其他方面都完全相同。莫拉利亚政府以做出最合乎道德的选择而自豪，而普拉格玛提亚则注重高效的支出。

Both countries have a $500 million budget for environmental preservation.⁠ 2 Moralia funds any project that benefits the environment, and is unable to say no to a project that would save animal lives. So , it spends $129 million on a project that saves 300 bats, $200 million on one that saves 200 bears, $170 million on a project to save a rare bird species, and oopsie, there’s no money left for anything else. Pragmatia , in contrast, prioritizes its environmental budget, asking each project to submit a proposal and funding them in order of impact per dollar spent. It allocates $20 million to save acres of wetland, $30 million for another project that saves 20,000 bats elsewhere, and so on. Because of this prioritization, Pragmatia’s projects achieve a far greater positive impact on the environment than Moralia’s .

两国都拥有5亿美元的环境保护预算。莫拉利亚（Moralia）会资助任何有益于环境的项目，并且无法拒绝任何能够拯救动物生命的项目。因此，它花费1.29亿美元用于一个拯救300只蝙蝠的项目，2亿美元用于一个拯救200只熊的项目，1.7亿美元用于一个拯救珍稀鸟类的项目，结果，哎呀，没有钱再做其他事情了。相比之下，普拉格玛蒂亚（Pragmatia）会优先考虑其环境预算，要求每个项目提交提案，并根据每美元投入的影响程度进行资助。它拨款2000万美元用于保护数英亩的湿地，3000万美元用于另一个在其他地方拯救2万只蝙蝠的项目，以此类推。由于这种优先排序，普拉格玛蒂亚的项目对环境的积极影响远大于莫拉利亚的项目。

However, Moralians are offended: to prioritize, Pragmatians had to put a value on animal life. Who are you to say how much a bat’s life is worth? Pragmatians reply calmly that, while it is uncomfortable and perhaps unfair to decide the worth of a life, the results speak for themselves: more animals were saved by selecting more efficient projects. One need not even assign a number to a bat’s life; it suffices to ask, “ We have this many millions; what projects save the most bats with this money?”

然而，道德主义者对此感到不满：实用主义者为了进行优先排序，不得不给动物的生命赋予价值。你凭什么来评判一只蝙蝠的生命值多少钱？实用主义者冷静地回应说，虽然决定一条生命的价值令人不安，或许也不公平，但结果不言自明：选择更高效的项目拯救了更多动物。我们甚至无需给蝙蝠的生命赋予一个具体的数字；只需问问自己：“我们有这么多钱；哪些项目能用这些钱拯救最多的蝙蝠？”

This story shows that being practical about resource use often helps more than focusing purely on moral imperatives. I am not suggesting we reduce everything to numbers and spreadsheets: that would miss the point. Yet when resources are limited, we must use them wisely. Every time we spend resources inefficiently, we forgo opportunities to do more valuable work. This is not just abstract economics; it has real consequences. Many once-prosperous nations began to decline by forgetting that resources are finite and gradually making poorer choices about how to use them.

这个故事表明，务实地利用资源往往比单纯关注道德准则更有帮助。我并非建议我们把一切都简化为数字和电子表格：那样就偏离了重点。然而，当资源有限时，我们必须明智地使用它们。每一次低效地使用资源，我们都错失了从事更有价值的工作的机会。这并非抽象的经济学理论，它会产生切实的后果。许多曾经繁荣的国家之所以开始衰落，正是因为它们忘记了资源的有限性，并在资源利用方面做出了越来越糟糕的选择。

Don’t get me wrong: many conservation experts already think this way. However , public discourse and political incentives often don’t. That’s a serious problem, as these forces strongly influence how resources are allocated and, consequently, outcomes. Similarly , real-world inefficiencies rarely result from bad intentions or incompetence; more often, they arise from political and bureaucratic constraints. This is precisely why spending efficiency should play a larger role in public discourse.

别误会我的意思：许多自然保护专家确实持有这种观点。然而，公众舆论和政治激励机制往往并非如此。这是一个严重的问题，因为这些因素会极大地影响资源的分配方式，进而影响最终结果。同样，现实世界中的效率低下很少是出于恶意或能力不足；更多时候，它们源于政治和官僚主义的制约。正因如此，提高支出效率应该在公众讨论中发挥更大的作用。

I will explore this topic more deeply in later chapters and offer practical solutions. But first, let’s tackle a more fundamental question: what actually creates prosperity?

我将在后面的章节中更深入地探讨这个话题，并提供切实可行的解决方案。但首先，让我们来探讨一个更根本的问题：究竟是什么创造了繁荣？

1 Sources: “HS2 spending more than £100m to build bat shed,” The Independent, 2024-11-07 ; and “HS2 building £100m shed to protect bats from trains,” Steve Robson, 2024-11-12.

1 来源：“HS2 花费超过 1 亿英镑建造蝙蝠棚”，《独立报》，2024 年 11 月 7 日；以及“HS2 建造价值 1 亿英镑的棚子以保护蝙蝠免受火车伤害”，史蒂夫·罗布森，2024 年 11 月 12 日。

2 Note: this example differs slightly from the opening anecdote. In the UK, the $129 million was spent by the construction company, whereas in Moralia and Pragmatia, it comes from the environmental budget. This distinction will be resolved in a later chapter, which argues that the costs of fulfilling environmental regulations should be attributed to the environmental budget to foster accountability, consideration of opportunity costs, and prioritization.

注2：此例与开篇轶事略有不同。在英国，这1.29亿美元是由建筑公司支出的，而在《道德与实用主义》一书中，这笔钱则来自环境预算。这一区别将在后续章节中加以阐述，该章节论证，履行环境法规的成本应计入环境预算，以促进问责制、机会成本考量和优先排序。

PART I
第一部分

SCARCITY AND ABUNDANCE

稀缺与富足

“What causes poverty? Nothing . It’s the original state, the default and starting point. The real question is, what causes prosperity?”

PER BYLUND

“贫困的根源是什么？没有什么根源。贫困是最初的状态，是默认状态，是起点。真正的问题是，繁荣的根源是什么？”——佩尔·比伦德

What causes prosperity?

什么因素会带来繁荣？

A common answer is natural resources. They are clearly important (a country is better off with them than without), but they are neither necessary nor sufficient. If they were necessary, no successful country would exist without them; yet Singapore exists and thrives.⁠ 1 And if they were sufficient, no country rich in resources would be poor; yet Venezuela exists and struggles: despite having the largest oil reserves in the world⁠ 2 and once being among South America’s wealthiest nations, it is now one of the poorest.

一个常见的答案是自然资源。它们显然很重要（一个国家拥有自然资源肯定比没有好），但它们既非必要条件，也非充分条件。如果自然资源是必要条件，那么任何成功的国家都不会在没有自然资源的情况下存在；然而新加坡依然存在并蓬勃发展。如果自然资源是充分条件，那么任何资源丰富的国家都不会贫穷；然而委内瑞拉依然存在并苦苦挣扎：尽管拥有世界上最大的石油储量，并且曾经是南美洲最富裕的国家之一，如今却沦为最贫穷的国家之一。

Others argue that prosperity or lack thereof stems from a country’s history of colonialism and oppression. While these forces have undoubtedly shaped our world, this explanation also falls short. For example, Portugal , once a colonial power, ⁠ 3 later ranked among the poorest nations in Western Europe . Conversely , Singapore and South Korea , both former colonies that faced major hardships, have achieved remarkable prosperity.⁠ 4 Even more striking, Haiti and the Dominican Republic share the same island and colonial history, yet their economic paths diverged sharply due to different policies.

另一些人则认为，一个国家的繁荣或衰落源于其殖民和压迫的历史。虽然这些因素无疑塑造了我们的世界，但这种解释也存在不足。例如，葡萄牙曾是殖民强国，后来却跻身西欧最贫穷的国家之列。相反，新加坡和韩国这两个曾经饱受苦难的前殖民地，如今都取得了令人瞩目的繁荣。更引人注目的是，海地和多米尼加共和国拥有相同的岛屿和殖民历史，但由于政策不同，它们的经济发展道路却截然不同。

More importantly, although natural resources and historical forces matter, they are factors beyond our control. Focusing on them does not help us move forward. So , for the rest of this book, we will focus on solutions that we can control, and ask again:

更重要的是，尽管自然资源和历史因素固然重要，但它们是我们无法控制的。关注它们并不能帮助我们前进。因此，本书余下部分将着重探讨我们可以掌控的解决方案，并再次提出这个问题：

What causes prosperity?

什么因素会带来繁荣？

* * *

A note on terminology

关于术语的说明

The word “prosperity” refers not only to financial success but also to other forms of well-being, such as happiness, health, safety, a clean environment, and a vibrant community.

“繁荣”一词不仅指经济上的成功，还包括其他形式的福祉，例如幸福、健康、安全、清洁的环境和充满活力的社区。

The first third of this book focuses on material prosperity because it is difficult to be happy if you struggle to survive or lack access to healthcare and other basic services, which require resources to exist and function effectively. Later chapters address aspects of prosperity related to civil rights, communities, and the environment.

本书前三分之一着重探讨物质繁荣，因为如果连生存都成问题，或者缺乏医疗保健和其他基本服务（这些服务都需要资源才能生存和有效运作），就很难感到幸福。后面的章节则探讨了与公民权利、社区和环境相关的繁荣层面。

1 Singapore’s strategic location on the Strait of Malacca is valuable, but that advantage has existed for centuries. If location were destiny, why didn’t Singapore prosper earlier, and why haven’t other countries along the Strait achieved similar success?

新加坡位于马六甲海峡的战略位置固然重要，但这种优势已经存在了几个世纪。如果地理位置决定命运，为什么新加坡没有更早繁荣起来？为什么海峡沿岸其他国家也没有取得类似的成功？

On the topic of Singapore, many bring the argument that its tiny size doesn’t make it representative. I agree its size might have helped, but it was also a hindrance, in terms of political and military weight or access to manpower and other resources. I could see many small countries bringing their small scale as a weakness and not as a strength. That said, while it’s true that many of their policies benefited from their small size, it doesn’t mean that those policies couldn’t have also benefited larger countries, with the necessary adjustments (of course, this doesn’t apply to all their policies, but some).

关于新加坡，很多人认为它国土面积小，不具代表性。我同意新加坡的国土面积小或许有利，但同时也存在劣势，例如在政治和军事实力、人力及其他资源获取方面。很多小国都把国土面积小视为劣势而非优势。话虽如此，虽然新加坡的许多政策确实受益于其国土面积小的特点，但这并不意味着这些政策经过必要的调整后，就不能惠及国土面积更大的国家（当然，这并非适用于所有政策，但确实存在一些）。

The size argument for Singapore is often like saying Nikola Jokic is only a great NBA player because he’s 6′ 11″. Height might have helped him, but his skill and technique mattered most. Similarly, Singapore’s success mostly depends on its governance.

新加坡的成功很大程度上取决于其治理水平，这就像说尼古拉·约基奇之所以成为伟大的NBA球员仅仅是因为他身高6英尺11英寸（约2.11米）一样。身高或许对他有所帮助，但他的技术才是最重要的。同样，新加坡的成功也主要取决于其治理水平。

2 Venezuela has the largest proven oil reserves, about 10% more than Saudi Arabia (second-largest) and roughly 50% more than Iran (third-largest). Sources: OPEC Energy Review, 2021-05-07, and U.S. Energy Information Administration, retrieved 2023-10-05.

2. 委内瑞拉拥有最大的已探明石油储量，比沙特阿拉伯（储量第二大）多约10%，比伊朗（储量第三大）多约50%。资料来源：欧佩克能源评论，2021年5月7日；美国能源信息署，2023年10月5日检索。

3 While Portugal isn’t poor by global standards, it lags behind Western European neighbors. Even if colonial power conferred an advantage, it is worth asking why much of that prosperity was lost.

3 虽然按全球标准衡量，葡萄牙并不算贫穷，但它落后于西欧邻国。即便殖民统治曾带来优势，也值得探究为何葡萄牙失去了大部分繁荣。

4 Singapore and South Korea overcame colonial rule (British and Japanese, respectively) to achieve success. South Korea also rebuilt after the devastation of the Korean War.

4. 新加坡和韩国分别摆脱了英国和日本的殖民统治，取得了成功。韩国还在朝鲜战争的破坏后进行了重建。

1

FROM SCARCITY TO ABUNDANCE

从稀缺到富足

I n the beginning, there was scarcity. Although medieval farmers worked hard, they did not harvest much food from their efforts. When not working in the fields, they built tools or sewed clothes, but it still took days to produce a shirt, meaning they could only have a few items of clothing.

起初，物资匮乏。尽管中世纪的农民辛勤劳作，却收成甚微。他们不下地干活时，就制作工具或缝制衣物，但即便如此，制作一件衬衫也需要数天时间，这意味着他们只能拥有寥寥几件衣物。

Of course, many factors contributed to their poverty. Nobles would take about a third of their harvest.⁠ 1 Sickness would make them weak and less effective as farmers. Wars caused disruption and devastation. And yet, even if there were no taxes, no illnesses, and no wars, they would still be poor, purely because farming and sewing were inefficient processes.

当然，导致他们贫困的因素有很多。贵族会拿走他们大约三分之一的收成。疾病会削弱他们的体质，降低他们的耕作效率。战争会带来混乱和破坏。然而，即使没有赋税、没有疾病、没有战争，他们仍然会贫穷，原因很简单，就是因为耕作和缝纫效率低下。

Even if a benevolent king had distributed the food perfectly fairly, they would still have gone hungry. That’s because the kingdom did not produce enough food to feed everyone adequately. And even if the king ordered every tailor to work around the clock making clothes for everyone, they would still have owned only a few items because making clothes by hand was so time-consuming that it was impossible to produce enough for everyone.⁠ 2

即使一位仁慈的国王将食物分配得尽善尽美，他们仍然会挨饿。这是因为王国生产的粮食不足以养活所有人。即使国王命令所有裁缝日夜不停地为每个人缝制衣服，他们也只能拥有寥寥几件，因为手工制作衣服非常耗时，根本不可能生产出足够的衣服供所有人穿着。

When production is inefficient, poverty is inevitable, and no system of redistribution can fix that.

生产效率低下，贫困不可避免，任何再分配制度都无法解决这个问题。

The Great Transformation

大转型

The good news is that, over the centuries, everything changed. Not because people worked harder (medieval farmers already worked very hard), but because they worked more efficiently. Today’s farmers no longer break their backs more than their ancestors did, yet each produces enough food to feed hundreds. Modern agriculture is so efficient that only about 2% of citizens need to farm,⁠ 3 freeing the rest of the population to create the vast array of goods and services we enjoy.

好消息是，几个世纪以来，一切都发生了改变。这并非因为人们更加辛勤劳作（中世纪的农民已经非常辛苦了），而是因为他们的劳动效率更高了。如今的农民不再像他们的祖先那样劳作，却能生产出足够数百人食用的粮食。现代农业效率极高，只需约2%的人口从事农业，其余人口便可腾出精力去创造我们所享用的种类繁多的商品和服务。

The same human effort that once could not even feed a village now feeds a city, and the same hours of work that once made a single shirt now produce hundreds. This is the power of efficiency: not working harder, but getting more from each hour of work.

过去连一个村庄都养不活的人力，如今却能养活一座城市；过去只能做一件衬衫的工时，如今却能做成数百件。这就是效率的力量：不是更努力地工作，而是每小时工作产出更多。

This shift from scarcity to abundance through efficiency is the secret behind modern prosperity.

通过提高效率实现从匮乏到富足的转变，是现代繁荣的秘诀。

There is no cure for scarcity but abundance. Everything else merely allocates scarcity.

PATRICK MCKENZIE

唯有富足才能根除匮乏。其他一切都只是加剧匮乏而已。——帕特里克·麦肯齐

It’s not about the money

这不是钱的问题。

Of course, prosperity requires more than efficient production and trade; it also depends on peace, civil rights, environmental protection, and many other factors. Yet , all these essential elements of modern society depend on having enough resources to sustain them.

当然，繁荣不仅仅需要高效的生产和贸易；它还取决于和平、公民权利、环境保护以及许多其他因素。然而，现代社会的所有这些基本要素都依赖于充足的资源来维持。

Doctors, teachers, and countless others can do their vital work only because the broader economy produces enough to support them. Without that productivity, we could not maintain hospitals, schools, or environmental programs: everyone would be too busy growing food or meeting their basic needs.

医生、教师以及无数其他人员之所以能够从事这些至关重要的工作，是因为整体经济的生产足以支撑他们的生计。如果没有这种生产力，我们就无法维持医院、学校或环境项目的运转：每个人都将忙于种植粮食或满足基本生活需求。

Without efficient production, there is no surplus to fund the institutions that make society fair, healthy, and sustainable.

如果没有高效的生产，就没有盈余来资助那些使社会公平、健康和可持续发展的机构。

Why this matters today

为什么这件事在今天很重要

I expect most readers to live in a country that has already at least partially solved the problem of scarcity. Why should they care about efficiency?

我预计大多数读者都生活在资源稀缺问题已经得到一定程度解决的国家。他们为什么要关心效率呢？

Because modern societies can easily slip back into hardship if they stop paying attention. When efficiency and productivity decline, even wealthy nations can drift into poverty, slowly at first, then more rapidly as problems compound. We will explore this process in more detail later.

因为现代社会一旦疏忽大意，很容易再次陷入困境。当效率和生产力下降时，即使是富裕国家也可能滑向贫困，起初速度较慢，但随着问题的累积，贫困化的速度会越来越快。我们将在后面更详细地探讨这一过程。

For now, remember this: prosperity is not humanity’s natural state; it’s poverty.

现在，请记住：繁荣不是人类的自然状态；贫穷才是。

We escaped scarcity through efficient production, and without it, we risk sliding back into it.

我们通过高效生产摆脱了物资匮乏的困境，而如果没有高效生产，我们就有重新陷入物资匮乏的风险。

* * *

In the next chapter, we will examine exactly how this works, using what I call the Abundance Equation .

在下一章中，我们将使用我称之为“丰饶方程式”的理论，来详细探讨其运作原理。

1 It’s hard to determine exactly how much medieval peasants were “taxed,” as it varied widely by province, period, and source. That said, 30% is a reasonable estimate for average taxation, including comparable obligations such as corvées and church dues.

1. 很难准确确定中世纪农民究竟缴纳了多少“税款”，因为不同省份、时期和资料来源的差异很大。不过，30% 是一个合理的平均税收估算值，其中包括徭役和教会税等类似的义务。

2 Moreover, because farming required so many workers just to feed the population, very few were left to work as tailors.

2 此外，由于农业需要大量劳动力来养活人口，因此很少有人能从事裁缝工作。

3 In the US and France, two of the major economies that are self-sufficient concerning food, 1.6% and 2.5% of the population work in agriculture, respectively. Source: "Employment in agriculture (% of total employment, modeled ILO estimate).”World Bank Open Data. Retrieved 2025-09-22.

3 在美国和法国这两个粮食自给自足的主要经济体中，分别有1.6%和2.5%的人口从事农业工作。资料来源：“农业就业（占总就业的百分比，国际劳工组织模型估算值）”。世界银行开放数据。检索日期：2025年9月22日。

2

THE ABUNDANCE EQUATION

丰度方程

T o understand how humanity escaped poverty through efficiency, let me introduce the Abundance Equation .

为了理解人类如何通过提高效率摆脱贫困，让我来介绍一下富足方程式。

We start with a simplified version that summarizes the previous chapter:

我们先来看一个简化版，概括上一章的内容：

Abundance = National Production – Basic National Needs

富足度 = 国民生产总值 – 国民基本需求

In other words, the equation shows that every population has basic needs (food, shelter, medicine, education, etc.), and that unless it produces enough to meet them, its people will remain poor, and redistribution alone cannot change that.

换句话说，这个等式表明，每个群体都有基本需求（食物、住所、医疗、教育等），除非它生产出足够的产品来满足这些需求，否则它的人民将一直贫困，而仅仅依靠再分配无法改变这一点。

In this form, the equation looks rather banal, so let’s move to a more useful version by breaking “ National Production ” into its two components: the working population and average productivity.

这种形式的等式看起来相当平淡，所以让我们通过将“国民生产总值”分解为两个组成部分——劳动人口和平均生产率——来得到一个更有用的版本。

Abundance = ( Working Pop × Avg Productivity ) – Basic National Needs

富足度 = （劳动人口 × 平均生产力） – 基本国民需求

This equation highlights the importance of average national productivity. Let’s examine why it matters so much.

这个等式凸显了国民平均生产率的重要性。让我们来探讨一下它为何如此重要。

The importance of average productivity

平均生产力的重要性

Before we continue, let me address the negative connotation of “productivity,” often linked to working harder or longer hours. In fact, it means the opposite: hard and long work is what you must do when your job is not productive.

在我们继续之前，我想先谈谈“生产力”这个词的负面含义，它通常与更努力工作或更长的工作时间联系在一起。事实上，它的意思恰恰相反：当你的工作没有成效时，你才需要付出艰苦而长时间的努力。

More importantly, your quality of life depends not only on your productivity but also on everyone else’s. Let me show you why with a simple example. A hairdresser today can serve roughly the same number of clients as hairdressers did centuries ago: their job has not become significantly more efficient.⁠ 1 Yet modern hairdressers enjoy a far better lifestyle. Why ? Because , even though their own productivity has not changed much, they benefit from everyone else’s increased productivity, from the farmers who grow their food, to the workers who sew their clothes, and the manufacturers who make their appliances.

更重要的是，你的生活质量不仅取决于你的生产力，也取决于其他人的生产力。让我用一个简单的例子来说明这一点。如今的理发师能服务的顾客数量与几个世纪前的理发师大致相同：他们的工作效率并没有显著提高。然而，现代理发师的生活质量却要好得多。为什么呢？因为，尽管他们自身的生产力并没有太大变化，但他们却受益于其他人生产力的提高，从种植粮食的农民到缝制衣服的工人，再到生产家用电器的制造商。

This interconnection affects every part of your day. Imagine a typical evening after work:

这种相互关联影响着你一天的方方面面。想象一下你下班后的典型夜晚：

  • You stayed late at the office because inefficient processes made everything take longer than it should.
    你因为效率低下的流程导致所有事情耗时过长而加班到很晚。
  • Your back hurts, but there is a three-month wait to see a specialist because hospital bureaucracy keeps each doctor tied up with paperwork, limiting the number of patients they can see.⁠ 2
    你背痛，但要等三个月才能见到专科医生，因为医院的官僚作风让每个医生都忙于文书工作，限制了他们接诊的病人数量。
  • As you get in your car, you think about buying a newer one, but you cannot afford it. Your company cannot raise wages due to low margins, which are in turn caused by low productivity.
    你坐进车里，想着要不要买辆新车，但你买不起。你的公司因为利润率低而无法提高工资，而利润率低又是生产力低下造成的。
  • Driving past the local college, you reflect on skyrocketing tuition. Inefficient administration means more staff per student and, thus, higher wages to pay.⁠ 3
    开车经过当地大学时，你不禁想到飞涨的学费。低效的管理意味着每个学生需要更多的教职工，因此也需要支付更高的工资。
  • On your way home, your car hits a hole in the road. You complain about the poor maintenance, which is due to an inefficient public sector that results in poor services despite high budgets.
    回家途中，你的车撞到路面上的一个坑里。你抱怨道路维护不善，而这源于公共部门效率低下，尽管预算充足，服务质量却很差。

Now, imagine if every service in your town became 20% more efficient. Each doctor could see more patients, reducing at least partially costs and waiting times. Each clerk could process forms faster. Each worker could produce more goods and services, which would translate into lower prices. You would benefit from all of this, even if your own productivity did not change.

现在，想象一下，如果镇上所有服务的效率都提高20%会怎样？每位医生都能接诊更多病人，至少可以部分降低成本并缩短等待时间。每位办事员都能更快地处理表格。每位工人都能生产更多商品和服务，从而降低价格。即使你自身的生产力没有改变，你也会从中受益。

We are all in this together. When national productivity drops, everything becomes more expensive and harder to access. Conversely , when it rises, life becomes easier for everyone, even those whose jobs remain unchanged. That is why maintaining adequate average national productivity is not just an economic issue but the foundation of our quality of life.

我们休戚与共。当国民生产率下降时，所有东西都会变得更贵，更难获得。反之，当国民生产率上升时，每个人的生活都会变得更轻松，即使是那些工作岗位没有改变的人也不例外。因此，维持足够的国民平均生产率不仅是一个经济问题，更是我们生活质量的基石。

Unless a nation ensures that average productivity stays above a certain threshold across the board, it will fail to produce enough to sustain its citizens, institutions, and needs, and will grow poorer over time.

除非一个国家确保平均生产力全面保持在一定水平以上，否则它将无法生产出足够的产品来维持其公民、机构和需求，并且随着时间的推移会变得越来越贫穷。

But wait, isn’t poverty the fault of inequality?

等等，贫困难道不是不平等造成的吗？

Don’t we already produce enough for everyone? Isn’t the problem that billionaires hoard wealth?

我们生产的物资难道还不够所有人用吗？问题难道不是亿万富翁囤积财富吗？

The next chapter explores this idea.

下一章将探讨这一观点。

1 Of course, hairdressers are a bit more efficient than they were, thanks to electric clippers, better scissors, etc. However, that productivity gain is not nearly enough to explain how much more their quality of life has improved across the centuries.

1 当然，由于电动理发器、更好的剪刀等的出现，理发师的效率比以前高了一些。然而，这种生产力的提高远远不足以解释几个世纪以来他们的生活质量得到了多大的改善。

2 Underfunding might have played a role, too. But that doesn’t mean smothering bureaucracy doesn’t play a significant role, too. Moreover, note that underfunding is caused by low productivity in the economy, which means less tax revenue to use to fund healthcare. So, we’re back at productivity playing a significant role.

2. 资金不足可能也是一个因素。但这并不意味着官僚主义作风就不重要。此外，值得注意的是，资金不足是由于经济生产力低下造成的，这意味着用于医疗保健的税收收入减少。因此，我们又回到了生产力发挥重要作用这一点上。

3 It’s not the full story: a phenomenon called Baumol’s cost disease also contributes to rising education costs. However, the lower average productivity of university staff is arguably a more significant and actionable factor. This topic will be discussed in Chapter 8, “What are wages, really?”

3 这并非全部原因：一种被称为鲍莫尔成本病的现象也导致了教育成本的上升。然而，大学教职工平均生产力的下降或许才是更重要、更可控的因素。我们将在第八章“工资的真正含义是什么？”中讨论这一话题。

# ↩
3

IS INEQUALITY THE CAUSE OF POVERTY?

不平等是贫困的根源吗？

I magine we collected all billionaires’ and millionaires’ wealth and redistributed it equally among everyone. Worldwide , that would be about $213 trillion, which, divided by 8.2 billion people, amounts to roughly $26,000 per person.⁠ 1

想象一下，如果我们把所有亿万富翁和百万富翁的财富集中起来，平均分配给所有人。全球财富总额约为 213 万亿美元，除以 82 亿人口，平均每人约 26,000 美元。

Hooray! Everyone is wealthier! Or are they?

太好了！大家都更富有了！真的是这样吗？

The problem is that the number of houses, roads, doctors, and so on has not changed, nor has your access to the goods and services you need to be prosperous. If your town lacked enough houses for every family or enough doctors for every patient, that problem still exists.

问题在于，房屋、道路、医生等的数量并没有改变，你获取维持生计所需商品和服务的途径也没有改变。如果你的城镇曾经缺少足够的住房供每个家庭居住，或者缺少足够的医生来照顾所有病人，那么这个问题依然存在。

For the most disadvantaged, things may improve a bit. But how much? The key is to look not at money but at goods and services. People’s situation improves only by the goods and services millionaires possess, divided by the population. For a trivial yet telling example, if the world’s 58 million millionaires owned an average of four cars each, that would make about 232 million cars to redistribute: just 0.03 cars per person. Even if each millionaire owned forty cars, it would still not be enough to give everyone a car. Redistribution cannot provide enough; only producing enough for everyone can.

对于最弱势群体而言，情况或许会有所改善。但改善幅度究竟有多大？关键在于关注的不是金钱，而是商品和服务。人们的生活水平只有在百万富翁拥有的商品和服务总量除以人口总数后才能得到改善。举个简单却又发人深省的例子：如果全球5800万百万富翁平均每人拥有四辆汽车，那么需要重新分配的汽车总数约为2.32亿辆，平均每人仅0.03辆。即使每个百万富翁拥有四十辆汽车，也无法让每个人都拥有一辆车。重新分配无法提供足够的资源；只有生产足够的商品和服务才能满足所有人的需求。

But wait! Isn’t everyone $26,000 richer thanks to redistribution? Can’t they all afford a car now? Again , no, because there are not enough cars. The only way for everyone to have a car is to produce enough cars.

等等！难道通过财富再分配，每个人都多了26000美元吗？他们现在不都能买得起车了吗？答案仍然是否定的，因为汽车数量不足。让每个人都拥有汽车的唯一办法就是生产足够的汽车。

The path to prosperity must run through producing enough goods and services for everyone.

通往繁荣的道路必须建立在生产足够的商品和服务以满足所有人需求的基础之上。

Then, on top of that, redistribution can play a role, but only on top of that. Redistribution won’t help much unless our nation produces enough for everyone in the first place.

此外，财富再分配也能发挥作用，但仅仅是锦上添花。如果我们的国家首先无法生产出足够的财富来养活所有人，那么财富再分配就无济于事。

The Scrooge McDuck’s fallacy

史高治·麦克老鸭的谬误

But wouldn’t everyone having $26,000 more stimulate the production of more cars? On one hand, yes. On the other hand, those $213 trillion we redistributed were not hoarded by billionaires in giant vaults à la Scrooge McDuck . They were invested in companies, machinery, and other productive assets. That capital must stay invested to maintain production capacity. If people spent their $26,000 on consumption instead of reinvestment, production capacity would shrink. In fact, the disruption caused by the redistribution would likely reduce future production capacity even further, meaning fewer cars for everyone.

但如果每个人都多拿2.6万美元，难道不会刺激汽车产量增加吗？一方面，的确如此。另一方面，我们重新分配的这213万亿美元并没有像史高治·麦克老鸭那样被亿万富翁们藏在巨大的金库里。它们被投资于公司、机器和其他生产性资产。这些资本必须继续投资才能维持生产能力。如果人们把这2.6万美元用于消费而不是再投资，生产能力就会下降。事实上，重新分配带来的冲击很可能会进一步降低未来的生产能力，这意味着每个人能买到的车都会减少。

The prosperity bottleneck

繁荣瓶颈

The point is,

关键是，

Consumption is subordinate to production.

消费服从于生产。

Adding money without adding goods and services merely makes them more expensive; it does not make them more accessible.

增加资金而不增加商品和服务，只会让它们更贵，并不会使它们更容易获得。

Hence the need for a paradigm shift: from dollars to goods and services, and from inequality to needs met.

因此，我们需要进行范式转变：从关注美元转向关注商品和服务，从关注不平等转向关注需求满足。

To truly fight poverty, we must first produce enough to meet everyone’s needs. Unless we do that, nothing else will matter much.

要真正消除贫困，我们首先必须生产足够的粮食来满足所有人的需求。如果我们做不到这一点，其他一切都无济于事。

1 Source: The 2024 UBS Global Wealth Report .

1 资料来源：《2024 年瑞银全球财富报告》。

# ↩
4

MONEY PRINTERS AND VALUE PRINTERS

印钞机和价值创造机

I magine a fictional world where nothing ever changes, no new technology is ever invented, and companies are always exactly as productive as they were yesterday. In that world, $5 bought you a burger yesterday, buys you a burger today, and will buy you a burger tomorrow.

想象一个虚构的世界，那里的一切都一成不变，没有新技术被发明出来，公司的生产力永远和昨天一样。在这个世界里，5美元昨天能买到一个汉堡，今天能买到一个汉堡，明天也能买到一个汉堡。

But one day, something does change. The government prints a lot of money to distribute as a gift to the population (elections are coming). What happens to the prices of burgers? In our fictional world where productivity never changes, if they do not hire more staff and purchase more machines, there will be more dollars chasing the same number of burgers, and burger prices will rise. Only if they do hire enough workers and buy enough machines to produce enough burgers will prices remain constant.

但有一天，情况发生了变化。政府印了很多钱，准备作为礼物分发给民众（选举即将到来）。汉堡的价格会如何变化呢？在我们这个生产力永不改变的虚构世界里，如果政府不增加员工、不购买更多机器，就会有更多的钱去追逐同样数量的汉堡，汉堡的价格自然会上涨。只有当政府雇佣足够的工人、购买足够的机器来生产足够的汉堡时，价格才能保持不变。

Now consider a different scenario. McDonald’s invents a revolutionary “burger printer” that dramatically increases burger production. People still have the same amount of dollars, but there are more burgers, so prices fall. Each dollar now buys more burgers.

现在设想另一种情况。麦当劳发明了一种革命性的“汉堡打印机”，大幅提高了汉堡的产量。人们的钱还是那么多，但汉堡的数量增加了，所以价格下降了。现在每一美元都能买到更多的汉堡。

Did you notice the pattern? When we create more money than goods, the value of our dollars decreases, and when we create more goods than money, the value of our dollars increases. ⁠ 1

你注意到其中的规律了吗？当我们创造的货币多于商品时，美元的价值就会下降；当我们创造的商品多于货币时，美元的价值就会上升。

The importance of spending efficiency

支出效率的重要性

Let’s examine a third possible scenario. What if the government printed money and used it to buy these revolutionary “burger printers” and create “national burger chains”?

让我们来探讨第三种可能的情况。如果政府印钞，用这些钱购买这些革命性的“汉堡打印机”，并建立“全国连锁汉堡店”，会怎么样呢？

The results depend on how wisely that money is spent. If the government overpays for inefficient machines or expensive shop locations, inflation rises without enough new production to offset it, and everyone loses. But if it buys efficient machines at reasonable prices, the resulting increase in burger production absorbs the new money in circulation.⁠ 2

结果取决于这笔钱的使用是否明智。如果政府为低效的机器或昂贵的店铺位置支付过高的价格，通货膨胀就会上升，而新增产量却不足以抵消，最终所有人都会受损。但如果政府以合理的价格购买高效的机器，由此带来的汉堡产量增加就能吸收流通中的新增货币。

This reveals a fundamental principle: money printing is only as good as the productivity of what it buys. It is beneficial when it increases production efficiently and generally harmful when it does not.

这揭示了一个基本原则：印钞的效用取决于其购买力。当印钞能有效提高生产力时，它就是有益的；反之，如果不能，则通常是有害的。

To be clear, not all public spending must go to productive endeavors; some aspirational or recreational projects are perfectly fine. However , these should be financed only from an existing surplus, not from deficits (which means using money printing, which fuels inflation and raises prices, or debt, which burdens future generations when used unproductively). Likewise , printing money or taking on debt to support the poorest citizens during a crisis can be effective, especially when production is depressed and the increased money supply can stimulate its recovery, thus preventing inflation.

需要明确的是，并非所有公共支出都必须用于生产性活动；一些旨在提升生活品质或娱乐休闲的项目也完全可以。然而，这些项目的资金来源应仅限于现有盈余，而非赤字（赤字意味着通过印钞来推高物价，而印钞会加剧通货膨胀，导致物价上涨；也意味着举债，而举债若被滥用，则会给子孙后代带来沉重负担）。同样，在危机时期，印钞或举债来帮助最贫困的公民也可能是有效的，尤其是在生产低迷、货币供应量增加能够刺激经济复苏，从而抑制通货膨胀的情况下。

That said, the point is: money printing and government spending are not inherently good or bad; they are only as good as the efficiency with which they use the resources they muster. ⁠ 3 ⁠ , 4

也就是说，关键在于：印钞和政府支出本身并无好坏之分；它们的好坏取决于它们利用现有资源的效率。

Do they finance productive assets (technology, skills, infrastructure, etc.) or merely fund consumption? And do they make the most of every dollar or squander it? These are all important questions that we should ask whenever we mention increasing public spending. When used well (and the bar is high), printing money and increasing debt can be a powerful governance tool. But when used poorly, they can leave a country fragile and even lead to poverty. The following chapter examines precisely how countries can slip from prosperity to poverty, and how this transition is often swifter than most realize.

这些资金是用于生产性资产（技术、技能、基础设施等）还是仅仅用于消费？每一分钱都物尽其用，还是被挥霍一空？每当我们谈到增加公共支出时，这些都是我们应该提出的重要问题。如果运用得当（而运用得当的标准很高），印钞和增加债务可以成为强有力的治理工具。但如果运用不当，它们会使一个国家变得脆弱，甚至导致贫困。下一章将详细探讨国家如何从繁荣滑向贫困，以及这种转变往往比大多数人意识到的要迅速得多。

1 Devon Eriksen’s quote, “Private companies print value, so your money is worth more. Governments print money, so your money is worth less,” inspired this sentence.

1 德文·埃里克森的名言“私营公司创造价值，让你的钱更有价值；政府印钞，让你的钱更不值钱”启发了这句话的创作。

2 Astute readers may notice a fourth, better solution: improve the overall economy so goods become cheaper and people, after covering other necessities, have more money left to buy burgers or burger printers. Later chapters discuss this.

2 敏锐的读者或许会注意到第四个更好的解决方案：改善整体经济状况，降低商品价格，让人们在满足其他必需品需求后，有更多钱去买汉堡或汉堡打印机。后续章节将对此进行探讨。

3 We often treat money printing and public spending as the same. This is incorrect. When a government uses tax revenue to hand out subsidies to the poor, it does not increase the number of dollars in circulation and, therefore, does not cause much inflation (unless it raises total demand beyond what the economy can supply). Conversely, if the government prints money to fund the subsidies, prices rise substantially, which hurts everyone who did not receive them (and even those who did, once the subsidies stop).

3. 我们常常把印钞和公共支出混为一谈，这是不正确的。当政府利用税收收入向穷人发放补贴时，并不会增加货币流通量，因此不会造成严重的通货膨胀（除非总需求超过经济供给能力）。相反，如果政府印钞来支付补贴，物价就会大幅上涨，这将损害所有未获得补贴的人（甚至包括那些曾经获得补贴的人，一旦补贴停止，他们也会受到影响）。

More importantly, money printing is both a symptom of a structural problem (the government does not produce enough to fund its spending) and a disincentive to solving it (why fix what is broken when you can just print more cash?). This, of course, doesn’t mean money printing should be fully avoided; it has legitimate uses. However, it’s not a free lunch and can easily cause more harm than it prevents.

更重要的是，印钞既是结构性问题的征兆（政府收入不足以支付支出），也是解决问题的阻碍（既然可以印更多钞票，何必去修补破损之处呢？）。当然，这并不意味着应该完全避免印钞；它也有其合理用途。然而，印钞并非万能，而且很容易造成弊大于利的后果。

4 Increasing public debt has effects similar to money printing: it can cause inflation (when investors are foreign, and thus their investments increase the money supply, if that increase is superior to the increase in goods to which it leads), is beneficial when used to acquire productive assets and harmful otherwise, and fosters complacency.

4 增加公共债务会产生类似于印钞的效果：它会导致通货膨胀（当投资者是外国人时，他们的投资会增加货币供应量，如果这种增加超过了由此带来的商品增加），当用于获取生产性资产时是有益的，否则是有害的，并且会助长自满情绪。

Excessive debt carries an additional risk. Once lenders begin to doubt a government’s ability to repay, they demand higher interest rates or impose strict conditions in exchange for funding. Several Latin American economies in the 1980s and 1990s learned this the hard way. Debt can therefore shift power from elected governments to creditors, forcing policies that would never be chosen voluntarily.

过度负债会带来额外的风险。一旦债权人开始怀疑政府的偿还能力，他们就会要求更高的利率或附加苛刻的条件来换取资金。上世纪八九十年代，一些拉丁美洲经济体就为此付出了惨痛的代价。因此，债务可能会将权力从民选政府转移到债权人手中，迫使政府推行一些原本不会自愿选择的政策。

We often forget that taking on a little debt is very different from taking on a lot: the latter leaves us fragile. This is why governments should always reduce debt to reasonable levels during good times; otherwise, they cannot borrow without consequences when the tide turns. (A principle I learned from Alessandro Riolo.)

我们常常忘记，承担少量债务与承担大量债务截然不同：后者会让我们变得脆弱不堪。因此，政府在经济繁荣时期应始终将债务控制在合理水平；否则，一旦经济形势逆转，它们将无法在不承担后果的情况下继续借贷。（这是我从亚历山德罗·里奥洛那里学到的一个原则。）

# ↩
5

THE FRAGILITY OF PROSPERITY

繁荣的脆弱性

I magine the following thought experiment. Tomorrow , you wake up and discover that overnight, every job’s efficiency dropped by a third. Each factory worker makes fewer products, each doctor sees fewer patients, and each farmer produces less food. What would happen?

想象一下以下这个思想实验。明天你醒来发现，一夜之间，所有工作的效率都下降了三分之一。每个工厂工人生产的产品更少了，每个医生接诊的病人更少了，每个农民生产的粮食也更少了。会发生什么？

With workers producing less, goods become scarcer and more expensive. With public servants being less productive, services degrade, meaning people receive worse education, healthcare, and other public services.

由于工人生产力下降，商品变得更加稀缺和昂贵。由于公务员效率降低，服务质量下降，这意味着人们获得的教育、医疗保健和其他公共服务质量降低。

If the productivity problem is not solved, the country can either accept lower consumption and worse public services, thus becoming poorer, or bridge the gap through various forms of debt:

如果生产力问题得不到解决，这个国家要么只能接受消费下降和公共服务恶化，从而变得更加贫穷，要么就只能通过各种形式的债务来弥补缺口：

  • Financial Debt : Citizens and countries spend savings or borrow to cover the gap between what the nation produces and consumes. This works temporarily, but interest payments snowball quickly. ( The US currently pays $658 billion yearly in interest, enough to give every American $164 per month if there were no debt.⁠ 1 )
    金融债务：公民和国家动用储蓄或借贷来弥补国家生产与消费之间的缺口。这在短期内有效，但利息支出会迅速累积。（美国目前每年支付6580亿美元的利息，如果没有债务，这笔钱足以让每个美国人每月获得164美元。）
  • Infrastructure Debt : Maintenance of roads, bridges, railways, and other critical infrastructure is delayed.
    基础设施债务：道路、桥梁、铁路和其他关键基础设施的维护工作被延误。
  • Trust Debt : Spending on police, judges, courts, and other institutions that maintain social order is reduced. As a result, disputes take longer to resolve and law enforcement weakens, making life and business gradually harder and more expensive for everyone.
    信任债务：用于维护社会秩序的警察、法官、法院和其他机构的支出减少。结果，纠纷解决时间延长，执法力度减弱，使每个人的生活和经商难度逐渐增加，成本也随之上升。
  • Cultural Debt : In a rush to maintain productivity, countries may bring in more immigrants than they can properly integrate, or may cut corners on education and training, creating long-term social challenges that are costly to fix.
    文化债务：为了维持生产力，各国可能会引进比自身能够妥善融合的更多的移民，或者在教育和培训方面偷工减料，从而造成长期的社会挑战，而这些挑战的解决成本很高。

Slow, then fast

先慢后快

The tricky part is that these debts seem harmless at first: a little financial debt feels like a free lunch, skipping infrastructure maintenance doesn’t seem to matter (after all, bridges take decades to fall apart), and small compromises in law enforcement or education appear manageable. By the way, this is the stage where much of Western Europe currently finds itself: using ballooning public debt to mask structural decline.

棘手之处在于，这些债务乍看之下似乎无害：少量的财务债务就像是白捡的午餐，忽略基础设施维护似乎无关紧要（毕竟，桥梁需要几十年才会损坏），执法或教育方面的小幅妥协似乎也还能应付。顺便一提，西欧大部分地区目前就处于这种阶段：利用不断膨胀的公共债务来掩盖结构性衰退。

In the short term, this strategy works well. In the long term, however, the story is different. Financial debt snowballs as interest compounds and lenders demand higher rates. Decades of neglected maintenance have left infrastructure in decay. When trust and cultural problems reach a tipping point, everyday life and business become increasingly difficult and expensive.

短期来看，这种策略行之有效。但从长远来看，情况则截然不同。随着利息的累积和贷款机构要求更高利率，债务会像滚雪球一样越滚越大。数十年的疏于维护导致基础设施日渐衰败。当信任和文化问题达到临界点时，日常生活和商业活动都会变得越来越困难和昂贵。

The second-order effects are even worse: citizens, businesses, and investors begin leaving for other countries. At first, only a few depart, but they are often the most productive. Their exit further reduces the nation’s productivity, worsening the problems above and tipping the scales for more to follow. Each new departure makes it even less attractive for others to stay (or for investors to invest), creating a downward spiral that can bring even a wealthy country to its knees.

二次效应更加严重：公民、企业和投资者开始迁往其他国家。起初，只有少数人离开，但他们往往是生产力最高的人。他们的离开进一步降低了国家的生产力，加剧了上述问题，并导致更多人效仿。每一次新的离开都会降低其他人留下的意愿（或投资者的投资意愿），从而形成恶性循环，甚至可能使一个富裕国家陷入困境。

# ↩

Why We Don't See It Coming

为什么我们预见不到它的到来

If declining productivity is so dangerous, why do prosperous nations often ignore the warning signs?

如果生产力下降如此危险，为什么富裕国家常常忽视这些警告信号？

There are several reasons. First , the consequences take years or even decades to appear. Just as a person can live on credit cards for years before bankruptcy hits, a nation can mask declining productivity for a long time through various forms of debt.

原因有很多。首先，后果往往需要数年甚至数十年才会显现。正如一个人可以靠信用卡生活多年直到破产一样，一个国家也可以通过各种形式的债务长期掩盖生产力下降的问题。

Second, we tend to underestimate how much our quality of life depends on national productivity. Yes , there is more to life than work: family, friends, culture, leisure, and so on. But even these non-work activities rely on the productive work of others. That dinner with friends requires farmers and restaurant workers, which in turn requires housing, food, and other goods and services. Your child's birth requires hospitals, medicines, and medical staff, who also require housing, food, infrastructure, and other goods and services. Similarly , environmental protection requires efficient green technology and a capable construction sector. When productivity declines, life becomes harder and duller.

其次，我们往往低估了生活质量对国家生产力的依赖程度。诚然，生活远不止工作：家庭、朋友、文化、休闲等等。但即使是这些非工作活动也依赖于他人的生产性劳动。与朋友共进晚餐需要农民和餐厅员工，而他们又需要住房、食物和其他商品及服务。孩子的出生需要医院、药品和医务人员，而他们也需要住房、食物、基础设施和其他商品及服务。同样，环境保护需要高效的绿色技术和强大的建筑业。当生产力下降时，生活就会变得更加艰难乏味。

Protecting Prosperity

保护繁荣

This picture may seem bleak, but the situation is far from hopeless. If we understand the fragility of prosperity, we can protect it appropriately.

眼前的景象或许令人沮丧，但情况远非绝望。如果我们认识到繁荣的脆弱性，就能采取适当的措施来保护它。

We must remember that prosperity is not our natural state; poverty is.⁠ 2 Like a garden, prosperity requires consistent maintenance. Brief periods of neglect are survivable, but prolonged inattention leads to problems that become increasingly difficult to reverse.⁠ 3 Hence , the importance of repairing the foundations while they still hold, not after they begin to crumble.

我们必须记住，繁荣并非我们的自然状态；贫穷才是。繁荣如同花园，需要持续的维护。短暂的疏忽尚可忍受，但长期的忽视会导致问题，而且这些问题会变得越来越难以挽回。因此，重要的是在根基稳固之时就进行修缮，而不是等到根基开始崩塌之后才去补救。

In the next chapters, we will explore specific strategies for maintaining and improving productivity without sacrificing our values or quality of life. Then , the second and third parts of the book describe how, with a solid foundation of productivity, we can build strong institutions and freedoms.

在接下来的章节中，我们将探讨如何在不牺牲价值观或生活质量的前提下，维持并提高生产力的具体策略。本书的第二部分和第三部分将阐述如何在稳固的生产力基础上，构建强大的制度和自由。

1 Source: the US government. By the way, a Senate press release dated 2024-06-18 estimates that “net interest costs are expected to grow from $658 billion in 2023, to $892 billion this year, to more than $1 trillion in 2025.”

1 资料来源：美国政府。顺便一提，参议院2024年6月18日发布的新闻稿估计，“净利息成本预计将从2023年的6580亿美元增长到今年的8920亿美元，到2025年将超过1万亿美元。”

2 For example, I recently learned that in the Dark Ages, people forgot how to treat fractured bones, resulting in more poorly healed skeletons. This illustrates that we should not underestimate the possibility of regression to worse times.

2 例如，我最近了解到，在中世纪早期，人们忘记了如何处理骨折，导致骨骼愈合不良的情况增多。这说明我们不应低估历史倒退到更糟糕时代的可能性。

Source: Roberts, 1988.

资料来源：Roberts，1988 年。

3 A reminder that we do not need to maximize productivity at all costs, which would be counterproductive, but we do need to maintain it above the threshold required for long-term prosperity.

3 提醒大家，我们不需要不惜一切代价追求生产力最大化，那样反而会适得其反，但我们确实需要将其保持在长期繁荣所需的阈值之上。

# ↩
6

YOU ARE NOT UNPRODUCTIVE; YOUR JOB IS

你并非效率低下；你的工作效率低下。

T his chapter’s title is a bit provocative. Of course, many people are unproductive because they lack skills or motivation. But probably just as many are unproductive because their jobs are unproductive. For example, imagine two equally talented door-to-door salespeople, both working their hardest. One sells printers, the other sells fax machines. We can expect the printer salesperson to make more sales: after all, who needs a fax machine nowadays? Same talent, same effort, different results.

本章标题颇具挑衅性。当然，许多人效率低下是因为缺乏技能或动力。但可能同样多的人效率低下是因为他们的工作本身效率低下。例如，想象一下两位同样才华横溢的上门推销员，他们都竭尽全力。一位推销打印机，另一位推销传真机。我们可以预期推销打印机的推销员会取得更多业绩：毕竟，现在谁还需要传真机呢？同样的才华，同样的努力，结果却截然不同。

Or picture two equally skilled doctors working the same hours. One works in a well-run hospital where staff handle all the paperwork. The other is buried in administrative tasks. Naturally , the first doctor can treat more patients, everything else being equal. Again , same talent, same effort, different results.

或者想象一下两位医术精湛的医生，工作时间相同。一位在管理完善的医院工作，所有文书工作都由专人负责；另一位则被繁杂的行政事务压得喘不过气来。显然，在其他条件相同的情况下，第一位医生可以接诊更多病人。同样是天赋相同，付出相同努力，结果却截然不同。

This pattern recurs in many contexts. Factory workers produce more in plants with modern equipment. Fashion photographers thrive in bustling cities full of opportunities. Your productivity often depends not just on your skills and work ethic but also on your job: what you do, where you do it, and how you are set up to do it.

这种模式在很多方面都反复出现。工厂工人在配备现代化设备的工厂里生产效率更高。时尚摄影师在充满机遇的繁华都市里如鱼得水。你的工作效率往往不仅取决于你的技能和职业道德，还取决于你的工作内容：你做什么，在哪里做，以及你的工作环境如何。

Prosperous societies help their citizens find productive jobs.

繁荣的社会会帮助公民找到有生产力的工作。

Before continuing, let me clarify that the term “productive” refers to both producing a large quantity of goods and services and producing what is in high demand. Work is unproductive either when it yields little or when it yields a lot of what people do not care much about.

在继续之前，我想先澄清一下，“生产性”一词既指生产大量商品和服务，也指生产市场需求量大的产品。如果工作产出甚少，或者产出大量人们并不在意的东西，那么这项工作就是低效的。

Unproductive work holds back people and nations

低效的工作阻碍了人民和国家的发展。

When choosing a job, most people focus on salary, work-life balance, or personal interest, but often overlook how productive they can be in that role. Working in an unproductive job (one with low demand, outdated tools, or inefficient processes) is like racing uphill: you can work extremely hard yet make little progress. Over time, this leads to lower wages, fewer opportunities, and even frustration or burnout.

在选择工作时，大多数人关注的是薪资、工作与生活平衡或个人兴趣，却往往忽略了自己在工作中的效率。从事一份低效的工作（例如需求低、工具陈旧或流程低效）就像是逆水行舟：即使你非常努力，也难以取得显著进展。长此以往，这会导致收入减少、机会减少，甚至最终导致沮丧或职业倦怠。

The alternative is to seek out productive environments: companies that invest in good tools and efficient processes, industries where your work meets real demand, and locations where your skills are needed.

另一种选择是寻找高效的工作环境：投资于良好工具和高效流程的公司，你的工作能够满足实际需求的行业，以及需要你技能的地方。

This does not mean we should maximize productivity; it simply means we should not entirely neglect it when making career choices. ( As a side note, it’s striking how most people spend years in school yet devote little time to ensuring they end up working for a company and boss productive enough to allow them to live the life they desire.)

这并不意味着我们应该追求效率最大化；这仅仅意味着我们在做职业选择时不应该完全忽视效率。（顺便一提，令人惊讶的是，大多数人花了数年时间上学，却很少花时间确保自己最终能为一家足够高效的公司和一位足够优秀的上司工作，从而过上自己想要的生活。）

What holds for individuals also holds for nations. When people move from less to more productive work, countries grow prosperous, and when too many remain in unproductive jobs, nations suffer.

适用于个人的道理同样适用于国家。当人们从低效工作转向高效工作时，国家就会繁荣昌盛；而当太多人从事低效工作时，国家就会遭受损失。

Countries should therefore go to great lengths to give citizens not just jobs but productive ones.

因此，各国应该竭尽全力为公民提供工作，而且是生产性工作。

This does not mean coercing anyone into a specific career. Instead , they should take a two-pronged approach. First , they should make jobs more productive by removing obstacles such as excessive bureaucracy and by improving infrastructure and job-relevant education. Second , they should provide the information needed to make informed career choices, so that those who want a productive job know where to find one.

这并不意味着强迫任何人从事特定职业。相反，他们应该采取双管齐下的策略。首先，他们应该通过消除繁文缛节等障碍、改善基础设施和提升与工作相关的教育水平，来提高工作效率。其次，他们应该提供必要的信息，帮助人们做出明智的职业选择，让那些渴望从事高效率工作的人知道去哪里寻找机会。

The next chapter discusses this last point.

下一章将讨论最后一点。

# ↩
7

HOW JOB MARKETS SHAPE PROSPERITY

就业市场如何影响繁荣

T o understand the importance of well-functioning job markets, let’s return to our two fictional countries, Moralia and Pragmatia . As a reminder, these nations are equal in all respects except for one key difference: Moralia's government prides itself on making the most ethical choices, while Pragmatia focuses on improving efficiency.

为了理解运转良好的就业市场的重要性，让我们回到虚构的两个国家——莫拉利亚和普拉格玛提亚。需要说明的是，这两个国家在所有方面都完全相同，只有一个关键区别：莫拉利亚政府以做出最符合道德的选择而自豪，而普拉格玛提亚则专注于提高效率。

Both countries have large manufacturing sectors, and as new technology emerges, some factories become outdated. However , they respond differently: Moralia tries to save every job by propping up struggling companies, while Pragmatia lets these companies fail.

两国都拥有庞大的制造业，随着新技术的出现，一些工厂逐渐被淘汰。然而，两国的应对方式截然不同：莫拉利亚试图通过扶持陷入困境的公司来保住每一个工作岗位，而普拉格马蒂亚则任由这些公司倒闭。

On the next page, let’s see how these approaches play out.

下一页，让我们看看这些方法的效果如何。

# ↩

A Tale of Two Countries

两个国家的故事

In Pragmatia , workers at struggling companies lose their jobs, but not for long: the more efficient companies, now producing cheaper goods with better technology, grow quickly and hire most of the laid-off workers. As workers move from less productive to more productive companies, national productivity rises. Goods and services become more abundant and cheaper, and everyone can buy more with their money. Even better, companies using these cheaper materials become more competitive globally, creating new jobs.

在普拉格玛提亚，那些苦苦挣扎的公司里的工人会失业，但这种情况不会持续太久：效率更高的公司凭借更先进的技术生产出更便宜的商品，迅速发展壮大，并雇佣了大部分下岗工人。随着工人从生产力较低的公司流向生产力较高的公司，国家生产力也随之提高。商品和服务变得更加丰富、价格更低，每个人都能用同样的钱买到更多东西。更重要的是，使用这些更便宜原材料的公司在全球范围内更具竞争力，从而创造了新的就业机会。

Conversely, Moralia’s kind and compassionate approach backfires. Their factories remain inefficient, goods become more expensive, and citizens can afford fewer of them. They end up importing cheaper goods from places like Pragmatia , sending Moralia’s money abroad. To keep failing companies alive, the government hands out subsidies, but to pay for them, it must raise taxes, leaving citizens with even less to spend. It becomes a downward spiral.

相反，莫拉利亚的仁慈和同情之举却适得其反。他们的工厂效率低下，商品价格上涨，民众的购买力下降。最终，他们不得不从普拉格玛提亚等地进口更便宜的商品，将莫拉利亚的资金转移到国外。为了维持濒临倒闭的企业，政府发放补贴，但为了支付这些补贴，政府不得不提高税收，导致民众的可支配收入进一步减少。这形成了一个恶性循环。

Of course, this is a simplistic example, but it nevertheless teaches two useful lessons. First , a compassionate approach works only to the extent it also addresses structural problems, and otherwise it worsens them. As I often say, problems grow to the size needed for us to acknowledge them. This does not mean we should be heartless: workers who lose their jobs deserve support in the form of temporary unemployment benefits and help finding new positions. The critical point is that this support should fix structural problems rather than deepen them.

当然，这只是一个简单的例子，但它仍然能给我们带来两个有益的教训。首先，富有同情心的做法只有在同时解决结构性问题时才有效，否则只会加剧问题。正如我常说的，问题会发展到我们不得不正视的地步。但这并不意味着我们应该冷酷无情：失业的工人理应获得临时失业救济金和就业援助。关键在于，这种援助应该着眼于解决结构性问题，而不是加剧问题。

Second, countries grow poorer when they keep workers in unproductive jobs, and grow more prosperous when they help them transition to productive ones. For example, I believe that capitalist countries have historically fared better than communist ones, not because they better incentivize workers to work hard (communist workers worked hard, too), but because they allocate people to productive jobs more effectively.

其次，如果一个国家让工人从事低效的工作，国家就会变得更加贫穷；如果帮助工人转型到高效的工作，国家就会变得更加繁荣。例如，我认为资本主义国家在历史上比共产主义国家发展得更好，并非因为它们更能激励工人努力工作（共产主义国家的工人也很努力工作），而是因为它们更有效地将劳动力分配到高效的工作岗位上。

Now that we learned the importance of helping people transition to productive jobs, let’s explore how to do it without coercion or central planning, which has a poor track record.

既然我们已经了解了帮助人们过渡到生产性工作的重要性，那么让我们来探讨如何在不采取强制或中央计划的情况下做到这一点，因为强制或中央计划的成效不佳。

Job Markets for Prosperity

促进繁荣的就业市场

A healthy job market needs two things:

健康的就业市场需要两样东西：

  1. Clear signals about which jobs are in demand. People need to know where their work is most needed and can create the most value. When this happens, everyone wins: workers find roles that better reward their efforts, and society gets more of the work it needs most.
    明确哪些工作岗位需求旺盛，需要明确的信号。人们需要知道自己的工作在哪里最受需要，能够创造最大的价值。这样一来，人人受益：劳动者能找到更能体现自身价值的工作，社会也能获得更多最需要的工作机会。
  2. The ability to let unproductive jobs fade away (letting the market decide which jobs are unproductive). This may sound harsh, but it’s not as harsh as the alternative: keeping people trapped in dying industries. This harms the very people we aim to protect, both directly (keeping them in low-wage, stagnant roles) and indirectly (if too many people remain in unproductive jobs, average national productivity lowers, prices rise, and everyone becomes effectively poorer). Also , remember that letting jobs fade does not imply abandoning workers: governments still can and should provide unemployment benefits and career transition support.
    允许低效工作岗位逐渐消失（让市场决定哪些工作岗位属于低效工作）。这听起来或许有些苛刻，但远不及另一种选择那么残酷：让人们困在日渐衰落的行业中。后者会直接（让他们从事低薪、停滞不前的工作）和间接（如果太多人继续从事低效工作，国家平均生产率就会下降，物价上涨，最终导致所有人的生活水平下降）损害我们想要保护的人群。此外，请记住，允许低效工作岗位逐渐消失并不意味着放弃劳动者：政府仍然可以而且应该提供失业救济金和职业转型支持。

If the above seems unnecessary, it is probably because we have not accepted that while subsidizing unproductive jobs may be feasible for a tiny percentage of jobs, so that its impact on average national productivity is negligible, it cannot be sustained at scale or over long periods. In that case, national productivity declines too far, and both state capacity and everyone’s purchasing power fall sharply, ultimately hurting the very workers we wanted to protect.

如果上述内容看似多余，那很可能是因为我们尚未认识到，虽然补贴低效工作岗位对极少数岗位来说或许可行，对全国平均生产率的影响也微乎其微，但这种做法无法大规模或长期持续。一旦出现这种情况，全国生产率就会大幅下降，国家产能和民众购买力都会急剧下降，最终损害的恰恰是我们想要保护的劳动者。

The solution is simple but requires a bit of courage: stop subsidizing failing companies and let wages and opportunities guide people to where their work creates the most value.

解决办法很简单，但需要一点勇气：停止补贴失败的公司，让工资和机会引导人们去到他们的工作能创造最大价值的地方。

The next chapter explores exactly how to do that.

下一章将探讨如何做到这一点。

8

WHAT ARE WAGES, REALLY?

工资究竟是什么？

W e saw the importance of job markets providing clear signals that guide workers toward more productive jobs. One of the most important such signals is wages.

我们看到，就业市场必须发出清晰的信号，引导劳动者找到生产效率更高的工作。其中最重要的信号之一就是工资。

To understand why, let’s return to our two fictional countries. Moralia believes each job is equally worthy and, therefore, mandates that everyone earn the same wage. Pragmatia , by contrast, lets the market determine salaries. Let’s see how their approaches play out in the healthcare sector.

为了理解个中缘由，让我们回到这两个虚构的国家。莫拉利亚认为每份工作都同等重要，因此规定所有人必须获得相同的工资。相比之下，普拉格玛提亚则让市场决定薪酬。让我们看看它们的做法在医疗保健领域是如何体现的。

Becoming a doctor takes years of intense study and exhausting work. In Moralia , where doctors earn no more than workers in other fields, few people choose this path. Some still do so out of passion or duty, but their numbers fall short of the country’s needs. The result is a doctor shortage, with longer waitlists and rising healthcare costs.

成为一名医生需要多年的刻苦学习和艰苦工作。在莫拉利亚，医生的收入与其他行业的从业者相差无几，因此很少有人选择这条道路。尽管有些人出于热爱或责任感仍然选择这条路，但他们的数量远远无法满足国家的需求。这导致医生短缺，候诊名单越来越长，医疗成本也不断上涨。

Moralia reacts by capping prices. In theory, this ensures everyone can afford care. In practice, it creates new problems. With too few doctors and artificially low prices, waiting lists grow even longer. People find backdoor solutions through personal connections or bribes. Despite Moralia’s attempts to make everyone feel worthy, or precisely because of them, most citizens lack proper healthcare.

莫拉利亚采取的应对措施是限制医疗价格。理论上，这能确保人人都能负担得起医疗服务。但实际上，这却引发了新的问题。由于医生数量不足，加上人为压低的价格，候诊名单越来越长。人们不得不通过人脉关系或行贿等手段寻求捷径。尽管莫拉利亚试图让每个人都觉得自己值得被尊重，或者正因为如此，大多数公民反而缺乏适当的医疗保健。

The ripple effects go further. Bright , ambitious people who might have become doctors choose other careers instead. Many become teachers, another meaningful profession, but this creates its own imbalance: more teachers than schools actually need. In a normal market, oversupply would lower wages and make services more affordable. In Moralia’s fixed-wage system, it simply produces more teachers per classroom, with only modest gains in education quality.

连锁反应远不止于此。许多才华横溢、雄心勃勃的人原本可能成为医生，却选择了其他职业。许多人成为教师，这同样是一项有意义的职业，但这也造成了新的失衡：教师数量超过了学校的实际需求。在正常的市场环境下，供过于求会降低工资，使服务更加经济实惠。但在莫拉利亚的固定工资制度下，供过于求只会增加每个教室的教师数量，而教育质量的提升却微乎其微。

So, Moralia’s well-intentioned policies produce significantly worse healthcare in exchange for marginally better schools. This is not just about numbers on a spreadsheet: it is about real people’s lives and their access to essential services. Ignoring the natural balance between supply and demand creates not only economic inefficiencies but also very real hardship.

因此，莫拉利亚出于好意的政策，换来的是医疗保健水平的显著下降，而学校教育的改善却微乎其微。这不仅仅是电子表格上的数字问题，而是关乎人们的真实生活以及他们获得基本服务的机会。忽视供需之间的自然平衡，不仅会造成经济效率低下，还会带来切实的困难。

Pragmatia, by contrast, treats wages not as measures of intrinsic worth but as signals of where workers are most needed. It understands that doctors earn more than teachers because the country needs another doctor more than it needs another teacher. If the number of doctors doubled overnight and that of teachers halved, teacher salaries would rise and doctor salaries would fall, even though the intrinsic value of the people in these jobs had not changed.

与此相反，实用主义并不将工资视为衡量内在价值的标准，而是将其视为衡量劳动力最紧缺领域的信号。它认为，医生比教师收入高，是因为国家更需要医生而不是教师。如果一夜之间医生数量翻了一番，教师数量减半，那么教师的工资就会上涨，而医生的工资就会下降，即便从事这些职业的人的内在价值并没有改变。

Therefore, Pragmatia allows wages to rise and fall with supply and demand. It understands that matching the jobs people take with the jobs society needs benefits everyone, both as workers, through higher wages, and as consumers, through more goods and services at lower prices.

因此，实用主义允许工资随供求关系波动。它认为，将人们从事的工作与社会所需的工作相匹配，对每个人都有好处：对劳动者而言，工资会更高；对消费者而言，商品和服务的价格会更低，因此都能从中受益。

The bottom line is that wages are not a measure of someone’s intrinsic worth. They are signals of a mismatch between demand and supply. ⁠ 1 ⁠ , 2 ⁠ , 3

归根结底，工资并不能衡量一个人的内在价值。它反映的是供需不匹配的情况。

Because low wages are a symptom rather than a root cause, trying to control wages superficially instead of addressing the underlying structural mismatch is often ineffective and frequently counterproductive, too.

因为低工资是一种症状而不是根本原因，所以试图从表面上控制工资而不是解决潜在的结构性不匹配问题往往是无效的，而且常常会适得其反。

Top-down allocation of labor and its problems

自上而下的劳动力配置及其问题

But wait! Moralia has a solution. To fix the doctor shortage, it mandates that more people become doctors. This sounds great until we ask who gets drafted into medical service. After all, the shortage exists precisely because too few people want to become doctors unless wages are high enough; so, the government now has to decide whom to compel. This creates two problems.

等等！莫拉利亚提出了一个解决方案。为了解决医生短缺问题，它强制要求更多人成为医生。这听起来很棒，直到我们问谁会被征召入伍。毕竟，医生短缺的根源恰恰在于，除非工资足够高，否则很少有人愿意当医生；因此，政府现在必须决定强制哪些人入伍。这就产生了两个问题。

First, how do you pick the right people? In Pragmatia , higher wages draw many candidates, so medical schools simply choose the most qualified. However , in Moralia , where hard jobs pay little, smarter people may deliberately fail admission to careers that are not worth the effort, or otherwise try to manipulate their performance in job assessments.

首先，如何挑选合适的人才？在实用主义社会，高薪吸引众多求职者，因此医学院只需选择最合格者即可。然而，在道德主义社会，艰苦的工作收入微薄，聪明人可能会故意挂科，拒绝那些不值得付出努力的职业，或者试图操纵求职评估中的表现。

Second, coerced doctors are unlikely to be motivated. Would you want surgery from someone wielding a scalpel only because they were ordered to?

其次，被迫行医的医生不太可能积极主动。你会希望让一个仅仅因为接到命令才挥舞手术刀的人为你动手术吗？

This is what Moralia’s leaders do not understand: the country does not just need a certain number of people with “doctor” printed on their badges; instead, it needs tens of thousands of successful procedures each year. The quality and motivation of doctors matter enormously.

这就是莫拉利亚领导人不明白的地方：国家需要的不仅仅是一定数量的胸牌上印着“医生”字样的人；相反，它需要每年数万例成功的手术。医生的素质和积极性至关重要。

Moralia could offer small perks or modest wage bumps to attract more doctors, but this would only go partway. To truly solve the shortage, it would have to raise wages enough to attract qualified, motivated candidates. In other words, it would have to match what Pragmatia already pays: market wages.

Moralia或许可以提供一些小福利或适度的加薪来吸引更多医生，但这只能起到部分作用。要真正解决医生短缺问题，它必须大幅提高工资，才能吸引合格且积极的求职者。换句话说，它必须达到Pragmatia目前的薪资水平：市场工资标准。

Of course, reality is not as black and white as depicted by Moralia and Pragmatia . Still , the contrast between these two imaginary countries illustrates effects that are often overlooked in public discussions about wages and job markets.

当然，现实并非像《道德论》和《实用论》所描述的那样非黑即白。不过，这两个虚构国家的对比确实揭示了一些在关于工资和就业市场的公共讨论中常常被忽视的影响因素。

# ↩

The Bigger Picture

大局观

This is not just about doctors or wages. It is about meeting basic needs. Essential goods and services such as healthcare, food, and housing directly affect everyone’s quality of life. Meeting these needs requires not just people in jobs but productive, competent professionals who do them well. Unless workers are matched to where they are most needed and motivated to perform, everyone’s quality of life will decline.

这不仅仅关乎医生或工资，更关乎基本需求的满足。医疗保健、食品和住房等必需品和服务直接影响着每个人的生活质量。满足这些需求不仅需要人们就业，更需要高效、称职的专业人士。除非劳动者能够胜任最需要的岗位，并被激励去努力工作，否则每个人的生活质量都将下降。

The best way to achieve this is not through top-down coercion but bottom-up allocation, letting wages signal which jobs face the greatest unmet demand.

实现这一目标的最佳途径不是自上而下的强制，而是自下而上的配置，让工资反映出哪些工作面临最大的未满足需求。

Chapter summary

章节概要

Wages signal demand-supply mismatches that should be solved structurally rather than superficially.

工资水平反映了供需不匹配的问题，应该从结构上而不是表面上解决这个问题。

Moreover, wages are among the best tools for driving such structural change while preserving individual choice.

此外，工资是推动这种结构性变革并同时保障个人选择的最佳工具之一。

* * *

Having explored the role of wages, we will examine prices in the next chapter.

在探讨了工资的作用之后，我们将在下一章研究价格。

* * *

Note: There is far more to say about wages than what I have covered in the last few pages. An important consideration is an effect called Baumol’s Cost Disease . However , while highly significant, it does not alter the preferred policy choices compared with not knowing about it. Therefore , to keep the book streamlined, I have relegated this discussion to the endnote below. ⁠ 4

注：关于工资，还有很多内容需要讨论，远不止我在前几页所涵盖的。一个重要的考虑因素是鲍莫尔成本病效应。然而，尽管该效应非常显著，但与不知道它的存在相比，它并不会改变人们的政策选择。因此，为了保持本书的简洁性，我将此讨论放在下面的尾注中。

* * *

1 A more precise definition is that wages signal a mismatch between demand and supply after taking into account their elasticity . For example, imagine an island needing 10 bartenders and 10 doctors and having exactly 10 of each. In this equilibrium, doctors would still have higher wages, but why, if demand perfectly matches supply? That’s because it matters whether people would rather work as bartenders or doctors at the same wage. The greater the difference in preferences, the higher the required difference between wages to reach equilibrium without coercion. This phenomenon is further explained in the last chapter of this book, “Choice and Coercion.”

更精确的定义是，工资反映了在考虑供给弹性之后，供求关系是否匹配。例如，假设一个岛屿需要10名调酒师和10名医生，并且恰好各有10名。在这种均衡状态下，医生的工资仍然会更高，但如果供求完全匹配，为什么呢？这是因为人们更愿意以相同的工资从事调酒师还是医生的工作至关重要。偏好差异越大，为了在不强制的情况下达到均衡，所需的工资差距就越大。本书最后一章“选择与强制”将对此现象进行更深入的解释。

2 This also explains the existence of high-paying jobs that arguably add little value, such as some “empty suits.” Wages are mostly not a measure of value but of the mismatch between demand and supply.

2 这也解释了为什么有些高薪工作实际上价值不高，例如一些“空架子”工作。工资大多不是价值的衡量标准，而是供需不匹配程度的体现。

3 Of course, wages are an incredibly complex topic, with many factors to consider: the delays with which some demand-supply mismatches affect pay, the country’s transportation and education infrastructure, and more. This chapter does not aim to be a comprehensive treatise on wages. Its goal is simply to explain the one concept whose importance outweighs everything else: that wages are, first and foremost, signals of mismatches between demand and supply.

3 当然，工资是一个极其复杂的话题，需要考虑诸多因素：例如，某些供需不匹配对工资的影响存在滞后性，以及国家的交通和教育基础设施等等。本章并非旨在对工资进行全面论述，其目的仅在于阐明一个至关重要的概念：工资首先是供需不匹配的信号。

4 Imagine a town with a fast-growing technology company. As its productivity rises, the tech company hires more people and pays them more. Other employers, such as the local baker, must also raise wages to attract workers or, at least, not lose existing ones.

4. 想象一下，在一个小镇上，有一家快速发展的科技公司。随着生产力的提高，这家科技公司雇佣了更多员工，并提高了他们的工资。其他雇主，例如当地的面包师，也必须提高工资才能吸引员工，或者至少不流失现有员工。

What happens to prices? Tech products become cheaper as long as productivity rises faster than wages. But bread becomes more expensive because baker productivity has not increased, but their wages have.

价格会发生什么变化？只要生产率增长速度超过工资增长速度，科技产品就会变得更便宜。但面包会变得更贵，因为面包师的生产率没有提高，而他们的工资却提高了。

This phenomenon, where productivity gains in one industry push up prices in others, is called “Baumol’s Cost Disease,” after the American economist who first described it.

这种现象，即一个行业的生产率提高推高了其他行业的价格，被称为“鲍莫尔成本病”，以首次描述这一现象的美国经济学家鲍莫尔的名字命名。

I did not include this topic in the main text because, while important, it does not substantially change the book’s recommendations. For example, one implication is that since government services lag in productivity compared with the private sector, their costs tend to rise over time. Unless budgets also grow, public services deteriorate. So, what should we do about it? The same things we should do even without knowing about Baumol’s Cost Disease: improve job efficiency, especially in public services, which otherwise tend to become less efficient over time.

我没有在正文中详细讨论这个话题，因为它虽然重要，但并不会实质性地改变本书的建议。例如，其中一个推论是，由于政府服务的生产力落后于私营部门，其成本往往会随着时间的推移而上升。除非预算也相应增加，否则公共服务质量就会下降。那么，我们应该怎么做呢？即使不了解鲍莫尔成本病，我们也应该采取同样的做法：提高工作效率，尤其是在公共服务领域，否则公共服务的效率往往会随着时间的推移而降低。

(Why do public services tend to become less efficient over time? One reason is that they lack the healthy replacement effect of the private sector, where unproductive firms go out of business and are replaced by more productive ones.)

（为什么公共服务效率会随着时间推移而降低？原因之一是它们缺乏私营部门那种健康的更替效应，在私营部门，生产力低下的企业会倒闭，并被生产力更高的企业所取代。）
