PART II
第二部分

VIRTUE AND DECADENCE

美德与颓废

Part I examined the policies that lead to poverty and those that foster prosperity. But why do countries often choose the former?

第一部分探讨了导致贫困的政策和促进繁荣的政策。但为什么各国往往选择前者呢？

What cultural and societal factors push formerly thriving nations toward a trajectory of poverty?

哪些文化和社会因素导致曾经繁荣的国家走向贫困？

And how can we influence these factors to create fertile ground for prosperity?

我们该如何影响这些因素，从而为繁荣创造沃土？

Part II answers these questions, starting with an analysis of how our tendency to treat demand and supply as fixed quantities leads us to misunderstand how the economy works.

第二部分回答了这些问题，首先分析了我们倾向于将需求和供给视为固定数量的做法如何导致我们误解经济的运作方式。

# ↩
14

ECONOMICS WITHOUT MONEY

没有货币的经济学

A s Italian economist Sandro Brusco noted, most bad policy ideas start with the assumption that demand, supply, and prices are fixed. If the supply of goods cannot change, taxing producers or capping prices seems harmless and is treated as a no-brainer. Similarly , if the supply of crimes is fixed, imprisonment offers little benefit and is seen as immoral toward criminals.

正如意大利经济学家桑德罗·布鲁斯科所指出的，大多数糟糕的政策构想都源于一个假设：需求、供给和价格都是固定的。如果商品供给无法改变，那么对生产者征税或限制价格似乎就无害，被视为理所当然之举。同样地，如果犯罪供给是固定的，那么监禁就几乎没有任何益处，而且会被视为对罪犯不道德的做法。

But why do we default to thinking about the economy in fixed terms, even though we live in a dynamic world? I believe it comes from our fixation on measuring everything in dollars (or any local currency). The moment money enters the conversation, our brains tend to switch from dynamic to static thinking. For example, if a house costs $500,000 and one only has $300,000, the solution to their lack of housing is anchored around needing the missing $200,000. But if everyone were given $200,000 without increasing the number of houses, no one would gain a home. Conversely , removing money from the conversation makes the solution clearer. If 10 million households want a home, but only 9 million homes exist, the answer is simple: we need to build more houses.

但为什么我们明明生活在一个动态的世界里，却总是习惯用固定的货币单位来思考经济呢？我认为这源于我们执着于用美元（或其他任何当地货币）来衡量一切。一旦谈到金钱，我们的思维方式就会从动态切换到静态。例如，如果一套房子价值50万美元，而某人只有30万美元，那么解决住房问题的方案就围绕着如何筹集剩余的20万美元。但如果每个人都得到20万美元，却不增加住房数量，那么最终没有人能拥有自己的房子。反之，如果把金钱因素排除在外，解决方案就更加清晰了。如果有1000万户家庭想要住房，但只有900万套住房，答案很简单：我们需要建造更多的房子。

Focusing on the quantities of goods and services helps us see that prices are usually symptoms, not causes, of our problems.

关注商品和服务的数量有助于我们认识到，价格通常是问题的表象，而不是问题的根源。

Instead of asking how much someone should earn to live comfortably, we should ask how to produce enough goods and services for everyone. Or instead of asking how to get the money we lack, we should ask how to get the things we lack.

与其问一个人应该挣多少钱才能过上舒适的生活，我们不如问问如何生产出足够所有人使用的商品和服务。或者，与其问如何获得我们所缺乏的金钱，我们不如问如何获得我们所缺乏的物品。

This way of thinking is more flexible and effective.

这种思维方式更加灵活有效。

Two ways to think about inequality

思考不平等问题的两种方式

At the time of writing, Elon Musk is worth about $413 billion. Many see this as unsettling, but a more nuanced view is helpful. Does Musk hoard all this wealth in a mega coffer like a modern Scrooge McDuck ? Obviously not. Most of it consists of shares of his companies. In other words, he owns factories and tools that provide goods, services, jobs, and innovation. He may also own national bonds, which help fund schools, hospitals, and other public services. He may enjoy villas and sports cars, but they make up only a tiny fraction of his wealth.

截至撰稿时，埃隆·马斯克的净资产约为4130亿美元。许多人对此感到不安，但更细致的分析或许更有帮助。马斯克是否像现代版的史高治·麦克老鸭那样，把所有财富都藏在一个巨型金库里？显然不是。他的大部分财富都以他旗下公司的股份形式存在。换句话说，他拥有生产商品、提供服务、创造就业机会和推动创新的工厂和设备。他可能还持有国家债券，这些债券用于资助学校、医院和其他公共服务。他或许享受别墅和跑车，但这些仅占其财富的一小部分。

How we think about wealth shapes the discussion. If we imagine wealth as stored resources, inequality seems important: one person’s gain is another’s loss. But if we think of wealth as factories, tools, and government loans, the focus shifts: what matters is that factories and government services exist and function efficiently and effectively.

我们如何看待财富会影响讨论。如果我们把财富想象成储存的资源，那么不平等就显得尤为重要：一个人的获益就意味着另一个人的损失。但如果我们把财富看作是工厂、工具和政府贷款，那么重点就发生了转变：重要的是工厂和政府服务能够存在并高效运转。

This is not to dismiss concerns about inequality entirely (for example, the next page addresses concerns regarding political influence), but to highlight that inequality is a far less pressing concern than poverty. Burning all of Musk’s “excess” wealth for the sake of equality would make us worse off, destroying not just money but productive assets and public funds.

这并非完全否定对不平等的担忧（例如，下一页将探讨政治影响力问题），而是要强调，与贫困相比，不平等远不是那么紧迫的问题。为了所谓的平等而焚毁马斯克的所有“剩余”财富，只会让我们的处境更加糟糕，不仅会摧毁金钱，还会摧毁生产性资产和公共资金。

A better approach to measuring inequality is to consider only personal-use assets. How many cars, houses, etc., does Musk own in excess of the average or median citizen? That’s a more precise and practical measure of inequality. It also reveals that true inequality is lower than what just measuring wealth shows. Once again, thinking in terms of goods and services rather than dollars brings clarity.

衡量不平等的更佳方法是只考虑个人用途的资产。马斯克拥有的汽车、房屋等资产比普通公民或中位数公民多多少？这才是更精确、更实用的不平等衡量标准。它还揭示出，真正的不平等程度低于仅衡量财富所显示的水平。再次强调，用商品和服务而非金钱来思考问题，能带来更清晰的认识。

Political inequality

政治不平等

Allow me a brief digression to address concerns that financial inequality gives the ultra-rich undue political influence. As entrepreneur Balaji Srinivasan points out, there are “political billionaires” who control enormous budgets despite not being especially wealthy. For example, he wrote (slightly edited for clarity): “ Political billionaires spend far more than mere tech billionaires. Consider San Francisco : it has a $14B budget, with eleven supervisors and one mayor; that’s more than $1B in cash per person per year. By contrast, a tech billionaire may have a billion in net worth, but only 5–10% is liquid, and that over their entire life. So , while a political billionaire controls $1B in cash per year, a tech billionaire can allocate maybe $100M over decades.” To me, political inequality seems a bigger concern than financial inequality.

请允许我稍作补充，谈谈人们对金融不平等赋予超级富豪过大政治影响力的担忧。正如企业家巴拉吉·斯里尼瓦桑（Balaji Srinivasan）所指出的，有些“政治亿万富翁”虽然并非特别富有，却掌控着巨额预算。例如，他写道（为了清晰起见略作编辑）：“政治亿万富翁的支出远远超过普通的科技亿万富翁。以旧金山为例：它拥有140亿美元的预算，由11名监事和1名市长组成；这意味着人均每年超过10亿美元的现金支出。相比之下，一位科技亿万富翁的净资产可能达到10亿美元，但只有5%到10%是流动资产，而且这还是在其一生中积累的。因此，虽然一位政治亿万富翁每年可以掌控10亿美元的现金，但一位科技亿万富翁可能只能在几十年内分配1亿美元。”在我看来，政治不平等似乎比金融不平等更令人担忧。

Two ways to think about productivity

思考生产力的两种方式

Imagine your local hairdresser suddenly operating without money, trading goods and services directly. His value would be measured by what he produces for others: “ Today , my customers paid me four pizzas and six burgers. That means I created value equal to ten meals.”

想象一下，你家附近的理发师突然间没有了资金，直接以商品和服务进行交易。他的价值将以他为他人创造的价值来衡量：“今天，我的顾客付给我四个披萨和六个汉堡。这意味着我创造的价值相当于十份餐食。”

If that hairdresser were unproductive and only delivered a few haircuts for which customers are only willing to pay a total of two meals, but the hairdresser eats three meals a day, it would be clear how that hairdresser’s lack of productivity made society less prosperous. This perspective highlights the importance of allocating jobs productively: if someone works in a role that produces less than they consume, the community remains with less to share.

如果一位理发师效率低下，每天只剪几次头发，而顾客只愿意支付相当于两顿饭的钱，但他自己却一天吃三顿饭，那么很明显，这位理发师的低效会降低社会的繁荣程度。这种观点凸显了合理分配工作的重要性：如果一个人的工作产出低于其消费，那么社会可共享的资源就会减少。

The same approach works in other contexts. Estimating the costs of renovating the local theater as “50 homes” rather than “$20 million” would help us make smarter choices: do we prefer a renovated theater or fifty homes for the community? Similarly , an inefficient post office means citizens spend more time in line and thus less time working, reducing the amount of goods and services available to the community.

同样的道理也适用于其他情况。如果将翻新当地剧院的成本估算为“50套住房”而不是“2000万美元”，就能帮助我们做出更明智的选择：我们是更希望翻新剧院，还是更希望为社区建造50套住房？同样，邮局效率低下意味着居民要花更多时间排队，从而减少工作时间，最终导致社区可获得的商品和服务减少。

Efficiency matters not just to company owners but to society as a whole.

效率不仅对公司所有者重要，对整个社会也至关重要。

Two ways to think about tariffs

思考关税的两种方式

If one believes the goal of the economy is to accumulate or distribute enough money for a wealthy life, tariffs might make sense. Imports are money leaving the country, so they should be minimized, and taxing them gives the government cash to use as it sees fit.

如果认为经济的目标是积累或分配足够的财富以维持富裕的生活，那么征收关税或许就说得通了。进口意味着资金流出国外，因此应该尽量减少进口，而对进口征税则能为政府提供可自由支配的资金。

However, if one sees the economy’s goal as increasing the amount of goods and services to make them cheaper and more accessible, it’s easy to see how tariffs are mostly counterproductive (with the narrow exception of incentivizing strategic industries). They reduce the flow of goods and services into the country and limit the raw materials and components available to domestic producers, making production more expensive. Once again, focusing on goods and services rather than money brings clarity to policy-making.

然而，如果将经济目标视为增加商品和服务数量，使其价格更低廉、更容易获得，那么很容易理解为什么关税大多会适得其反（除了激励战略性产业这一少数例外）。关税会减少流入本国的商品和服务，限制国内生产商可获得的原材料和零部件，从而增加生产成本。再次强调，关注商品和服务而非货币，有助于政策制定更加清晰。

# ↩

Chapter summary

章节概要

We often equate money with goods and services, since having money allows us to buy them. This works for a single transaction, a snapshot in which demand, supply, and prices can be treated as constant. But it’s different for a nation conducting countless transactions over the years. Demand , supply, and prices fluctuate, and money is useless if there aren’t enough goods and services for everyone.

我们常常将金钱等同于商品和服务，因为有了钱我们就能购买它们。这种观点适用于单笔交易，也就是需求、供给和价格可以被视为恒定不变的瞬间。但对于一个国家多年来进行的无数交易而言，情况就截然不同了。需求、供给和价格都在波动，如果商品和服务不足以满足所有人的需求，那么金钱就毫无用处。

That’s why it is important to discuss the economy and policies in terms of goods and services, not just money. Asking “ Does this policy increase the amount of goods and services in the country?” is far more meaningful than “ Does it increase wages?” Similarly , inequality in access to goods and services matters far more than inequality in net worth. We should be wary of policies that promise financial wealth while reducing access to goods and services.

因此，讨论经济和政策时，我们应该从商品和服务的角度出发，而不仅仅是金钱。与其问“这项政策是否提高了工资？”，不如问“这项政策是否增加了国内的商品和服务总量？”，这更有意义。同样，商品和服务获取方面的不平等远比净资产方面的不平等重要得多。我们应该警惕那些承诺增加经济财富却减少商品和服务获取的政策。

Next time you hear a policy debate, try mentally replacing every dollar sign with actual goods and services. You might be surprised by how differently the issue looks.

下次你听政策辩论时，试着把每一个美元符号都替换成实际的商品和服务。你可能会惊讶地发现，问题看起来完全不一样了。

15

FAIRNESS IN A PROSPEROUS ECONOMY

繁荣经济中的公平

T his chapter examines fairness in wages and prices, but to make the discussion clearer, I must begin with a brief digression on fairness in the justice system.

本章探讨工资和价格的公平性，但为了使讨论更清晰，我必须先简要地谈谈司法系统的公平性。

Prisons serve several purposes: punishment (for past crimes), dissuasion (for future ones), rehabilitation (helping offenders reintegrate into society), and incapacitation (preventing further crimes). Someone who sees prison mainly as punitive will base sentences on how evil they believe a criminal is, whereas someone who sees prison mainly as incapacitative will base sentences on how dangerous they think the offender is.

监狱有多种用途：惩罚（针对过去的犯罪行为）、威慑（预防未来的犯罪行为）、改造（帮助罪犯重新融入社会）以及限制犯罪能力（防止再次犯罪）。如果人们主要将监狱视为惩罚手段，那么他们会根据罪犯的邪恶程度来量刑；而如果人们主要将监狱视为限制犯罪能力的手段，那么他们会根据罪犯的危险程度来量刑。

These assumptions lead to very different views on sentencing. For instance, a person assuming prison’s main function is punitive might favor a short sentence for a mentally ill killer who didn’t know what they were doing. Conversely , someone assuming a prison’s main function is incapacitative might favor a long sentence, since the killer’s lack of awareness makes them especially dangerous.

这些假设导致了截然不同的量刑观点。例如，如果有人认为监狱的主要功能是惩罚，那么他可能会倾向于对患有精神疾病且不了解自己行为的杀人犯判处短期监禁。相反，如果有人认为监狱的主要功能是剥夺犯罪能力，那么他可能会倾向于判处长期监禁，因为杀人犯缺乏认知能力使其格外危险。

The point is that one’s belief about prison’s purpose shapes their view of what constitutes fair sentencing. Similarly , people’s opinions of what is fair with respect to prices and wages depend on what they believe their primary function is.

关键在于，人们对监狱目的的信念会影响他们对公平判决的看法。同样，人们对价格和工资公平性的看法也取决于他们认为价格和工资的主要功能是什么。

The function of wages

工资的功能

Wages serve two functions: allocative and distributive.

工资具有两种功能：配置功能和分配功能。

  • Wages are allocative in that they guide people’s choices about which work to pursue and how hard and long to work at it. If artists and engineers earned the same, society would end up with too many artists and too few engineers, leading to fewer and therefore more expensive manufactured goods and services. By paying engineers more, wages influence the career choices of many young people, helping balance jobs to maximize consumer surplus.
    工资具有资源配置作用，因为它影响着人们选择从事哪种工作以及工作的强度和时长。如果艺术家和工程师的收入相同，社会最终会面临艺术家过多而工程师过少的局面，导致制成品和服务减少，价格上涨。通过提高工程师的工资，工资水平影响着许多年轻人的职业选择，有助于平衡就业，从而最大化消费者剩余。
  • Wages are distributive in that they determine how the economic pie is shared among individuals and households, shaping living standards and inequality.
    工资具有分配性，因为它决定了经济蛋糕如何在个人和家庭之间分配，从而影响生活水平和不平等状况。

Most people recognize both functions and, therefore, believe that, say, surgeons who underwent long training and work long hours should earn more than burger flippers. However , the different weights that different people assign to the allocative and distributive functions determine how large a wage difference each of them considers fair.

大多数人都认可这两种功能，因此认为，比如说，经过长时间培训且工作时间长的外科医生应该比汉堡店的翻煎员收入更高。然而，不同的人对配置功能和分配功能的权重不同，这决定了他们认为合理的工资差距有多大。

So, just like the question of what sentencing is fair is mostly a question of what the relative weight should be between the punitive and incapacitative functions of prisons, the question of what wages are fair is mostly a question about what the right relative weight should be between the allocative and distributive functions of wages.

因此，正如量刑是否公平的问题主要取决于监狱的惩罚功能和监禁功能之间的相对权重一样，工资是否公平的问题主要取决于工资的配置功能和分配功能之间的正确相对权重。

(Note: from the point of view of workers, all that matters is wage after tax; therefore, for this discussion, we always consider net wages.)

（注：从劳动者的角度来看，最重要的只是税后工资；因此，在本次讨论中，我们始终考虑的是净工资。）

# ↩

Wages and fairness

工资与公平

Imagine a video rental shop still standing on your town’s main street, a remnant of another era. Decades ago, it thrived; today, it is nearly empty. Its owner keeps it open out of passion, even if he earns little from it. As long as he does, however, that valuable space cannot host another business that might better serve the citizens’ needs. Which outcome is fairer: letting the owner keep his beloved but unprofitable shop, or allowing a more in-demand business to take its place? It depends. If the owner accepts lower income in exchange for the satisfaction of doing what he loves, it’s his choice. But if he is shielded from consequences, for example, through subsidies that supplement his low earnings, fairness falters. In that case, taxpayers pay for his choice, and in particular those taxpayers who have made the opposite one: taking less enjoyable jobs precisely because they are in higher demand and thus pay more.

想象一下，你镇上的主街上仍然矗立着一家录像带出租店，它是另一个时代的遗迹。几十年前，它生意兴隆；如今，却几乎空无一人。店主出于热爱，即使收入微薄，也依然坚持营业。然而，只要他还在经营，这块宝贵的店面就无法容纳其他可能更能满足市民需求的商家。哪种结果更公平：让店主继续经营他心爱的、但却不盈利的店铺，还是允许一家更受欢迎的商家取而代之？这取决于具体情况。如果店主为了做自己喜欢的事而接受较低的收入，那是他的选择。但如果他能免于承担后果，例如通过补贴来弥补低收入，那么公平就难以保证。在这种情况下，纳税人将为他的选择买单，尤其是那些做出相反选择的纳税人：他们为了更高的收入而选择从事不那么令人愉快的工作。

Fairness does not mean equality of outcome, but alignment between choices and consequences: whoever enjoys the benefit of a preference should also carry its cost.

公平并不意味着结果平等，而是选择与后果的一致性：享受某种偏好带来的好处的人也应该承担相应的代价。

If this sounds cruel or unjust, it is because we tend to imagine society’s production of goods and services as a fixed quantity. While this is relatively true at the individual level (my work-related choices, like a drop in the ocean, do not meaningfully affect what goods and services are available to others), it is false at the societal level, where the aggregate of our individual choices determines what is available to us.

如果这听起来残酷或不公，那是因为我们倾向于将社会生产的商品和服务视为一个固定总量。虽然这在个人层面上相对正确（我与工作相关的选择，就像沧海一粟，对他人可获得的商品和服务影响甚微），但在社会层面上则不然，我们每个人的选择总和决定了我们最终能获得什么。

Improving living standards, for ourselves or others alike, requires giving large weight to the allocative function of wages.

提高我们自己和他人的生活水平，需要高度重视工资的资源配置功能。

This is not a collectivist argument

这并非集体主义论点。

The point isn’t to suppress choice in favor of collective good: we’re not an insect hive, and people should be free to pursue what matters to them. But since our lives are interconnected and what we can afford depends on what others produce, it’s in everyone’s selfish, individual interest that people have incentives to create what others want; otherwise, almost no one would do what we want, and we wouldn’t be able to have it.

重点并非为了集体利益而压制选择：我们不是虫巢，人们应该有追求自己所重视之事的自由。但由于我们的生活相互关联，我们的消费能力取决于他人的生产，因此，为了每个人的自身利益，人们有动力去创造他人想要的东西；否则，几乎没有人会去做我们想做的事，我们也无从拥有。

The worker-consumer duality

劳动者与消费者的二元性

Let’s dig one last time into our duality as both producers of what others consume and consumers of what others produce, and let’s do it with a personal example. As an author, I am strongly tempted to choose my next book’s topic solely based on my personal interests, neglecting my audience’s needs. I am also tempted to skip spending time polishing my writing for clarity. Yet , I am also a reader, and how much I enjoy reading depends on how much other authors consider my needs over their own when deciding what to write about and how well to do it.

让我们最后再深入探讨一下我们作为生产者和消费者的双重身份，并举一个我个人的例子。作为一名作家，我很容易只根据个人兴趣来选择下一本书的主题，而忽略读者的需求。我也很容易为了追求清晰度而偷工减料，忽略对文字的润色。然而，我同时也是一名读者，我阅读的乐趣取决于其他作者在决定写作主题和写作质量时，是否将我的需求置于自身需求之上。

This same duality applies to everyone: we are both workers and consumers. Our quality of life as consumers depends on how much others weigh our needs when deciding what to work on, how well, and how long to work on it.

这种二元性适用于所有人：我们既是劳动者，也是消费者。作为消费者，我们的生活质量取决于他人在决定我们从事什么工作、工作质量如何以及工作时长时，如何权衡我们的需求。

This duality explains why the distributive function of wages cannot be fulfilled without giving substantial weight to its allocative function. ⁠ 1

这种二元性解释了为什么如果不充分重视工资的配置功能，就无法实现工资的分配功能。

It’s not just about quantity but about the mix, too

重要的不仅是数量，还有组合方式。

This logic goes beyond the simple fact that producing a lot of something makes it cheaper. It is not only about producing enough, but about producing the right mix. For example, take food. Feeding a population is not just a question of volume. The types and quality of foods produced matter just as much. If everyone decided to grow only potatoes, but no other vegetables, abundance would coexist with scarcity.

这种逻辑超越了“大量生产某种产品会降低其成本”这一简单事实。它不仅关乎生产数量，更关乎生产组合的合理性。例如，以食物为例。养活人口不仅仅取决于食物的数量，食物的种类和质量同样重要。如果每个人都只种植土豆，而不种植其他蔬菜，那么就会出现食物过剩与短缺并存的局面。

The same applies to work in general. What counts is not only how many people work, or how efficiently, but what they choose to produce. For society to meet its needs, those choices must be guided by genuine demand, and thus, by the signals that prices and wages convey.

这一点同样适用于所有工作。重要的不仅是工作人数或工作效率，更是他们选择生产什么。为了满足社会的需求，这些选择必须以真实的市场需求为导向，因此，价格和工资所传递的信号也必须得到体现。

This explains why subsidies to specific industries often do more harm than good (with a few exceptions, including temporary aid following a natural disaster). By distorting people’s decisions of what to work on, subsidies encourage the overproduction of unwanted goods and, consequently, the underproduction of desired ones.

这就解释了为什么对特定行业的补贴往往弊大于利（少数例外情况除外，例如自然灾害后的临时援助）。补贴扭曲了人们选择工作方向的决策，导致不受欢迎的商品过度生产，进而造成人们需要的商品生产不足。

# ↩

Fairness and random allocation

公平性和随机分配

As I write these pages, an online debate rages over soaring concert ticket prices, with some calling for price caps. Earlier , I discussed price caps in terms of incentivizing supply, but unlike factories, you can’t easily add a second Taylor Swift . So , for the sake of the exercise, let us only consider effects unrelated to supply, and let’s consider the following thought experiment, proposed by online commenter Wayne Burkett .⁠ 2

在我撰写本文时，网上正就演唱会门票价格飙升展开激烈辩论，一些人呼吁设定价格上限。此前，我曾从激励供给的角度讨论过价格上限，但与工厂不同，你不可能轻易再造一个泰勒·斯威夫特。因此，为了便于讨论，我们只考虑与供给无关的影响，并考虑以下由网络评论员韦恩·伯克特提出的思想实验。

Imagine using lotteries to decide who gets to attend, say, Taylor Swift concerts. I am not a fan, so I would not pay $400 for a ticket, but if entering the lottery were free or almost free, I might do it anyway, and so would millions of others who are not true fans. The audience would then mostly consist of people who do not care much, making the concert worse (crowd energy matters) and wasting much of its value (“value is in the eyes of the beholder,” as they say).

想象一下，如果用抽签来决定谁能参加泰勒·斯威夫特的演唱会，那会是什么景象？我不是她的粉丝，所以我不会花400美元买票，但如果抽签是免费的或者几乎免费，我可能还是会去参加，其他数百万并非铁杆粉丝的人也会这么做。这样一来，观众席上的大部分人都会对演唱会漠不关心，这会让演唱会变得更糟（现场气氛很重要），也浪费了演唱会的大部分价值（正如人们常说的，“价值在于观者的眼中”）。

Some might argue that, although the total value drops, at least a few die-hard fans who cannot afford $400 now have a chance to attend. Yes , but that doesn’t mean they are better off, all things considered. For example, who pays for the concert? If the lottery were free, taxpayers, including these die-hard fans, would pay. A few of them would get free tickets, but would also have to pay for all the concerts they do not attend. That hardly seems fair. And if people had to pay to enter, say $1 per ticket, some fans might spend heavily on lottery tickets and still get none, while a few lucky ones win nearly free tickets. That is not fair either.

有人可能会说，虽然总价值下降了，但至少一些买不起400美元门票的铁杆粉丝现在有机会去现场观看演出了。没错，但考虑到所有因素，这并不意味着他们就更幸运了。例如，谁来支付演唱会的费用？如果抽奖免费，那么包括这些铁杆粉丝在内的纳税人就要买单了。他们中的一些人虽然能获得免费门票，但同时也要为他们没能参加的所有演唱会买单。这显然不公平。如果抽奖需要付费，比如每张票1美元，那么一些粉丝可能会花很多钱买彩票却一无所获，而少数幸运儿却能赢得几乎免费的门票。这同样不公平。

A third idea would be to ration tickets. For example, each person might receive one concert ticket per year. But how to decide who gets to go to the events everyone wants to see? A lottery would create the same problems described above, so that wouldn’t work either. As Burkett goes on writing, “ You definitely want some way for people to prove that they want a good or service more than everybody else […] You have to let people be free to weigh the tradeoffs for themselves in a free market .”

第三个想法是实行门票配给制。例如，每人每年可以获得一张音乐会门票。但是，如何决定谁能去看大家都想看的演出呢？抽签会产生与上述相同的问题，因此行不通。正如伯克特继续写道：“你肯定需要某种方式让人们证明他们比其他人更需要某种商品或服务……你必须让人们在自由市场中自由权衡利弊。”

This illustrates that attempting to equalize access can reduce overall value and fairness, similar to the outcomes of capping wages without regard for productive contribution.

这说明，试图实现机会均等可能会降低整体价值和公平性，类似于不考虑生产贡献而限制工资的结果。

Fairness in an abundant world

富足世界中的公平

Another online commenter, Dylan Esper , poignantly remarked, still referring to the debate on concert tickets being too expensive:⁠ 3 “ People really have to come to grips with what living in a prosperous society means. It means there’s more disposable income chasing limited quantities […] The reason why you could see Sinatra for $5 in a lounge in Vegas in the late 1950s is that a lot of Americans couldn’t afford to travel to Vegas , and it wasn’t easy for most Americans to get there […] You can wish to go back to a world where you could see Sinatra for $5, but the reason that world worked the way it did was because people were poorer and technology was lousier, and folks couldn’t afford to buy nice things. Life sucked a lot more. We’re just paying the price of prosperity, and it's a price worth paying.”

另一位网友迪伦·埃斯珀(Dylan Esper)也发表了一番意味深长的评论，他仍然在讨论演唱会门票价格过高的争议：“人们真的需要好好想想生活在一个繁荣的社会意味着什么。这意味着更多的可支配收入在追逐有限的资源……20世纪50年代末，你之所以能在拉斯维加斯的酒吧里花5美元看到弗兰克·辛纳屈的演出，是因为当时很多美国人负担不起去拉斯维加斯的旅费，而且对大多数美国人来说，去拉斯维加斯也并非易事……你或许会怀念过去花5美元就能看到辛纳屈演出的时代，但那个时代之所以如此，是因为人们更穷，科技更落后，人们买不起好东西。生活也更艰难。我们现在只是在为繁荣付出代价，而这个代价是值得的。”

And that is the crux of the matter. There are enough houses for everyone, just not enough in the most desirable locations; enough education for all, just not enough places at Ivy League colleges; enough entertainment, just not enough tickets to the most sought-after concerts. First -world societies have mostly solved unbranded scarcity; what remains is branded scarcity, which is by definition scarce and, therefore, cannot be truly solved.

这就是问题的关键所在。住房数量足够，只是在最理想的地段不够；教育资源足够，只是常春藤盟校的学位不够；娱乐活动足够，只是最热门音乐会的门票不够。发达国家大多已经解决了非品牌稀缺问题；剩下的就是品牌稀缺问题，而品牌稀缺问题从定义上来说就是稀缺的，因此无法真正解决。

Note that I wrote “mostly.” I do not plan to ignore the places where scarcity still exists. Rather , I want to highlight that, in first-world countries, a significant amount of what people claim is scarce is actually abundant when we consider unbranded versions (think about education after everyone got access to the internet).

请注意我用的是“大多数情况下”。我并非打算忽略仍然存在资源匮乏的地方。相反，我想强调的是，在发达国家，人们声称稀缺的很多东西，如果我们考虑的是非品牌版本（例如，互联网普及后的教育），实际上其实很丰富。

Hence, we shall distinguish between unbranded scarcity (which is relatively easy to solve by removing the frictions that limit the growth of supply) and branded scarcity, which the government should abstain from solving (if anything, because it would incur huge opportunity costs by diverting resources towards a mostly unsolvable problem).

因此，我们将区分非品牌稀缺（通过消除限制供给增长的摩擦相对容易解决）和品牌稀缺，政府应该避免解决品牌稀缺（如果一定要解决的话，因为将资源转移到一个基本无法解决的问题上会产生巨大的机会成本）。

(If the last sentence sounds untrue, let me remind you that branded scarcity increases as the poorest get better off, because now more of them can bid up the price of items that had a more limited audience and have inelastic supply.)

（如果最后一句话听起来不真实，请允许我提醒您，随着最贫困人群的生活水平提高，品牌稀缺性会加剧，因为现在更多的贫困人群可以抬高那些受众有限、供给缺乏弹性的商品的价格。）

Fairness in a perfectly fair world

在一个完美公平的世界里，公平依然存在

Imagine a perfectly fair world where everyone is born with similar health and talents, from equally wealthy, stable, and supportive families, in areas with comparable environments and opportunities, and experiences similar levels of good and bad luck throughout their lives. In this ideal world, we would still observe that:

想象一个完美公平的世界，每个人都拥有相似的健康和天赋，来自同样富裕、稳定和充满关爱的家庭，生活在环境和机遇相近的地区，一生中经历的吉凶祸福也大致相同。在这个理想的世界里，我们仍然会观察到：

  • Older people tend to be wealthier than younger ones (because they have accumulated savings for a longer time).
    老年人往往比年轻人更富有（因为他们积累的积蓄时间更长）。
  • Those who prioritize material possessions over experiences will accumulate more material goods.
    那些将物质财富置于体验之上的人，会积累更多的物质财富。
  • Individuals who focus on providing value to others will receive more in return than those who prioritize their own interests.
    那些专注于为他人创造价值的人，会比那些优先考虑自身利益的人获得更多回报。
  • People who exercise regularly will look better and be healthier than those who do not.
    经常锻炼的人比不锻炼的人身材更好、更健康。

The point of this thought experiment is not to claim that all inequality in the real world stems from personal choices or demographics; clearly, many forms of inequality arise from unfair causes, such as discrimination, theft, or sheer luck. Rather , the aim is to show that even in a perfectly fair world, inequality would still exist.

这个思想实验的目的并非要断言现实世界中的所有不平等都源于个人选择或人口统计因素；显然，许多形式的不平等是由不公平的原因造成的，例如歧视、盗窃或纯粹的运气。相反，其目的是为了表明，即使在一个完全公平的世界里，不平等依然存在。

This matters because people often imagine a fair world as one where everyone ends up equally wealthy, and from that assumption conclude that any inequality must be unfair. Yet , as we’ve seen, even in a perfectly fair world, wealth would differ. What truly counts as unfair, then, is only the inequality that exists on top of what would already arise in a perfectly fair world.

这一点很重要，因为人们常常把公平的世界想象成每个人最终都拥有同等财富的世界，并由此得出结论：任何不平等都是不公平的。然而，正如我们所见，即使在一个完全公平的世界里，财富也会有所不同。因此，真正不公平的，只是在完全公平的世界已经存在的不平等之上，又叠加了其他不平等。

Addressing unfairness beyond that is usually a bad idea. Primarily because of opportunity costs, but also because if the reason Adam has fewer material possessions than Bob is that he prioritized experiences, taking some of Bob’s wealth to give to Adam would be deeply unfair. Societies improve when governments only address the inequality that exists beyond what would appear in a perfectly fair world, and decline when they go further than that.

解决超出表面现象的不公平问题通常不是个好主意。这主要是因为机会成本，也因为如果亚当比鲍勃拥有更少的物质财富是因为他更注重体验，那么拿走鲍勃的一部分财富给亚当就极不公平。政府只解决那些在理想情况下并不存在的、超出公平范畴的不平等现象，社会才能进步；反之，如果政府做得过头，社会就会退步。

Fairness and games people play

人们玩的公平游戏

There are positive-sum games (activities that make society better off, such as a baker baking and selling bread) and negative-sum games (activities that make society worse off, such as theft).⁠ 4

博弈分为正和博弈（使社会受益的活动，例如面包师烘焙和出售面包）和负和博弈（使社会受损的活动，例如盗窃）。

Most people are neither inherently good nor evil; the kinds of games they play depend on their environment and opportunities. In a growing economy, they are more likely to improve their condition through positive-sum games. Conversely , in a stagnant economy, ambitious individuals tend to turn toward negative-sum games.

大多数人并非天生善良或邪恶；他们参与何种博弈取决于所处的环境和机遇。在经济增长时期，他们更有可能通过正和博弈来改善自身境况。相反，在经济停滞时期，雄心勃勃的人往往会转向负和博弈。

Of course, this is not a strict dichotomy. Even in growth, some still rise through negative-sum games, and even in decline, some continue to create value. The difference lies in the proportion of people playing each game. Positive -sum games yield higher returns when the economy expands, making them more appealing, and thus causing more people to play them. Positive -sum games also require a longer-term view, while in times of contraction and scarcity, people’s horizons naturally shorten, causing more people to play short-term games.

当然，这并非绝对的二元对立。即使在经济增长时期，一些企业仍然通过负和博弈获利；即使在衰退时期，一些企业仍然能够创造价值。区别在于参与这两种博弈的人数比例。经济扩张时，正和博弈的回报更高，因此更具吸引力，也更吸引人参与。此外，正和博弈需要更长远的眼光；而在经济萎缩和资源匮乏时期，人们的目光自然会缩短，从而更多地参与短期博弈。

That is another reason why sustaining growth matters: not because growth is an end in itself (it’s not), but because it shapes people’s preferences for what kinds of games to play.

这也是持续增长很重要的另一个原因：不是因为增长本身就是目的（它不是），而是因为它塑造了人们对玩什么类型游戏的偏好。

# ↩

Chapter conclusions

本章结论

This chapter was not meant to be a comprehensive treatise on fairness. Instead , it set out to explore a few related principles and phenomena that are significantly under-discussed.

本章并非旨在对公平进行全面论述，而是着重探讨一些鲜少被讨论的相关原则和现象。

We have seen that while everyone has the right to choose what to work on, and how long and well to do so, one’s quality of life depends on how much others consider one’s needs in their own choices. It is therefore only fair that one’s income, which determines the share of society’s production one can purchase, reflects how much one considers others’ needs when deciding what to work on, how long to work, and how well.

我们已经看到，虽然每个人都有权选择从事什么工作、工作时长以及工作质量，但一个人的生活质量取决于他人在做出选择时对他人的考虑程度。因此，一个人的收入决定了他/她能够购买的社会产品份额，而收入也理应反映出他在决定从事什么工作、工作时长以及工作质量时对他人的考虑程度，这才是公平的。

We have also seen the importance of distinguishing between unbranded scarcity, which can be addressed relatively easily, and branded scarcity, which cannot be fully eliminated and is difficult to reduce without harming the poorest. By refusing to accept the inherent scarcity of branded goods, we end up perceiving scarcity even when there’s abundance.

我们也看到了区分非品牌稀缺性和品牌稀缺性的重要性。非品牌稀缺性相对容易解决，而品牌稀缺性则无法彻底消除，而且在不损害最贫困群体利益的情况下难以减少。如果我们拒绝接受品牌商品固有的稀缺性，最终即使在商品充足的情况下，我们仍然会感受到稀缺。

Finally, we have seen that even in a perfectly fair world, people would still have different outcomes simply because of different choices. All choices bring benefits, but only some of those benefits appear as measurable wealth. We should therefore distinguish between inequality that stems from bad luck or unfair circumstances and inequality that arises from personal choices.

最后，我们看到，即使在完全公平的世界里，人们仍然会因为不同的选择而拥有不同的结果。所有选择都会带来益处，但只有部分益处会以可衡量的财富形式体现出来。因此，我们应该区分因运气不佳或不公平环境造成的不平等，以及因个人选择造成的不平等。

The general point is that fairness and equality are complex topics that must be analyzed at a higher resolution than “inequality is always bad.” Some inequality is unjust, some is not. Solving some of it would be fair, while solving another part of it would be unfair. Addressing some forms would make us better off, while addressing others would make us worse off, including the poorest.

总的来说，公平和平等是复杂的问题，必须从更高的层面进行分析，而不能简单地用“不平等总是坏事”来概括。有些不平等是不公正的，有些则不是。解决一部分不平等是公平的，而解决另一部分不平等则可能是不公平的。解决某些形式的不平等会让我们受益，而解决其他形式的不平等则会让我们（包括最贫困的人）的境况变得更糟。

The discourse around fairness and inequality must match this complexity, or it risks misleading us into poor choices.

围绕公平和不平等的讨论必须与这种复杂性相匹配，否则就有可能误导我们做出错误的选择。

1 There is, of course, an alternative: coercing people into working the exact jobs society needs. However, this would not only be unethical and likely ineffective, but also, perhaps most importantly, would create even more unhappiness than our current imperfect system. By definition, being forced into a job you do not want produces a lower quality of life than willingly taking a job you do not want. In the latter case, the tradeoffs are better, as evidenced by the fact that you chose them without coercion.

当然，还有另一种选择：强迫人们从事社会真正需要的工作。然而，这不仅不道德，而且很可能无效，更重要的是，它造成的痛苦甚至会超过我们目前并不完善的制度。从定义上讲，被迫从事自己不想要的工作，其生活质量必然低于自愿接受自己不想要的工作。在后一种情况下，权衡取舍更为合理，因为这是你在没有受到胁迫的情况下做出的选择。

In practice, total impact is rarely if ever zero-sum. 16

NECESSARY AND SUPERFLUOUS

必要与多余的

L ast week, my local newspaper ran two headlines that caught my eye. The first announced that our town didn’t have the money to hire enough doctors. The second, just inches away, celebrated a $25 million renovation of our modern art museum.

上周，我当地报纸刊登了两条引人注目的头条新闻。第一条新闻宣布我们镇没有足够的资金聘请足够的医生。紧随其后的第二条新闻则庆祝我们现代艺术博物馆耗资2500万美元进行了翻新。

The journalists didn’t notice that the second headline undermined the first. If we have $25 million for an art museum renovation, we also have the money to hire additional doctors. The problem is that we often make budget decisions in isolation, asking, “ Should we give $25 million to the art museum?” instead of considering, “ We have $25 million, should we use it to hire the missing doctors or to renovate the art museum?”

记者们没有注意到第二个标题削弱了第一个标题的说服力。如果我们有2500万美元用于美术馆的翻新，我们也应该有钱聘请更多医生。问题在于，我们常常孤立地做预算决策，问自己“我们应该给美术馆2500万美元吗？”，而不是考虑“我们有2500万美元，我们应该用它来聘请缺席的医生，还是用来翻新美术馆？”

Of course, we should also ask other questions. Does the museum renovation really need to cost $25 million? Could it be done for less? Why is our budget so tight? Can we strengthen the economy to increase tax revenue and thus both the healthcare and culture budgets?

当然，我们也应该问其他问题。博物馆翻修真的需要2500万美元吗？能不能用更少的钱完成？为什么我们的预算如此紧张？我们能否提振经济，增加税收，从而增加医疗保健和文化预算？

Yet the point remains: when allocating money, we often only ask whether an investment is worth it, not whether it is the best use of that money. As we will see over the next pages, this approach produces poor outcomes over the long run.

然而，关键依然在于：在分配资金时，我们往往只考虑一项投资是否值得，而忽略了它是否是资金的最佳用途。正如我们将在后续章节中看到的，从长远来看，这种做法会导致糟糕的结果。

Luxury beliefs

奢侈品理念

Luxury beliefs, a term coined by author Rob Henderson , are perspectives that confer status on the upper class while creating problems for everyone else. The earlier museum renovation example illustrates this perfectly: supporting the arts over healthcare is usually promoted by those who can afford private doctors or feel healthy enough not to expect requiring medical attention anytime soon.

“奢侈观念”（Luxury beliefs）一词由作家罗伯·亨德森（Rob Henderson）提出，指的是那些赋予上层阶级地位却给其他人带来问题的观念。早前的博物馆翻新案例便完美地诠释了这一点：那些能够负担得起私人医生或自认为身体健康、近期无需就医的人，往往会鼓吹支持艺术而非医疗保健。

This pattern is common across society. “ Defund the police” gains traction in safe neighborhoods while affecting high-crime areas. Advocating for an extensive liberal arts education may seem virtuous, but it disadvantages students who need practical skills to earn a living quickly. During the pandemic, young and healthy people often dismissed health precautions, putting the vulnerable at risk.

这种模式在社会各处都很普遍。“削减警察经费”的呼声在治安良好的社区获得支持，却对高犯罪率地区造成影响。倡导普及博雅教育看似高尚，但却使那些需要实用技能才能快速谋生的学生处于不利地位。疫情期间，年轻健康的群体往往忽视了防疫措施，使弱势群体面临风险。

These beliefs are especially dangerous because they appear well-meaning. Yet , they benefit those whose basic needs are already met while harming those still struggling. When societies treat luxury beliefs as universal truths rather than privileged perspectives, decline follows.

这些观念尤其危险，因为它们看似出于好意。然而，它们惠及那些基本需求已得到满足的人，却伤害那些仍在挣扎求生的人。当社会将奢侈观念视为普遍真理而非特权视角时，衰落便随之而来。

Luxury consumption

奢侈消费

Just as individuals hold luxury beliefs, nations engage in luxury consumption: public spending that may be reasonable for wealthy countries but diverts resources from essential needs. This appears in three main ways. First , governments subsidize self-actualization while neglecting survival infrastructure. Supporting arts and sports is admirable, but not before securing healthcare and defense. Second , public discourse focuses on small urgent issues while crucial challenges are ignored. Third , education systems often prioritize length over relevance, creating student debt without delivering enough value in return.

正如个人持有奢侈观念一样，国家也存在奢侈消费：对富裕国家而言或许合理的公共支出，却会挤占原本用于基本需求的资源。这种情况主要体现在三个方面。首先，政府补贴个人自我实现，却忽视了生存基础设施。支持艺术和体育固然值得称赞，但前提是必须保障医疗和国防。其次，公共讨论往往聚焦于一些无关紧要的紧急问题，而忽略了真正重要的挑战。第三，教育体系常常过分注重学时长而非课程实用性，导致学生背负沉重债务，却未能获得足够的教育价值。

This doesn’t mean eliminating all non-essential spending. A museum may receive, say, $2 million for basic operations. However , a $25M renovation is a luxury that should wait until essential healthcare is secured. Countries with financial or infrastructural debt should follow the same principle as household budgeting: essentials first, luxuries later.

这并不意味着要取消所有非必要开支。例如，一家博物馆可能会收到200万美元用于基本运营。然而，耗资2500万美元的翻新工程属于奢侈消费，应该等到基本医疗保健得到保障后再进行。背负财政或基础设施债务的国家应该遵循与家庭预算相同的原则：优先考虑必需品，其次才是奢侈品。

Case study: culture subsidies

案例研究：文化补贴

Allow me a brief diversion on opera tickets. I recently discovered that the city of Geneva subsidizes single opera tickets at about $541 each!⁠ 1 This pattern, where most theater revenue comes from subsidies rather than the audience, is common in Europe . For example, in my hometown of Turin , Italy , public subsidies amount to $163 per ticket, representing about 58% of total revenue (tickets cover another 17%, and the rest comes mostly from private sponsors).⁠ 2 In Paris , public subsidies account for about 57% of the Bastille Opera’s revenue.⁠ 3

请允许我稍微谈谈歌剧票。我最近发现，日内瓦市政府竟然对每张歌剧票进行补贴，补贴金额高达541美元！这种大部分剧院收入来自补贴而非观众的模式在欧洲很常见。例如，在我的家乡意大利都灵，每张票的公共补贴高达163美元，约占总收入的58%（门票收入占17%，其余部分主要来自私人赞助）。在巴黎，巴士底歌剧院的公共补贴约占其收入的57%。

Despite these enormous subsidies, attendance remains low. Last year, Turin’s opera filled only 74% of available seats, even with subsidies lowering the average ticket price from 204€ to 41€, an 80% discount.

尽管政府提供了巨额补贴，但上座率仍然很低。去年，都灵歌剧院的上座率仅为74%，即便补贴已将平均票价从204欧元降至41欧元，优惠幅度高达80%。

The problem is not insufficient subsidies but excessive costs. If Turin’s opera reduced costs by 10%, ticket prices could fall to 20€, assuming the same level of subsidies. A 20% reduction in costs and filling the empty seats could even make tickets free. That would be fantastic.

问题不在于补贴不足，而在于成本过高。如果都灵歌剧院能降低10%的成本，在补贴水平不变的情况下，票价就能降至20欧元。如果成本降低20%，并且填满所有空位，甚至可以实现免费入场。那将是极好的。

The issue is that, too often, subsidies are treated as a false dichotomy: either cover all costs or none. This ignores that some costs are essential (basic staff and utilities), while others are discretionary (unnecessary employees and extravagances). It is critical to ensure that theaters and museums are efficiently managed: culture as a basic good is incompatible with poor management and inflated wages.

问题在于，补贴常常被错误地视为非此即彼的选择：要么全额补贴，要么全额补贴。这种观点忽略了某些成本是必不可少的（例如基本人员配备和水电费），而另一些成本则是可自由支配的（例如不必要的员工和铺张浪费）。确保剧院和博物馆的高效管理至关重要：文化作为一种基本公共服务，与管理不善和工资过高是水火不容的。

This is particularly relevant since public subsidies are a finite quantity. The more we fund unnecessary expenses in one theater, the fewer theaters we can fund. Similarly , the more we fund unnecessary expenses in theaters, the fewer schools and hospitals we can fund.

这一点尤其重要，因为公共补贴是有限的。我们越是资助一家剧院不必要的开支，我们能资助的剧院就越少。同样地，我们越是资助剧院不必要的开支，我们能资助的学校和医院就越少。

It is precisely because culture is important that we should care about how efficiently subsidies are used.

正因为文化很重要，我们才更应该关心补贴的使用效率。

Hence, we shall review the income statements and operating expenses of all recipients of public subsidies carefully and make these subsidies conditional on the recipient removing unnecessary costs.

因此，我们将仔细审查所有公共补贴接受者的损益表和运营费用，并将这些补贴与接受者消除不必要的成本挂钩。

Unless we do that, we will get less culture despite spending more on it.

如果我们不这样做，即使我们在文化方面投入更多，我们得到的文化也会更少。

Decisions in good and bad times

顺境和逆境中的决定

How should a nation spend its money? Think of your household budget: you don't just ask, “ Are two opera tickets worth $200?” but also, " Can we afford them?” and " What else could we do with that money?"

一个国家应该如何使用它的钱？想想你的家庭预算：你不仅会问“两张歌剧票值200美元吗？”，还会问“我们负担得起吗？”以及“我们还能用这笔钱做什么？”

Nations should follow the same logic. In surplus years, some luxury spending is acceptable. However , in deficit years, the focus should be on reducing debt and investing in projects that boost future productivity.

各国应遵循同样的逻辑。在财政盈余年份，适度的奢侈消费是可以接受的。然而，在财政赤字年份，重点应放在减少债务和投资能够提升未来生产力的项目上。

Yet most countries do the opposite. During Europe’s post-war boom, luxury public spending soared. When growth slowed, governments either borrowed more or cut spending across the board, leaving even hospitals underfunded. Borrowing was not used to build future capacity but to maintain an unsustainable lifestyle.

然而，大多数国家的做法恰恰相反。在欧洲战后经济繁荣时期，奢侈性公共支出飙升。当经济增长放缓时，各国政府要么增加借贷，要么全面削减开支，甚至连医院都面临资金不足的问题。借贷并非用于建设未来设施，而是为了维持不可持续的生活方式。

The responsible path in good times is to pay down debt and create a buffer for future crises. Instead , many nations continue borrowing even when prosperous, forcing harsh measures when trouble arrives.

在经济繁荣时期，负责任的做法是偿还债务，为未来的危机建立缓冲。然而，许多国家即便在经济繁荣时期也继续举债，一旦遇到困难，就不得不采取严厉的措施。

The following quote by investor Howard Marks captures another risk of prosperity: “ Investments are made that shouldn’t be made, buildings are built that shouldn’t be built, and risks are borne that shouldn’t be borne.” And even worse, because the consequences fall on future generations, current leaders and voters can ignore them.

投资者霍华德·马克斯的以下引言揭示了繁荣带来的另一个风险：“人们会做出不该做的投资，建造不该建造的建筑，承担不该承担的风险。”更糟糕的是，由于后果将由子孙后代承担，当前的领导人和选民可以对此视而不见。

The key point is that public spending decisions must differ sharply depending on whether a country runs a surplus or a deficit.

关键在于，一个国家是财政盈余还是财政赤字，其公共支出决策必然会有显著差异。

Governments that fail to do so set their nations on a path of increasing poverty.

未能做到这一点的政府将使国家走上日益贫困的道路。

# ↩

Preventing complacency

防止自满

To stay on a responsible path even during good times, we should celebrate past decisions that brought prosperity and remember those that brought poverty. This could be done in schools, on television, or even with a national “ Poverty and Prosperity ” holiday, not to forget the lessons of the past, and not to grow complacent.

为了即使在顺境中也能保持负责任的态度，我们应该庆祝过去那些带来繁荣的决策，并铭记那些导致贫困的决策。这可以通过学校教育、电视节目，甚至设立全国性的“贫困与繁荣”假日来实现，以此铭记历史教训，避免自满懈怠。

These remembrances must go beyond superficial mentions of past events. They should explain why good and bad decisions were made and for what purpose. When recalling past mistakes, it is crucial not to see ourselves as superior to those who made them, but to understand what might have led smart and reasonable people to make those errors and what similar mistakes could seem smart and reasonable today.

这些回忆不应仅仅停留在对过往事件的表面提及。它们应该解释当时做出正确或错误决定的原因和目的。在回顾过去的错误时，至关重要的是不要认为自己比犯错的人更优越，而是要理解是什么原因导致聪明理智的人犯下这些错误，以及在今天看来，类似的错误又会显得多么明智和合理。

Similarly, we should study past successes and failures without politicizing them. For example, describing Nazism primarily as “far-right” rather than “authoritarian” risks narrowing our understanding of its nature and enabling new authoritarian movements to emerge under different symbols.

同样，我们在研究过去的成败时，也应该避免将其政治化。例如，如果仅仅将纳粹主义描述为“极右翼”而非“威权主义”，就可能限制我们对纳粹主义本质的理解，并可能使新的威权运动以不同的象征符号出现。

It is necessary to keep historical lessons as apolitical as possible to protect common sense from partisanship and enable more people to recognize past successes and call out past mistakes.

为了保护常识免受党派偏见的影响，并使更多的人能够认识到过去的成功并指出过去的错误，有必要尽可能地保持历史教训的非政治性。

# ↩

Chapter summary

章节概要

Making smart choices about resources does not imply eliminating everything beyond the bare necessities. Rather , it requires honesty about what’s essential and what’s a luxury, and ensuring that the latter only receives the bare minimum until the former is satisfied.

明智地分配资源并不意味着要舍弃一切必需品以外的东西。相反，它需要诚实地分辨什么是必需品，什么是奢侈品，并确保在必需品得到满足之前，奢侈品只能获得最低限度的供给。

This is not a call for austerity but wisdom: because money, energy, and focus are scarce resources, we must spend them wisely.

这不是呼吁节俭，而是呼吁智慧：因为金钱、精力和注意力都是稀缺资源，我们必须明智地使用它们。

Countries become and remain prosperous in the measure they prioritize the necessary over the superfluous and decline in the measure they do not.

一个国家能否繁荣昌盛，取决于它是否优先考虑必需品而非非必需品；反之，则取决于它是否优先考虑必需品而非非必需品。

17

NOW AND LATER

现在和以后

W ealth creation and wealth redistribution are commonly associated with capitalism and communism, respectively.

财富创造和财富再分配通常分别与资本主义和共产主义联系在一起。

However, it would be unfair to say that capitalism does not care about redistribution or that communism does not care about creation. After all, the epitome of capitalism, the USA , spends over 22% of its federal budget on social security, and the epitome of communism, the USSR , famously pursued ambitious industrial plans. In fact, wealth creation and redistribution are practiced in all countries, poor or prosperous, developing or decadent; what changes is the relative importance given to each.

然而，说资本主义不关心财富再分配，或者共产主义不关心财富创造，都是不公平的。毕竟，资本主义的典范——美国，将其联邦预算的22%以上用于社会保障；而共产主义的典范——苏联，也曾大力推行雄心勃勃的工业计划。事实上，财富创造和再分配在所有国家都存在，无论贫穷还是富裕，发展中还是衰落；不同之处在于，各国对二者的重视程度有所不同。

Is there an optimal point?

是否存在最佳点？

The next chart suggests that there is.

下一张图表表明确实如此。

# ↩

The most misunderstood chart in economy

经济领域最容易被误解的图表

The chart below depicts the so-called Laffer Curve , and most people misunderstand its key takeaway.

下图描绘了所谓的拉弗曲线，但大多数人误解了它的关键含义。

The horizontal axis represents a country’s tax rate, and the vertical axis represents its tax revenue.

横轴代表一个国家的税率，纵轴代表该国的税收收入。

The left part of the curve rises because increasing the tax rate also increases the tax collected. The right part drops because excessively high tax rates lead people to evade taxes or leave the country. ( Of course, the curve in real life is not as perfectly round as the one depicted below, but its general shape is similar.)

曲线左侧上升是因为提高税率也会增加税收。曲线右侧下降是因为过高的税率会导致人们逃税或移居国外。（当然，现实生活中的曲线并不像下图所示那样完美圆润，但其大致形状相似。）

Most people focus on point B , which maximizes tax revenue. This point is important, but not as important as point A , which represents the point of maximum tax revenue growth.

大多数人关注的是B点，即税收收入最大化点。这一点固然重要，但不如A点重要，A点代表的是税收收入增长最大化点。

The fact that points A and B do not coincide is the most important feature of this chart.

A点和B点不重合是该图表最重要的特征。

Let’s see why.

让我们来看看原因。

The axes do not contain scales because the chart is supposed to be qualitative. After all, the exact shape of the curve varies for each country.

由于该图表旨在定性展示数据，因此坐标轴没有刻度。毕竟，每个国家的曲线形状都不尽相同。

A, B, and the road to C

A、B 以及通往 C 的路

First of all, let me justify the existence of points A and B .⁠ 1

首先，让我证明点 A 和点 B 的存在性。

Point B exists because excessive tax rates are usually followed by tax evasion or emigration. Even if draconian measures prevent these, excessive tax rates still mean that capital is taken from those who have proven they can use it best and given to those who can use it worst.

B点之所以存在，是因为过高的税率通常会导致逃税或移民。即使严厉的措施能够阻止这些行为，过高的税率仍然意味着资本从那些已经证明自己能够最好地利用资本的人手中流向了那些最不会善用资本的人。

Point A exists for a similar reason. Lower tax rates incentivize the immigration of people and capital and thus grow the tax base, leading to higher future tax revenue even if the tax rate remains constant. Moreover , lower tax rates also mean that more capital remains with its best allocators, growing a country’s wealth over time and, consequently, its tax base and tax revenue.

A点的存在也出于类似的原因。较低的税率能够激励人口和资本的流入，从而扩大税基，即使税率保持不变，也能带来更高的未来税收收入。此外，较低的税率也意味着更多的资本会留在最合适的投资者手中，随着时间的推移，这将增加国家的财富，进而扩大税基，提高税收收入。

It is paramount to acknowledge that points A and B do not coincide. This means there is a tradeoff between increasing today’s tax revenue and increasing tomorrow’s.

必须认识到，A点和B点并不重合。这意味着增加当前的税收收入和增加未来的税收收入之间存在权衡取舍。

I’m not saying that countries should necessarily aim for point A . I can see reasons, such as temporary crises, why a country might want to move closer to B . However , two things should be clearly understood: (1) that moving away from A toward B means shrinking future tax revenue, and (2) that moving from B toward C is suicidal.⁠ 2

我并不是说各国一定要以A点为目标。我能理解一些原因，比如暂时的危机，会让一个国家想要向B点靠拢。但是，有两点必须明确：（1）从A点向B点靠拢意味着未来税收收入的减少；（2）从B点向C点靠拢无异于自杀。

Of course, the Laffer Curve only partially explains a country’s future trajectory, but it is an important factor. We have seen how being overly eager to solve problems quickly without thinking about the long term is, to put it mildly, very suboptimal, whereas a longer-term outlook is beneficial.

当然，拉弗曲线只能部分解释一个国家的未来发展轨迹，但它是一个重要的因素。我们已经看到，过于急于快速解决问题而不考虑长远发展，说得委婉些，是非常不明智的，而着眼长远则更有益。

Now, let’s look at another instance of this fallacy: modern activism.

现在，让我们来看另一个体现这种谬误的例子：现代行动主义。

# ↩

Activism in 2024

2024年的行动主义

Throwing soup at Van Gogh paintings, sitting on the highway to block traffic, and spraying orange paint on Stonehenge are just some of the stunts climate activists performed in 2024. Of course, these acts do not represent the whole movement (there are more serious activists), but they have become the movement's most visible face.

向梵高的画作泼汤、坐在高速公路上堵塞交通、在巨石阵上喷洒橙色油漆，这些只是气候活动人士在2024年实施的一些噱头。当然，这些行为并不能代表整个运动（还有更严肃的活动人士），但它们已经成为该运动最引人注目的面孔。

Throwing soup and throwing a tantrum while sitting on the ground are also tactics used by another notable group: toddlers. In fact, writer Gurwinder Bhogal coined the term “ Neotoddlerism ” to describe “the view that utopia can be achieved by acting like a 3-year-old.”

扔汤、坐在地上发脾气，也是另一群值得关注的群体——幼儿——常用的策略。事实上，作家古尔温德·博加尔创造了“新幼儿主义”一词，用来描述“认为像3岁孩子一样行事就能实现理想境界的观点”。

Shocking acts like those performed by neotoddler activists might seem effective at first glance. They grab attention and attract like-minded supporters. Eventually , though, these activist groups will find it impossible to grow further once they run out of extremists to enlist and have to engage with the bulk of the population that hates vandals.

像幼儿激进分子所实施的那些令人震惊的行为，乍看之下似乎很有效。它们能吸引眼球，并吸引志同道合的支持者。然而，最终，一旦这些激进组织无法再招募极端分子，而不得不与憎恶破坏行为的大多数民众打交道时，它们就会发现发展壮大已无可能。

The change activists seek requires societal change, which can only be achieved by either being a tyrant or becoming a leader that the majority of the population wants to follow. The latter requires creating trust, and the first step toward that is to stop taking shortcuts that destroy it.

活动家们所寻求的变革需要社会变革，而社会变革只能通过两种途径实现：要么成为暴君，要么成为大多数民众愿意追随的领导者。后者需要建立信任，而建立信任的第一步就是停止走那些会破坏信任的捷径。

The tricky part is that short-term tactics work well in the short term, often even better than long-term tactics. However , growth obtained through short-term tactics eventually plateaus, creating a dead end.

棘手之处在于，短期策略在短期内往往效果显著，甚至比长期策略更有效。然而，通过短期策略实现的增长最终会停滞不前，陷入僵局。

Trying to solve a complex problem as fast as possible limits you to bad solutions, whereas adopting a longer-term view opens up better ones.

试图尽快解决复杂问题只会得到糟糕的解决方案，而采取长远的眼光则能找到更好的解决方案。

Want to fight climate change effectively? Do what some of the most serious activists already do: build trust and develop expertise, get engineering degrees and work on clean technologies, or run for office and change policies from within. It’s slower than throwing soup on paintings, but it’s much more effective.

想有效应对气候变化？那就学学那些最认真的环保人士：建立信任、积累专业知识，攻读工程学位、致力于清洁技术研发，或者竞选公职，从内部改变政策。这虽然比往画上泼汤慢，但效果却好得多。

Winning Long-Term Games

赢得长期比赛

The takeaway from both the Laffer Curve and Neotoddlerism is that maximizing short-term gains rarely works. As I like to say, “ The key to winning long-term games is to stop playing them as a series of disconnected short-term games.”

拉弗曲线和新幼儿主义都表明，追求短期利益最大化很少奏效。正如我常说的，“赢得长期博弈的关键在于停止将它们视为一系列互不关联的短期博弈。”

Winning long-term games requires building and maintaining long-term assets such as trust, relationships, and competencies, as well as a solid economy and a strong team. None of these is necessary to prosper tomorrow, but they are all necessary to prosper over the next decades. Therefore , we must remain focused on developing them.

要想赢得长期的竞争，需要建立并维护长期资产，例如信任、人际关系和能力，以及稳固的经济基础和强大的团队。这些并非明天繁荣的必要条件，但却是未来几十年繁荣发展的必要条件。因此，我们必须持续专注于发展这些资产。

This remains true even if we feel like we don’t have the bandwidth to care about the long term, because short-termism is precisely what led and will keep us there. Even more importantly, we must be wary of the policies and behaviors that undermine these long-term assets and, in particular, those that destroy trust. The following chapter discusses them. But before that, let me explain what it means to play economics and politics as an iterated game, and why doing so is so important.

即使我们感觉自己无暇顾及长远，这一点依然成立，因为正是短视主义导致我们陷入困境，并将使我们继续深陷其中。更重要的是，我们必须警惕那些破坏长期资产的政策和行为，尤其是那些摧毁信任的政策和行为。下一章将对此进行探讨。但在此之前，我想先解释一下，将经济和政治视为一场迭代博弈意味着什么，以及为什么这样做如此重要。

Economics as an iterated game

经济学是一场循环博弈

In a single “round” of the game, all that matters from the taxpayers’ point of view is to get as many services and handouts from the government as possible. From this perspective, public spending is always good, and investing in productive assets seems relatively pointless. However , over multiple rounds, how much one extracts in any single round is dwarfed by how much one can receive in the following rounds. Hence , investing in productive assets becomes the most important thing.

在游戏的单轮“博弈”中，从纳税人的角度来看，最重要的就是尽可能多地从政府那里获得服务和补贴。从这个角度来看，公共支出总是好的，而投资生产性资产似乎意义不大。然而，在多轮博弈中，单轮的收益与后续轮次的收益相比就显得微不足道了。因此，投资生产性资产就变得至关重要。

The takeaway is that voters’ time horizons are among the most important factors in determining a country’s long-term prosperity, as their voting patterns shape the time horizons of politicians and their policies.

由此可见，选民的时间观念是决定一个国家长期繁荣的最重要因素之一，因为他们的投票模式塑造了政治家的时间观念及其政策。

Once we acknowledge the importance of voters’ time horizons, we should become extremely wary of any idea, ideology, policy, or event that shortens them. The consequences may be catastrophic.

一旦我们认识到选民时间观念的重要性，就应该对任何缩短他们时间观念的理念、意识形态、政策或事件保持高度警惕。其后果可能是灾难性的。

Politics as an iterated game

政治是一场反复的游戏

I was born in Italy , a country that has had 68 governments in its 78 years as a democracy. I also hold French citizenship, and France has had 74 governments in 78 years. ( I expect these numbers to have increased by the time you read this.⁠ 3 ) My two countries are a good example of what happens when politics is treated as a short-term game: every citizen wins many battles (every few years, your party wins), yet everyone loses the war (you rarely get a competent government).

我出生在意大利，这个国家在78年的民主历史中已经换了68届政府。我也拥有法国国籍，而法国在78年的历史中也换了74届政府。（我估计在你读到这篇文章的时候，这些数字已经增加了。）我的这两个国家很好地诠释了把政治当作短期游戏会造成什么后果：每个公民都能赢得很多次战役（每隔几年，你的政党就能赢一次），但最终每个人都输掉了整场战争（你很难得到一个称职的政府）。

This is because voters, journalists, and politicians treat elections as a one-off game whose only goal is to get their party elected, with no regard for whether this is achieved in ways that decrease societal trust or government competence. Instead , we should consider elections as an iterated game, in which the goal is not to get your favorite party elected, but to ensure that, no matter who wins, they are good and competent.

这是因为选民、记者和政客将选举视为一次性的游戏，其唯一目标就是让自己的政党当选，而丝毫不顾及这种做法是否会降低社会信任或政府能力。相反，我们应该将选举视为一场循环博弈，其目标不是让自己支持的政党当选，而是确保无论谁最终获胜，他们都是优秀且称职的。

Of course, for this to happen, three things must be true. First , we must have a long-term time horizon. This is easier with a growing economy than with a declining one, where many voters struggle to make it to the end of the month. One more reason to pay attention to building a solid national economy, even if all one cares about is civil rights.

当然，要实现这一点，必须满足三个条件。首先，我们必须有长远的眼光。经济增长时期比经济衰退时期更容易做到这一点，因为在经济衰退时期，许多选民甚至难以熬过月底。这又是一个理由，让我们重视建设稳固的国民经济，即便人们只关心公民权利。

Second, we must reframe our definition of friends and foes to go beyond superficial appearances. We must acknowledge that electing a terrible person from our own side is worse than electing a good and competent person from the other side. The following chapter expands on this point.

其次，我们必须重新定义朋友和敌人，超越肤浅的外表。我们必须认识到，从己方选出一个糟糕的人，比从对方选出一个优秀且称职的人更糟糕。下一章将对此进行详细阐述。

Third, the quality of the discourse surrounding how we talk about elections and candidates should remain high. This means asking good questions, avoiding double standards, and discussing the long-term effects of policies instead of superficially focusing on short-term ones. The chapter after the next one discusses this.

第三，围绕选举和候选人的讨论质量应保持高水准。这意味着要提出好的问题，避免双重标准，并讨论政策的长期影响，而不是肤浅地关注短期效应。下一章将对此进行探讨。

1 Can we, in addition to proving their existence, determine where exactly points A and B lie on the Laffer Curve?

1 除了证明它们的存在之外，我们能否确定 A 点和 B 点在拉弗曲线上的确切位置？

Not easily. The curve’s exact shape differs across countries and can change over time, even within the same one. This is because people do not have a fixed tax rate above which they decide to evade or emigrate. Instead, they weigh that rate alongside the overall pros and cons of living in a particular country, with its specific problems and opportunities.

并非如此简单。这条曲线的具体形状因国家而异，甚至在同一国家内部也会随时间变化。这是因为人们并没有一个固定的税率阈值，超过这个阈值他们就会选择逃税或移民。相反，他们会权衡税率以及在特定国家生活的所有利弊，包括该国的具体问题和机遇。

Moreover, since points A and B depend on individual decisions, and we cannot read minds, we cannot know their exact location in advance. We can only observe how people respond to tax rate changes and infer from those reactions where we might be on the Laffer Curve.

此外，由于A点和B点取决于个人决策，而我们又无法读懂人心，因此我们无法预先知道它们的确切位置。我们只能观察人们对税率变化的反应，并根据这些反应推断我们在拉弗曲线上的位置。

2 It sometimes seems that far-left extremists look at the Laffer curve and think, "Yes, point B maximizes short-term tax revenue, but point C maximizes the dismantling of the current socio-economic system, so let’s go closer to C.”

2 有时，极左极端分子似乎看着拉弗曲线，心想：“是的，B 点可以最大限度地提高短期税收，但 C 点可以最大限度地瓦解当前的社会经济体系，所以我们应该更接近 C 点。”

3 It actually did. I’m writing this endnote on the evening before sending the final manuscript to the printer, and France is now at 76 governments in 78 years. The 77th lasted less than a month. I change Wi-Fi passwords faster than that.

3 确实如此。我是在把最终稿送去印刷的前一天晚上写下这篇尾注的，而法国在78年里已经换了76届政府。第77届政府的任期不到一个月。我换Wi-Fi密码的速度都比这快。

18

FRIENDS AND FOES

朋友与敌人

T he image below depicts my rendering of a famous diagram by Steve Conover .⁠ 1

下图是我根据史蒂夫·康诺弗的一幅著名图表绘制的示意图。

It illustrates a simple yet powerful concept: some of "our people" are, in fact, our adversaries, while some of "them" are our natural allies.

它阐明了一个简单而强大的概念：一些“我们的人”实际上是我们的敌人，而一些“他们”则是我们天然的盟友。

Note that the diagram is supposed to be qualitative and not quantitative: do not pay attention to the relative size of the depicted areas.

请注意，该图旨在定性而非定量：不要在意图中所示区域的相对大小。

Of course, the diagram is meant to be qualitative, not quantitative. So , don’t focus on the proportions of the areas; instead, pay attention to the importance of defining people not by who they are, but by what they do. This may seem banal, but it is of paramount importance. Judging bad actors by their actions rather than their identity helps us recognize them accurately and develop better solutions. Conversely , defining enemies by who they are leaves only violent and ineffective remedies (because good luck trying to destroy a whole class instead of just their bad apples: you’ll face extreme resistance and, probably, retaliation).

当然，这张图表旨在提供定性分析，而非定量分析。因此，不要过于关注各区域的比例；相反，应该关注的是，定义人应该基于他们的行为，而不是他们的身份。这或许看似老生常谈，但却至关重要。根据行为而非身份来判断不良行为者，有助于我们准确识别他们，并制定更有效的解决方案。反之，如果仅仅根据身份来定义敌人，最终只会导致暴力且无效的应对措施（因为试图消灭整个阶层而非仅仅是其中的害群之马，只会遭遇极大的阻力，甚至可能遭到报复）。

This insight also challenges our instincts about group loyalty. From an early age, we are taught to stick with our tribe, whether that’s our family, community, or nation. But what if this ingrained loyalty is actually making things worse?

这一洞见也挑战了我们对群体忠诚的本能认知。我们从小就被教导要忠于自己的群体，无论是家庭、社区还是国家。但如果这种根深蒂固的忠诚实际上让事情变得更糟呢？

Ingroup vs. Outgroup

内群体与外群体

I edited the previous diagram as shown below. By “ingroup,” I refer to any group or groups you feel you belong to. This could be people who share your nationality, ethnicity, religion, education, ideology, or other affiliations. Conversely , by “outgroup,” I mean those who are not part of your ingroup.

我修改了之前的图表，如下所示。“内群体”指的是你认为自己属于的任何群体。这可能包括与你拥有相同国籍、种族、宗教、教育背景、意识形态或其他共同特征的人。相反，“外群体”指的是那些不属于你内群体的人。

Again, the diagram is supposed to be qualitative and not quantitative: do not pay attention to the relative size of the depicted areas.

再次强调，该图旨在定性而非定量：不要关注图中所示区域的相对大小。

Before we continue, let me address some common objections.

在继续之前，我想先回应一些常见的反对意见。

  1. “The proportions are wrong.” This diagram is meant to be qualitative, not quantitative. It cannot be quantitative, because it must look correct both when looked at by you and by someone from the other side of the world, for whom you’re part of the outgroup.
    “比例不对。” 这张图旨在定性分析，而非定量分析。它不能进行定量分析，因为它必须既符合你的视角，也符合远在世界另一端、与你属于“外群体”的人的视角。
  2. “There is no universal definition of good and bad.” Sure . But whatever your definition is, you can still acknowledge that not everyone in the outgroup does bad things, and that some people in your ingroup also do.
    “善与恶没有统一的定义。”没错。但无论你如何定义，你仍然可以承认，并非所有外群体成员都会做坏事，而且你所属群体中也有些人会做坏事。
  3. “I define my outgroup as people doing bad things; so, for me, the left and right figures are equivalent.” Sure . But you must recognize that, periodically, people doing bad things will emerge from your ingroup. If you never re-classify people from your ingroup to your outgroup, you’re not truly defining your outgroup by actions.
    “我把做坏事的人定义为外群体；所以对我来说，左边和右边的人是等价的。” 当然。但你必须认识到，你的内群体中也会时不时地出现做坏事的人。如果你从不把内群体中的人重新归类为外群体，你就无法真正根据他们的行为来定义外群体。
  4. “Outgroups organize to do bad things to your ingroup.” Sure , some people in the outgroup do. But this typically occurs because their own ingroup fails to police them, and this is often a direct result of the ingroup/outgroup dynamic I’m calling out here.
    “外群体会组织起来对你的内群体做坏事。” 当然，外群体中有些人确实会这样做。但这通常是因为他们自己的内群体未能有效约束他们，而这往往是我在此提到的内群体/外群体动态的直接结果。

This last point is worth exploring. Let’s do it with a thought experiment.

最后一点值得探讨。让我们通过一个思想实验来验证。

# ↩

The Alien Refugees Camp

外来难民营

Let me tell you a story that might change how you think about groups.

让我给你讲个故事，或许会改变你对群体的看法。

Imagine you live in a small town in the countryside. One day, something extraordinary happens: a spacecraft malfunctions and crashes nearby. The aliens aren’t invaders; they’re just stranded travelers waiting for rescue. They set up a temporary camp on the edge of town.

想象一下，你住在乡间一个小镇上。有一天，一件非同寻常的事情发生了：一艘宇宙飞船发生故障，坠毁在附近。外星人并非入侵者，他们只是被困的旅行者，等待救援。他们在镇子边缘建立了一个临时营地。

These aliens look different from humans, speak differently, and have customs you don’t understand. But they seem peaceful enough. Most townspeople keep their distance, maintaining a cautious attitude, not hostile, but not welcoming either.

这些外星人外貌与人类不同，语言也不同，习俗更是你无法理解。但他们似乎相当友善。大多数镇民都与他们保持距离，态度谨慎，既不敌视，也不热情。

Then there’s Jimmy , a local troublemaker you used to go to school with.

还有吉米，他是你以前的同学，一个当地的捣蛋鬼。

One evening, Jimmy throws a few rocks at the alien camp, shouting insults. Since he causes no real damage (his aim is terrible), you and the other townspeople shrug it off. “ That’s just Jimmy being Jimmy .” No one apologizes to the aliens or condemns Jimmy’s behavior. It seems unnecessary.

一天晚上，吉米朝外星人营地扔了几块石头，还大声辱骂。由于他没造成什么实际伤害（他的准头实在太差），你和其他镇民都耸耸肩，不以为意。“吉米就是这样。”没有人向外星人道歉，也没有人谴责吉米的行为。似乎没有必要。

However, step into the aliens’ shoes for a moment.

然而，让我们暂时设身处地地站在外星人的角度思考一下。

You’re stranded on a strange planet, surrounded by creatures you barely understand. Most seem tolerable, if distant. Then , one day, one attacks your camp. More troubling than the attack itself is the response from the human community: silence. They do not condemn it nor apologize. The message is clear: either they approve, or they don’t care enough to speak up. Either way, humans can’t be trusted.

你被困在一个陌生的星球上，周围都是你几乎无法理解的生物。大多数生物看起来还算可以容忍，只是彼此疏远。然而有一天，一个生物袭击了你的营地。比袭击本身更令人不安的是人类的反应：沉默。他们既不谴责，也不道歉。这传递的信息很明确：要么他们赞同，要么他们漠不关心，不愿发声。无论如何，人类都不可信。

What happens next is predictable. The aliens grow wary. One day, one of them, feeling threatened, attacks a person. Humans respond with anger, demanding to know who did it. The aliens, now feeling even more threatened, close ranks and refuse to name the aggressor. The humans, seeing this unity as a conspiracy, grow even more hostile.

接下来发生的事情在意料之中。外星人开始提高警惕。有一天，其中一个外星人感到受到威胁，便攻击了一个人。人类愤怒地回应，要求知道是谁干的。外星人感到更加不安，于是团结起来，拒绝透露攻击者的身份。人类将这种团结视为阴谋，变得更加敌对。

And so the cycle continues.

于是，循环往复。

A Universal Pattern

普遍模式

This isn't just a thought experiment. This pattern plays out every day in every corner of our world:

这并非仅仅是一个思想实验。这种模式每天都在世界各地的每个角落上演：

  • A community refuses to condemn extremists in their midst, fearing it will give ammunition to their critics.
    一个社区拒绝谴责其内部的极端分子，担心这样做会给批评者提供攻击的弹药。
  • A political party stays silent about a corrupt politician because they do not want to lose votes.
    政党对腐败政客保持沉默，是因为他们不想失去选票。
  • A professional is unwilling to call out a colleague’s mistake because they do not want to hurt their field’s reputation.
    专业人士不愿指出同事的错误，因为他们不想损害自己领域的声誉。
  • A family covers up abuse because they do not want to bring shame to their name.
    一个家庭为了不让自己的名声蒙羞，会掩盖虐待行为。

In each case, the logic seems sound in the short term. Why give your enemies ammunition? Why risk division in your ranks? Why help the other side?

短期来看，这些逻辑似乎都成立。为什么要给敌人提供弹药？为什么要冒着内部分裂的风险？为什么要帮助对方？

However, this short-term thinking leads to long-term disasters. Every time we protect the bad actors in our group, we encourage more bad behavior, and we justify our opponents’ worst suspicions about us.

然而，这种短视的做法会导致长期的灾难。我们每包庇一次群体中的害群之马，就等于助长了更多的不良行为，也印证了对手对我们的种种猜疑。

# ↩

The Way Out

出路

The solution is not comfortable, but it is simple: we must be willing to police our in-groups. This doesn’t mean betraying our people but saving them from themselves.

解决办法并不轻松，但很简单：我们必须愿意约束内部群体。这并非背叛我们的人民，而是让他们免于自我毁灭。

Here are five considerations:

以下是五点需要考虑的因素：

  1. True loyalty means wanting what’s best for your group in the long term, not shielding its worst elements.
    真正的忠诚意味着希望你的团队从长远来看变得更好，而不是包庇其中最糟糕的部分。
  2. Condoning friends’ bad behavior doesn’t create a loyal tribe; it leaves you with a group of untrustworthy cutthroats.
    纵容朋友的不良行为并不会建立起忠诚的团队；只会让你身边围绕着一群不可信赖的恶棍。
  3. Unchecked bad behavior becomes normalized. As I like to say, problems grow to the size necessary for us to acknowledge them.
    放任不良行为不管，就会逐渐被正常化。正如我常说的，问题只有发展到一定程度，我们才会正视它们。
  4. Preventing generalizations from the outgroup requires identifying the bad apples in your own group.
    防止以偏概全需要，需要找出自己群体中的害群之马。
  5. Silence equals complicity : outsiders interpret your inaction as approval, which justifies a reaction against your group.
    沉默等于同流合污：外人会将你的不作为解读为默许，从而有理由对你的群体采取行动。

But Luca, this is so hard!

但是卢卡，这太难了！

I get it. We all have a few people we cannot criticize, whether out of loyalty or fear of consequences: our spouses, our children, our best friends, maybe even our boss. But here’s the point.

我明白。我们每个人都有一些不能批评的人，无论是出于忠诚还是害怕后果：我们的配偶、孩子、最好的朋友，甚至可能是我们的老板。但重点是……

It is precisely because we all have a few people we cannot call out that it becomes paramount to cover each other’s blind spots and call out everyone else in our ingroup: other colleagues, other community members, and so on.

正因为我们每个人都有一些不能公开批评的人，所以互相弥补彼此的盲点，并公开批评我们圈子里的其他人（其他同事、其他社区成员等等）就显得至关重要。

Some readers might label this behavior hypocritical, but hypocrisy is overrated. If only perfect people were allowed to call out others, no one would be able to call out anyone, and the result would be a world of mediocrity. A far better alternative is a mildly hypocritical world, where people can challenge bad behavior regardless of their own imperfections.

有些读者可能会认为这种行为是虚伪的，但虚伪被过分夸大了。如果只有完美的人才能指出他人的错误，那么就没有人能够指出任何人的错误，最终只会造就一个平庸的世界。一个更好的选择是营造一个略带虚伪的世界，在这个世界里，人们可以不计自身缺点地指出不良行为。

# ↩

Politics as an iterated game (part II)

政治是一场反复博弈（第二部分）

This principle becomes especially crucial in politics. Remember when, in a previous chapter, I mentioned it’s an iterated game? Well , here is why it matters.

这一原则在政治领域尤为重要。还记得我在前一章提到过，政治是一场反复博弈吗？这就是它为何如此重要的原因。

When we keep voting for “our side” despite declining standards, we think we’re choosing the lesser evil, but in reality, we’re ensuring that standards continue to fall.

当我们明知标准不断下降，却仍然继续投票支持“我们这边”时，我们以为自己是在两害相权取其轻，但实际上，我们却是在确保标准继续下降。

The solution isn’t just about voting differently; it’s about creating systems that let us send clear messages without sacrificing our core interests.

解决之道不仅仅是改变投票方式；而是要建立一套系统，让我们能够在不牺牲核心利益的前提下发出清晰的信息。

Here are some practical proposals (the first two inspired by Italian researcher Pasquale Cirillo ⁠ 2 ):

以下是一些实用建议（前两项建议的灵感来自意大利研究员帕斯夸莱·西里洛）：

  • Empty Seat System : When voter turnout is low, leave a corresponding share of Parliament seats empty. For example, if 30% of people abstain or vote blank, 30% of seats remain vacant.
    空席位制度：当投票率较低时，议会席位应相应比例空缺。例如，如果30%的人弃权或投空白票，则30%的席位空缺。
  • Negative Voting : Let citizens vote against candidates as well as for them.
    否定投票：允许公民投票反对候选人，以及支持候选人。
  • “None of the Above ” Option : If this wins, all candidates are disqualified from future elections, and a new election with new candidates must be held.
    “以上皆非”选项：如果该选项获胜，所有候选人将被取消未来选举的资格，必须举行新的选举，选出新的候选人。

Implementing one or more of these measures could help, but they should remain our last line of defense against incompetence and self-servingness. Our first line of defense must be principled citizens and journalists willing to call out inadequate politicians, even when those politicians belong to their favorite party.

实施上述一项或多项措施或许有所帮助，但它们应该始终是我们抵御无能和自私自利的最后一道防线。我们的第一道防线必须是那些有原则的公民和记者，他们愿意公开批评不称职的政客，即便这些政客属于他们支持的政党。

# ↩

The Personal Choice

个人选择

Ultimately, this isn’t about systems or politics. It’s about you. Every time you see someone from your group doing something wrong, you have a choice: stay silent or speak up.

归根结底，这与制度或政治无关，而是与你有关。每次你看到自己群体中的人做错事时，你都有选择：保持沉默还是挺身而出。

The easy choice is silence. The right choice is to speak up. Remember : at this very moment, you are both someone’s ingroup and someone’s outgroup. Your behavior and that of your fellows will influence how others treat your group. This isn’t just about morality; it’s about survival.

保持沉默是最简单的选择，而正确的选择是勇敢发声。记住：此时此刻，你既是某些人的“圈内人”，也是某些人的“圈外人”。你和同伴的行为会影响他人如何对待你的群体。这不仅仅关乎道德，更关乎生存。

Similarly, the next time you see bad behavior from “your side,” remember that your silence does not protect your group but endangers it. ⁠ 3

同样地，下次当你看到“自己人”有不良行为时，请记住，你的沉默非但不能保护你的群体，反而会危及它。

This is the paradox of true loyalty: sometimes, the most loyal thing you can do is criticize your own side.

这就是真正忠诚的悖论：有时候，最忠诚的做法就是批评自己人。

Because, in the end, the real battle isn’t between different groups. It’s between those who do right and those who do wrong, regardless of which group they belong to.

因为归根结底，真正的斗争不在于不同的群体之间，而在于行善者和作恶者之间，无论他们属于哪个群体。

Let’s not forget that many tactics are effective as one-offs but terrible as long-term solutions.

别忘了，很多策略在一次性使用时可能有效，但作为长期解决方案却很糟糕。
