THE QUALITY OF THE DISCOURSE

话语的质量

W hen we read about a new study in a scientific journal, we tend to trust it. After all, it has supposedly undergone rigorous peer review by experts in the field. Right ? Not necessarily. Consider the following excerpts from research on the peer-review process itself:

当我们在科学期刊上读到一项新研究时，往往会倾向于相信它。毕竟，它理应经过该领域专家的严格同行评审。对吗？未必如此。请看以下关于同行评审过程本身的研究摘录：

  • “Studies that replicate are cited at the same rate as studies that do not.”⁠ 1 [in psychology]
    “能够重复验证的研究与不能重复验证的研究的引用率相同。”⁠ 1 [心理学]
  • "80% of papers [on COVID ] citing retracted research were published after the retraction date.”⁠ 2
    “引用已撤稿研究的（关于新冠病毒的）论文中，80%是在撤稿日期之后发表的。”
  • “Even when they do take action, journals will often let scientists correct faked figures instead of retracting.”⁠ 3
    “即使期刊采取行动，通常也会允许科学家更正伪造的数据，而不是撤稿。”
  • “And even after being caught for outright fraud, about half of the offenders are allowed to keep working: they have received over $123 million in federal funding for their post-misconduct research efforts.”⁠ 4
    “即使被抓到犯有公然欺诈罪，大约一半的违法者仍被允许继续工作：他们已获得超过 1.23 亿美元的联邦资金，用于其不当行为后的研究工作。”

These quotes, and a few additional hilarious ones you can find in this endnote,⁠ 5 show that while peer review often works as intended, it remains far from foolproof.

这些引语，以及你可以在这篇尾注中找到的一些其他搞笑的引语， 5 表明，虽然同行评审通常能按预期发挥作用，但它仍然远非万无一失。

This can have dramatic consequences when a bad scientific study misleads researchers. One notorious example is a fraudulent Alzheimer’s study that allegedly steered research down the wrong path for 16 years, wasting hundreds of millions of dollars.⁠ 6 What’s even more jarring is that scientific journals certainly do not lack the money to conduct proper reviews. For example, publisher Elsevier posted about $2 billion in profits in 2023 (thanks to, among others, governments not demanding that studies receiving public money be published where the public can read them freely).

当一项糟糕的科学研究误导研究人员时，可能会造成严重的后果。一个臭名昭著的例子是阿尔茨海默病研究的欺诈行为，据称该研究误导研究方向长达16年，浪费了数亿美元。更令人震惊的是，科学期刊显然并不缺乏资金进行适当的评审。例如，出版商爱思唯尔（Elsevier）在2023年公布的利润约为20亿美元（这在一定程度上要归功于政府没有要求接受公共资金的研究必须发表在公众可以免费阅读的地方）。

But why am I talking about peer review in a book on economic policy? That’s because of the following principle. Science advances fastest when researchers debate ideas honestly, and it stalls, or even regresses, when trust is broken through deception, whether by outright fraud, omitting key details, or overstating results. Crucially , politics works much the same way. Honest debate builds trust and shared understanding, which in turn fosters good policies. But when discussion is tainted by lies, omissions, exaggerations, or insults, stagnation follows.

但我为什么要在一本关于经济政策的书里谈论同行评审呢？原因如下：当研究人员坦诚地辩论各种观点时，科学进步最快；而当信任被欺骗破坏时，无论是公然的欺诈、隐瞒关键细节还是夸大结果，科学都会停滞不前，甚至倒退。至关重要的是，政治的运作方式也大同小异。坦诚的辩论能够建立信任和共识，进而促进良好政策的制定。但当讨论充斥着谎言、隐瞒、夸大或侮辱时，停滞便随之而来。

The Quality of the Discourse

话语的质量

In every human exchange, from casual conversation to formal debate, an invisible force shapes the outcome: the quality of the discourse, measured not by complex vocabulary or deep subject matter but by the intellectual integrity and mutual respect shown by the participants.

在每一次人际交流中，从随意的谈话到正式的辩论，都有一种无形的力量在塑造结果：那就是话语的质量，而衡量标准不是复杂的词汇或深奥的主题，而是参与者所表现出的知识诚信和相互尊重。

At its lowest level, discourse is riddled with rhetorical tricks: deliberate lies, strategic omissions, dramatic exaggerations, and calculated misrepresentations. “ Winning ” takes precedence over understanding, and participants resort to personal insults or emotional manipulation to push their agenda. We see this in social media flame wars and in political debates where candidates speak less to persuade their opponents than to inflame their base.

在最底层，话语充斥着各种修辞技巧：蓄意的谎言、策略性的省略、戏剧性的夸张和精心策划的歪曲。“获胜”凌驾于理解之上，参与者诉诸人身攻击或情绪操控来推进自身议程。我们在社交媒体的骂战和政治辩论中都能看到这一点，候选人与其说是为了说服对手，不如说是为了煽动自己的支持者。

By contrast, high-quality discourse is marked by integrity and a genuine respect for both truth and one’s interlocutors. Those engaged in it acknowledge complexity, admit the limits of their knowledge, and treat disagreement not as a battle to win but as a chance for mutual growth.

相比之下，高质量的对话以诚信为标志，并真正尊重真理和对话者。参与对话的人承认问题的复杂性，坦诚面对自身知识的局限性，并将分歧视为共同成长的契机，而非必须取胜的斗争。

# ↩

Politics as an iterated game (Part III)

政治是一场反复博弈（第三部分）

Like any game, political discourse has short-term tactics and long-term strategies. In the immediate term, debates often resemble chess matches, where the primary goal is checkmate: in this case, winning the argument. This naturally tempts us to use rhetorical moves. But when we step back and look at the longer arc of intellectual exchange, what matters most is not winning a single debate but earning enough respect to be taken seriously in future ones.

如同任何游戏一样，政治辩论既有短期策略，也有长期战略。短期来看，辩论往往如同下棋，首要目标是将死对方：也就是赢得辩论。这自然会诱使我们运用修辞技巧。但当我们退后一步，从更长远的视角审视思想交流时，最重要的并非赢得一场辩论，而是赢得足够的尊重，从而在未来的辩论中被认真对待。

In debates with real-world consequences, such as public policy, the priority should not be winning today but achieving good policies. Sadly , history shows again and again that parties in power sometimes sacrifice the quality of the discourse to push through friendly policies, only to watch their opponents later undo those gains and enact worse ones. Such reversals are far less likely when discourse stays at a high level.

在诸如公共政策等具有现实影响的辩论中，首要任务不应是赢得眼前的胜利，而是制定出好的政策。令人遗憾的是，历史一次又一次地表明，执政党有时为了推行有利于自身的政策而牺牲辩论的质量，结果却眼睁睁地看着对手日后推翻这些成果，甚至出台更糟糕的政策。如果辩论始终保持高水平，这种情况发生的可能性就会大大降低。

Politics is an iterated game, and we should play it as such.

政治是一场反复博弈的游戏，我们应该这样看待它。

Discourse as an iterated game

话语作为一种反复的游戏

When someone resorts to dishonest rhetoric, their counterpart usually senses the manipulation and responds in kind. The discourse quickly spirals downward: both parties grow defensive, close themselves off to new perspectives, and may even slip into ad hominem attacks. Collaboration turns into competition. In such an atmosphere, constructive conversation becomes impossible. Lowering the quality of the discourse creates a vicious circle whose negative effects are greater than we expect. It is never worth it.

当有人诉诸不诚实的言辞时，对方通常会察觉到这种操纵，并以牙还牙。对话很快陷入恶性循环：双方都变得充满防御心理，封闭自己，拒绝接受新的观点，甚至可能诉诸人身攻击。合作变成了竞争。在这种氛围下，建设性的对话变得不可能。降低对话质量会形成恶性循环，其负面影响远超我们的预期。这样做得不偿失。

By contrast, successful diplomatic negotiations maintain high standards even under tension. They use verified facts, clear definitions, and careful documentation of agreements and disagreements. This high quality of the discourse makes progress possible even between adversaries.

相比之下，成功的谈判即使在紧张局势下也能保持高标准。谈判中会使用经过核实的事实、清晰的定义，并仔细记录双方的共识和分歧。这种高质量的对话使得即使是敌对双方也能取得进展。

Raising the quality of the discourse creates a virtuous cycle whose benefits exceed anything we can foresee. It is always worth it. If it seems otherwise, we are viewing the situation through too short a time horizon.

提升话语质量会形成良性循环，其益处远超我们所能预见。这样做永远值得。如果感觉并非如此，那说明我们看待问题的时间视野过于短浅。

Cultivating Higher Discourse

培养更高层次的话语

Maintaining a high quality of the discourse means acknowledging uncertainty when it exists, representing opposing views in their strongest form, admitting mistakes promptly and clearly, prioritizing accuracy over persuasiveness, and treating counterarguments as opportunities for learning rather than obstacles to overcome.

保持高质量的讨论意味着在存在不确定性时承认它，以最强有力的形式呈现对立观点，及时、清晰地承认错误，优先考虑准确性而不是说服力，并将反驳论点视为学习的机会而不是需要克服的障碍。

All of this, however, must be done in the right measure. Taken to excess, these virtues can come across as condescending or manipulative. And while we must respect both our counterpart and the truth, we should never compromise the latter to appease the former. Soothing hostility at the cost of accuracy does not earn genuine respect.

然而，这一切都必须适度。过犹不及，这些美德可能会显得居高临下或别有用心。我们固然要尊重对方和真相，但绝不能为了迎合对方而牺牲真相。以牺牲准确性为代价来平息敌意，并不能赢得真正的尊重。

The key is to cultivate higher discourse through a “via negativa” approach: rather than straining to do something good, simply refrain from doing what is bad. Do not disrespect your opponent, and do not disregard or misrepresent the truth. Often , that alone is enough.

关键在于通过“否定之道”来培养更高层次的对话：与其费尽心思去做善事，不如简单地避免做恶事。不要不尊重你的对手，也不要无视或歪曲事实。通常，仅此就足够了。

Facts Before Opinions

事实先于观点

Imagine two people debating the death penalty. One believes most death-row inmates are wrongfully convicted; the other believes such mistakes never occur. As long as they disagree about the actual rate of wrongful convictions, the conversation cannot move forward constructively. This doesn’t mean every discussion must end in agreement: differences in values may make that impossible, and that’s perfectly okay. But when people rush to argue over interpretations and opinions without first agreeing on the underlying facts, it’s a recipe for a destructive exchange: one that produces no insight and often erodes trust between those involved.

想象一下两个人正在辩论死刑。一个人认为大多数死刑犯都是冤案；另一个人则认为这种错误根本不会发生。只要他们对冤案的实际发生率存在分歧，对话就无法进行建设性的推进。这并不意味着每次讨论都必须以达成一致告终：价值观的差异可能导致无法达成一致，而这完全可以理解。但是，如果人们在没有就基本事实达成共识的情况下，就急于就各种解读和观点争论不休，那注定会引发一场破坏性的交流：这种交流不仅无法产生任何新的见解，而且往往会破坏参与者之间的信任。

The distinction between facts and opinions is essential. Productive discourse doesn’t require unanimity. Divergent views can enrich a discussion, and the best outcomes often arise from accommodating multiple perspectives. What it does require is a shared commitment to factual common ground. Without that foundation, debates quickly devolve into people talking past each other.

区分事实与观点至关重要。富有成效的讨论并不要求意见完全一致。不同的观点可以丰富讨论内容，而包容多种视角往往能带来最佳结果。真正需要的是对事实共识的共同承诺。如果没有这个基础，辩论很快就会演变成各说各话的争论。

Practical Strategies for High-Quality Discourse

高质量话语的实用策略

A simple way to foster high-quality discourse is to frame the discussion not as person A versus person B , but as person A and person B versus a common challenge, such as unfairness, poverty, ignorance, or whatever the issue may be. For example, instead of framing a debate about crime as “left vs. right,” frame it as “left and right vs. crime.” This approach establishes common ground and keeps the focus on the problem itself.

促进高质量对话的一个简单方法是，不要将讨论的焦点放在“A 对 B”上，而是放在“A 和 B 共同面对的挑战”上，例如不公平、贫困、无知或其他任何问题。例如，与其将关于犯罪的辩论定义为“左派对右派”，不如将其定义为“左派和右派共同对抗犯罪”。这种方法有助于建立共同基础，并将焦点集中在问题本身。

Next, maintain a clear distinction between factual claims and matters of judgment. This does not mean you cannot express opinions: you absolutely can, but explicitly label them as such. Few things are more frustrating than hearing someone state an opinion as fact.

其次，要明确区分事实陈述和主观判断。这并不意味着你不能表达观点：你当然可以，但要明确标明它们属于观点范畴。没有什么比听到有人把观点当作事实陈述更令人恼火的了。

It also helps to clarify the assumptions behind your opinions . If participants disagree on an assumption, the discussion can refocus on that point. Returning to the death penalty example, identifying early disagreements about the rate of wrongful convictions allows the debate to move from policy opinions to factual discussion. Participants may even find they both support the death penalty for certain rates of wrongful conviction and oppose it under others.

澄清观点背后的假设也很有帮助。如果参与者对某个假设存在分歧，讨论就可以重新聚焦于这一点。以死刑为例，尽早明确关于冤案率的分歧，可以让辩论从政策意见转向事实探讨。参与者甚至可能会发现，他们在某些冤案率的情况下支持死刑，而在另一些情况下则反对。

Focus on your strongest, best-supported argument rather than diluting the conversation with weaker points that can erode trust. For instance, if asked for your best argument in favor of your preferred presidential candidate, you likely have a solid case. Asking for ten arguments, however, will produce weaker, more subjective points that may antagonize the audience. Keeping the discussion on the strongest argument is far more productive.

与其用一些薄弱的论点分散讨论，以免损害信任，不如专注于你最有力、最有说服力的论点。例如，如果你被问及支持你心仪的总统候选人的最佳论点，你很可能已经准备好了。但如果要求你列举十个论点，就会产生一些较弱、更主观的观点，这可能会激怒听众。将讨论集中在最有力的论点上，效率会更高。

Finally, correct mistakes swiftly and proactively. People will forgive you and trust you more for addressing them. Correct mistakes made by your allies as well; failing to do so undermines credibility for your entire side.

最后，要迅速主动地纠正错误。人们会因为你主动处理错误而原谅你，也会更加信任你。同时也要纠正盟友的错误；否则，会损害你们整个阵营的信誉。

These strategies should not be treated as a rigid checklist but as guiding principles: work together against a shared challenge, separate facts from opinions, and maintain credibility.

这些策略不应被视为僵化的清单，而应被视为指导原则：共同应对共同挑战，区分事实与观点，并保持信誉。

The Importance of the Track Record

过往业绩的重要性

A common scene in politics unfolds like this: the government proposes raising taxes on a specific group (say, farmers) who, in turn, oppose them. Part of their resistance is self-interest: who wants to pay more taxes? But even if farmers were perfect altruists, they might still resist based on the government’s track record of wasting tax revenue.

政治中经常会出现这样的场景：政府提议对特定群体（比如农民）增税，而这些群体则反对增税。他们反对的部分原因是出于自身利益：谁愿意多缴税呢？但即便农民都是完全的利他主义者，他们也可能因为政府以往浪费税收的记录而抵制增税。

This illustrates a key principle: without a credible track record, even the best ideas, presented flawlessly, will not be taken seriously.

这说明了一个关键原则：如果没有可信的过往业绩，即使是最好的想法，即使表达得完美无瑕，也不会被认真对待。

The solution is to build a track record: not just of good ideas, but of effective use of people’s time and resources.

解决办法是建立良好的业绩记录：不仅要有好的想法，还要有有效利用人们的时间和资源的记录。

Hence, my suggestion to politicians and activists alike is to start small: propose modest changes and ensure they deliver positive results. Success in these smaller efforts makes people more likely to support larger initiatives later.

因此，我对政治家和活动家的建议是：从小处着手，提出一些适度的改革方案，并确保这些方案能够带来积极的成果。这些小规模努力的成功会让人们更有可能在日后支持更大规模的举措。

This holds even when the issue at hand feels urgent. For example, no matter how pressing climate action may seem, rushing ahead without building trust is likely to end in a dead end after some initial progress. Sometimes , the fastest way to reach a destination is to avoid rushing.

即使当前问题看似紧迫，这条原则依然适用。例如，无论气候行动看起来多么紧迫，如果不建立信任就仓促推进，很可能在取得一些初步进展后就陷入僵局。有时候，到达目的地最快的方法就是避免仓促行事。

If anything, the possibility of having to confront an urgent problem in the future is yet another reason to start building a track record of trustworthiness today. Precisely because this takes time, we should prepare now to be ready when a crisis strikes.

如果说有什么理由促使我们今天就开始建立信誉，那就是考虑到未来可能面临紧急问题。正因为这需要时间，我们才更应该现在就开始准备，以便在危机来临时能够迅速应对。

Semmelweis’ Horror Story

塞麦尔维斯的恐怖故事

In 1847, Ignaz Semmelweis , a Hungarian physician, demonstrated that doctors’ failure to wash their hands caused the high mortality in Vienna’s maternity wards. He not only proposed the idea but also collected data to prove it, cutting his hospital’s maternal death rate from 18% to less than 2%. Yet , other doctors rejected his findings, and instead of acknowledging his discovery, had him committed to an asylum, where he died. Handwashing took decades to be accepted.⁠ 7

1847年，匈牙利医生伊格纳兹·塞麦尔维斯证明，维也纳产科病房的高死亡率是由于医生不洗手造成的。他不仅提出了这一观点，还收集了数据来证明，并将他所在医院的孕产妇死亡率从18%降低到2%以下。然而，其他医生拒绝接受他的发现，非但没有承认他的贡献，反而将他送进了精神病院，最终他在那里去世。洗手的习惯花了数十年才被人们接受。

But have doctors truly learned the lesson?

但医生们真的吸取了教训吗？

It depends on what we consider the lesson to be. If it is simply that washing hands is important, then yes, they have learned it. But if the lesson is that peer culture and the status quo can blind even knowledgeable professionals to obvious truths, then no. Crowded hospital waiting rooms illustrate this perfectly: the idea of cramming the sick and vulnerable together indoors has somehow survived unscathed a century and a half of germ theory.

这取决于我们如何看待这个教训。如果仅仅是洗手的重要性，那么是的，他们已经吸取了教训。但如果教训是同伴文化和现状会蒙蔽即使是知识渊博的专业人士，让他们看不到显而易见的真理，那么答案是否定的。拥挤的医院候诊室完美地诠释了这一点：将病人和弱势群体集中安置在室内的做法，在一个半世纪的细菌理论发展中竟然毫发无损地保留了下来。

The problem is not a lack of knowledge (germ theory is well-known and well-accepted) nor a lack of technology (we know how to stagger appointments and triage patients so that the sick and the vulnerable do not have to spend too much time in waiting rooms). The problem is a lack of high-quality discourse that digs deep beyond superficial aspects.

问题不在于缺乏知识（细菌理论广为人知且被广泛接受），也不在于缺乏技术（我们知道如何错开预约时间并对病人进行分诊，从而避免病人和弱势群体在候诊室停留过久）。问题在于缺乏高质量的深入探讨，而这种探讨往往停留在表面现象。

A poor quality of the discourse bottlenecks societal progress.

低质量的话语会阻碍社会进步。

The Role of the Experts

专家的作用

Beyond individual conversations, the quality of the discourse has profound implications for society’s ability to tackle complex challenges. Without high-quality discourse, policy ideas are riddled with blind spots and lack the consensus needed to be truly effective.

除了个人对话之外，讨论的质量对社会应对复杂挑战的能力有着深远的影响。缺乏高质量的讨论，政策构想就会充满盲点，并且缺乏真正有效所需的共识。

This commitment is especially critical when it comes to experts, politicians, and journalists. Experts must clearly separate factual claims from personal judgments, making falsifiable statements that allow ideas to be tested and refined. Politicians should explicitly state the assumptions behind their policy proposals, enabling faster error correction and more productive debate over both means and ends. Journalists must prioritize accuracy over sensationalism, uphold high standards of evidence, and resist oversimplifying complex issues merely to attract attention.

对于专家、政治家和记者而言，这种承诺尤为重要。专家必须清晰地区分事实主张和个人判断，提出可证伪的陈述，以便检验和完善观点。政治家应明确阐述其政策提案背后的假设，从而加快纠正错误，并就政策手段和目标展开更富有成效的辩论。记者必须优先考虑准确性而非耸人听闻，坚持高标准的证据要求，并避免为了博取眼球而过度简化复杂问题。

Moreover, a core function of the education system and journalism should be to reduce the share of political disagreement driven by inaccurate factual beliefs about the state of the world (as opposed to disagreement driven by different preferences).

此外，教育系统和新闻业的核心功能应该是减少因对世界状况的错误事实信念而导致的政治分歧（而不是因偏好不同而导致的分歧）。

By demanding high-quality discourse from these influential voices, we can gradually elevate public conversation. This creates a virtuous cycle: better discourse leads to better decisions, which in turn demonstrates the value of maintaining high standards in debate.

通过要求这些有影响力的人士发表高质量的言论，我们可以逐步提升公共对话的水平。这会形成一个良性循环：更高质量的对话带来更明智的决策，而这反过来又体现了在辩论中保持高标准的重要性。

Ultimately, so much of our prosperity depends on good policies, and good policies depend heavily on the quality of the discourse that produces them. Only by upholding high standards in how we engage with others can we create the conditions necessary for sustained progress.

归根结底，我们的繁荣很大程度上取决于良好的政策，而良好的政策又高度依赖于产生这些政策的讨论的质量。只有坚持高标准的与他人互动方式，我们才能创造持续进步所需的条件。

After all, passing a policy that gets reversed in the next election cycle, as soon as opponents take power, serves no one’s interests. The better question is how to pass policies that endure, and the only answer (short of authoritarian measures) is to take the time to debate them thoroughly, write them clearly enough to seem reasonable to most voters, and implement them competently so they do not become a source of frustration for half of the electorate.

毕竟，如果一项政策在下一次选举周期中，一旦反对派掌权就被推翻，那么通过这项政策对任何人都没有好处。更重要的问题是如何制定能够长期有效的政策，而唯一的答案（除了采取专制措施之外）就是花时间进行充分的辩论，将政策表述得足够清晰，使大多数选民觉得合理，并妥善地执行，以免让一半选民感到失望。

Performative vs Genuine Quality of the Discourse

话语的表演性与真实性

If a high quality of discourse is so important, why do some places with supposedly high-quality discourse still produce poor outcomes?

如果高质量的讨论如此重要，为什么有些地方的讨论质量明明很高，却仍然产生糟糕的结果？

Often, these places have a performative idea of what high-quality discourse means. They may focus so much on politeness that they avoid calling out mistakes, or do so so indirectly that it becomes ineffective. They might dwell on marginal issues while sidestepping the most important ones, or they may gatekeep who is allowed to participate. In all these cases, the focus is on form rather than substance.

这些场所往往对高质量对话的定义存在一种形式主义的观念。它们可能过于注重礼貌，以至于避免指出错误，或者指出错误的方式过于隐晦，以至于无效。它们可能纠缠于无关紧要的问题，而回避最重要的问题，或者设置准入门槛，限制参与者的权限。在所有这些情况下，它们关注的是形式而非实质。

As we work to improve the quality of the discourse, we must avoid these mistakes.

在努力提高讨论质量的过程中，我们必须避免这些错误。

Always keep an eye on the substance.

时刻注意物质的变化。

THE DEPOLARIZATION MANIFESTO

去极化宣言

You don’t win at politics when your party gets elected.

在政治上，政党当选并不意味着你就赢了。

You win when your party loses, and the government is still good.

即使你的政党输了，你也是赢家，但政府依然良好。

I am writing this chapter in April 2025. The US President is Donald Trump , and the American Left wonders how half of their fellow citizens could have voted for someone like him.

我写这一章是在2025年4月。美国总统是唐纳德·特朗普，美国左派人士不禁纳闷，为什么有一半的美国同胞会投票给像他这样的人。

The answer is polarization. The American Right became so polarized by some policies of the previous administration that they voted for a flawed candidate. The more polarized a population becomes, the more it sees elections as life-or-death situations and seeks to win at any cost, even tolerating behavior from leaders that would normally be unacceptable.

答案是极化。美国右翼因前任政府的一些政策而极度分裂，以至于他们投票支持了一位有缺陷的候选人。一个群体越是极化，就越会将选举视为生死攸关的大事，并试图不惜一切代价赢得胜利，甚至容忍领导人一些通常不可接受的行为。

Polarization is always mutual. ⁠ 1

极化总是相互的。

When one half of the electorate becomes polarized, it runs polarizing candidates, who then polarize the other half, making them more likely to run polarizing candidates as well. This creates a vicious circle where everyone loses.

当一半选民的立场变得两极分化时，他们就会推出立场两极分化的候选人，而这些候选人又会使另一半选民的立场也变得两极分化，从而使后者更有可能推出立场两极分化的候选人。这就形成了一个恶性循环，最终所有人都是输家。

Hence, the importance of depolarization.

因此，去极化非常重要。

# ↩

THE DEPOLARIZATION MANIFESTO

去极化宣言

I

我

In the democratic version of Orwell’s Animal Farm , the pigs stay in control by making elections a choice between two pigs in different-colored shirts. They mislead the other animals into aiming for the wrong goal: electing their preferred party instead of stopping pigs from being elected at all. The greatest threat to democracy is not dictators (they are only a symptom) but voters losing sight of what truly matters.

在奥威尔《动物庄园》的民主版本中，猪通过将选举变成在两只穿着不同颜色衬衫的猪之间做出选择来维持统治。它们误导其他动物追求错误的目标：选举自己支持的政党，而不是阻止猪当选。对民主最大的威胁不是独裁者（他们只是表象），而是选民们失去了对真正重要的东西的认识。

II

二

Voters lose focus when they see winning the next election as more important than electing a competent government. This happens when a particular issue is viewed as life-or-death, lowering their standards for what they expect from representatives, including their own. In their urgency to ensure their party wins, they tolerate incompetence and corruption, overlook mistakes, support flawed policies, and abandon the fight for truth and competence.

当选民认为赢得下次选举比选出一个称职的政府更重要时，他们就会失去关注点。这种情况发生在某个特定议题被视为生死攸关之事时，从而降低了他们对代表（包括他们自己的代表）的期望标准。为了确保本党获胜，他们急于容忍无能和腐败，对错误视而不见，支持有缺陷的政策，并放弃了对真相和能力的追求。

If this happened only once, the damage might be limited. But when every election is framed as life-or-death and voters keep accepting worse behavior, the quality of government quickly deteriorates.

如果这种情况只发生一次，损害或许有限。但如果每次选举都被渲染成生死攸关的大事，而选民又不断容忍更糟糕的行为，那么政府的质量就会迅速下降。

III

三

Declining government quality not only makes citizens poorer and worsens services, but also pushes dissatisfied voters to switch sides, even when the opposition is weak. Lowering standards to win the next election may succeed temporarily, but it ultimately leads to losing future ones, letting incompetent and polarized opponents take power with disastrous results.

政府素质下降不仅会加剧民众贫困、降低公共服务质量，还会迫使不满的选民倒戈，即便反对派实力较弱。降低标准以赢得下次选举或许能暂时奏效，但最终会导致未来选举的失败，让无能且政治立场两极分化的反对派掌权，从而酿成灾难性后果。

This is why it is never worth lowering standards for your party’s candidates, even when stopping the opposition feels like a matter of life or death.

这就是为什么即使阻止反对派感觉像是生死攸关的大事，也永远不值得降低本党候选人的标准。

RATIONALE

理由

I

我

Polarization is not just political disagreement or heated debate. It is the belief that the opposing group is so dangerous that it justifies unethical behavior against them: insults, lies, cheating, suspending due process, collective punishment, and more.

极化不仅仅是政治分歧或激烈辩论，它更是一种信念，即对立群体极其危险，因此可以对其采取不道德的行为：侮辱、谎言、欺骗、中止正当程序、集体惩罚等等。

II

二

Polarization is fear-driven but not irrational. Its logic is that the other group is so dangerous that extreme measures are justified to curb its influence and power.

两极分化是由恐惧驱动的，但并非非理性的。其逻辑在于，对方群体如此危险，以至于采取极端措施来遏制其影响力和权力是正当的。

Yet, adopting extreme measures makes one’s own group seem unreasonable and dangerous, which in turn justifies extreme measures from the opposition.

然而，采取极端措施会使自己的团体显得不讲道理且危险，这反过来又会为反对派采取极端措施提供正当理由。

Thus, polarization is always mutual.

因此，极化总是相互的。

III

三

If polarization weren’t mutual, it could be an effective tool for advancing political goals. But precisely because polarized behavior from one group triggers similar responses from others, it erodes societal trust and weakens institutions. Governing becomes harder even if one wins elections, and society suffers even when favored policies pass.

如果两极分化不是双向的，它或许可以成为推进政治目标的有效工具。但正因为一方的两极分化行为会引发其他群体的类似反应，它才会侵蚀社会信任，削弱制度。即便赢得选举，治理也会变得更加艰难；即便推行了受欢迎的政策，社会依然会遭受损失。

For instance, seeing environmental neglect as a life-or-death risk may make extreme tactics seem reasonable. Yet if these tactics alienate most people, gaining the broad support needed to solve the largest environmental challenges becomes increasingly difficult, if not impossible.

例如，将环境忽视视为生死攸关的风险，可能会使一些极端策略显得合理。然而，如果这些策略疏远了大多数人，那么要获得解决最严峻环境挑战所需的广泛支持就变得越来越困难，甚至不可能。

It is therefore essential never to let virtuous ends justify polarized means. It won’t have mattered achieving an objective if a polarized population sabotages it shortly thereafter.

因此，绝不能以崇高的目标为借口，采取极端手段。如果分裂的民众很快破坏了目标，那么即使实现了目标也毫无意义。

IV

第四

Over a short time horizon, using polarizing tactics may seem sensible; however, over a long time horizon, it never is.

从短期来看，使用两极分化的策略似乎是明智的；然而，从长远来看，这绝不是明智之举。

For example, censoring a would-be dictator might help block their rise to power, but it also risks normalizing censorship, making it easier for another would-be dictator to emerge later. ( A better option is to arrest the wannabe dictator as soon as they break a law, which they will inevitably do.)

例如，审查潜在独裁者的言论或许有助于阻止其掌权，但也可能导致审查制度常态化，使其他潜在独裁者更容易在日后出现。（更好的做法是，一旦潜在独裁者违法，就立即将其逮捕，而他们必然会违法。）

So while polarizing tactics can bring good short-term results, their long-term effect is almost always negative.

因此，虽然两极分化的策略可以带来良好的短期效果，但其长期影响几乎总是负面的。

ESCALATION

升级

I

我

Polarization begins when someone expresses a belief seen as dangerous by the outgroup, and their own group fails to distance itself from them.

当一个人表达出被外群体视为危险的观点，而他自己的群体却未能与这种观点划清界限时，两极分化就开始了。

For example, if someone makes a racist comment and their community does not call them out, the silence makes the entire group appear complicit.

例如，如果有人发表了种族歧视言论，而他们的社区没有谴责他们，这种沉默会让整个群体看起来像是同谋。

A group that’s unable to police its worst members is seen as dangerous by the outgroup.

一个无法约束其最恶劣成员的群体，会被外部群体视为危险的。

II

二

The perceived danger of a group comes from two factors:

人们对某个群体的危险感知来源于两个因素：

  1. It harbors some unethical individuals, and
    它庇护了一些不道德的人，而且
  2. It seems unwilling or unable to hold them accountable.
    它似乎不愿或无力追究他们的责任。

A third factor often worsens this perception: when the group openly celebrates its unity, including unity with the unethical people within.

第三个因素往往会加剧这种看法：当一个团体公开庆祝其团结时，包括与内部不道德的人团结在一起。

III

三

There are several reasons the ingroup may be unwilling to police its members who do or say unethical things:

群体内部成员不愿约束其不道德的行为或言论的原因有很多：

  1. They find justifications such as “he didn’t mean that,” “he was just joking,” or “he wasn’t thinking.”
    他们会找各种理由来辩解，比如“他不是那个意思”、“他只是开玩笑”、“他当时没想那么多”。
  2. They see the person as “that weird guy” and assume others will not take that person seriously or understand they do not represent the group.
    他们认为这个人是“那个怪人”，并认为其他人不会认真对待这个人，也不会理解这个人并不能代表群体。
  3. They justify his actions as a “tit for tat.”
    他们为他的行为辩解说这是“以牙还牙”。
  4. They are so polarized that they view the situation as life-or-death, making it paramount to stay united and show no vulnerability to opponents.
    他们之间的分歧如此之大，以至于他们将局势视为生死攸关的大事，因此保持团结、不向对手示弱至关重要。

Whether these behaviors are justified is irrelevant.

这些行为是否合理并不重要。

What matters is that they provoke similar actions from the other group.

重要的是，他们能够激起对方采取类似的行动。

IV

第四

And yet, the very people who believe points (1), (2), or (3) above often fail to extend the same benefit of the doubt to the outgroup.

然而，那些相信上述第（1）、（2）或（3）点的人，往往不会对群体外的人给予同样的信任。

When someone from the outgroup says something polarizing, they take it at face value.

当外群体成员发表一些具有争议性的言论时，他们会信以为真。

When “that weird guy” from the other group says something dangerous, they present it as if it comes from a respected representative speaking for the entire group.

当对方团体的“那个怪人”说出一些危险的话时，他们会把它说成是某个受人尊敬的代表代表整个团体说的。

V

V

These behaviors intensify polarization, making all groups more likely to engage in further polarizing actions and polarizing rhetoric.

这些行为加剧了极化，使所有群体更有可能参与进一步的极化行动和极化言论。

A race to the bottom where even the winners lose.

一场竞相压低价格的竞赛，最终连赢家也输了。

TEMPTATIONS

诱惑

I

我

Because polarization is always mutual, it cannot be resolved through polarizing actions. For example, censoring a political opponent only deepens polarization, as some will see the censorship as unjustified and view the censors themselves as the real threat.

因为极化总是相互的，所以无法通过加剧极化的行为来解决。例如，审查政治对手只会加深极化，因为有些人会认为这种审查毫无道理，并将审查者本身视为真正的威胁。

II

二

It is paramount to resist the temptation to think, “ The other side exaggerates and misrepresents, so we are justified to do the same.” As the saying goes, an eye for an eye makes the whole world blind.

必须抵制住“对方夸大其词、歪曲事实，所以我们也有理由这样做”这种想法的诱惑。正如俗语所说，以眼还眼只会让世界变得盲目。

III

三

It is paramount to resist the temptation to call for censorship. Not only is focusing on what people say rarely the best approach to address hate speech (as I will argue in a later chapter, enforcing existing laws against criminal actions would put most hateful individuals behind bars anyway, with far less collateral damage to free speech) , but censorship itself is polarizing and invites retaliatory censorship.

抵制呼吁审查的诱惑至关重要。关注人们说了什么很少是应对仇恨言论的最佳方法（正如我将在后面的章节中论述的，执行现有的打击犯罪行为的法律无论如何都会将大多数仇恨者绳之以法，而且对言论自由的附带损害要小得多），而且审查本身会加剧两极分化，并招致报复性审查。

IV

第四

It is paramount to resist the temptation to say, “ The other side is so dangerous, we must stop them at all costs.” Is the entire opposing side truly dangerous, or only certain members? And if only some are dangerous, is exaggeration really the most effective way to get their side to distance themselves from them?

至关重要的是要抵制住“对方非常危险，我们必须不惜一切代价阻止他们”这种想法的诱惑。整个对方阵营真的危险吗？还是只有部分成员危险？如果只有部分成员危险，夸大其词真的是让对方与他们划清界限的最有效方法吗？

Accurately representing the dangers posed by specific individuals often makes a more compelling argument and can gain broader support than exaggeration ever could. Especially over the long term.

准确地描述特定个人构成的危险，往往比夸大其词更有说服力，也更容易获得更广泛的支持，尤其是在长期来看。

V

V

It is paramount to resist the temptation to think, “ If we do not exaggerate and misrepresent, we will lose the elections.”

最重要的是要抵制住“如果我们不夸大其词、歪曲事实，就会输掉选举”这种想法的诱惑。

However, resorting to exaggeration and misrepresentation will get pigs elected, no matter the color of their shirt.

然而，无论穿什么颜色的衣服，靠夸大其词和歪曲事实就能让猪当选。

Electing a pig makes you miserable even when they share your party colors, and it increases the likelihood of losing future elections as dissatisfied voters switch sides.

即使对方是你的党派成员，选出一个猪也会让你痛苦不堪，而且由于不满的选民会倒戈，还会增加未来选举失败的可能性。

DEPOLARIZATION

去极化

I

我

The first step in reducing polarization is to recognize that your political opponents include two distinct groups, reasonable individuals and unreasonable ones, and to avoid conflating the two.

减少政治极化的第一步是认识到你的政治对手包括两个截然不同的群体：理性的人和非理性的人，并避免将两者混为一谈。

Limit unnecessary engagement with the unreasonable, especially on social media, since interacting with them can tempt you to act or speak in polarizing ways.

尽量避免与不讲道理的人进行不必要的接触，尤其是在社交媒体上，因为与他们互动可能会诱使你以极端的方式行事或说话。

And when you do engage with the unreasonable, treat them as individuals and never imply that their community as a whole is unreasonable.

当你遇到不讲道理的人时，要把他们当作个体来对待，千万不要暗示他们的整个群体是不讲道理的。

II

二

The second step to reduce polarization is to always address specific individuals when criticizing the opposing group, and never misrepresent or exaggerate their actions.

减少两极分化的第二步是在批评对立群体时，始终要针对具体个人，并且永远不要歪曲或夸大他们的行为。

Any generalization will inevitably be seen as polarizing.

任何概括性的结论都必然会引发争议。

III

三

The third step to reduce polarization is to address the reasonable members of the opposing group when proposing policies, actively listening to their concerns, and responding without dismissing them. This not only decreases polarization but also helps craft better and more widely acceptable policies that are more likely to be implemented and sustained.

减少极化的第三步是在提出政策时，要重视反对派中理性成员的意见，积极倾听他们的担忧，并予以回应，而不是置之不理。这不仅能降低极化程度，还有助于制定更好、更易被广泛接受的政策，从而提高政策的实施和持续性。

This contrasts with the common approach of addressing only one’s ingroup, who already support the policy and need no further convincing, while antagonizing the opposing group, whose support we need for the policy to be implemented and to survive the next election cycle.

这与常见的做法形成鲜明对比，即只针对已经支持该政策且无需进一步说服的群体，同时激怒反对群体，而我们需要他们的支持才能实施该政策并度过下一个选举周期。

IV

第四

The fourth step to reduce polarization is to focus on the strongest argument for or against a policy rather than exploring the second-strongest, third-strongest, and weaker points.

减少两极分化的第四步是集中精力关注支持或反对某项政策的最有力论点，而不是去探究第二有力、第三有力以及较弱的论点。

The further down the list of arguments you go, the weaker they become, and the more public discussion fixates on divisive details.

论点越往下看，就越显得薄弱，公众讨论也越发集中在容易引起分歧的细节上。

V

V

The fifth step to reduce polarization is to consistently call out unreasonable behavior within your own side. Failing to do so encourages more such behavior and signals tacit approval to the opposing group. Nothing feels more threatening than an unreasonable individual gaining widespread support.

减少两极分化的第五步是持续指出己方阵营内部的不合理行为。否则，就会助长此类行为，并向对立阵营发出默许的信号。没有什么比一个不理智的人获得广泛支持更具威胁性了。

VI

六年级

The sixth step to reduce polarization is to consistently call out exaggerations and misrepresentations from both sides, especially from your own. Failing to challenge your unreasonable allies makes your whole group appear dangerous.

减少两极分化的第六步是持续指出双方的夸大其词和歪曲事实，尤其是来自己方的此类言论。如果不对不讲道理的盟友提出质疑，会让整个群体显得危险。

VII

第七章

The seventh and final step to reduce polarization is to constantly emphasize that it is always mutual. That terrible president? They rose to power because of mutual polarization. That lack of trust in institutions? It happened because of mutual polarization.

减少极化现象的第七个也是最后一个步骤，是不断强调极化始终是相互的。那个糟糕的总统？他/她正是因为相互极化才上台的。人们对机构缺乏信任？也是因为相互极化才造成的。

Even when one side bears more responsibility, polarization must be treated as a shared problem.

即使一方负有更多责任，两极分化也必须被视为共同问题。

Failing to do so is itself polarizing and can lead the less culpable group to justify unethical behavior.

不这样做本身就会造成两极分化，并可能导致责任较轻的一方为不道德行为辩护。

The more the term “mutual polarization” enters public discourse, the more people will understand what is happening and the more they will avoid solutions that are themselves polarizing.

“相互极化”一词越是进入公共话语，人们就越能理解正在发生的事情，也就越会避免那些本身就具有极化效应的解决方案。

HYPOCRISY

虚伪

I

我

Reducing polarization to zero is clearly impossible, but that does not mean it cannot be significantly reduced.

将极化降低到零显然是不可能的，但这并不意味着不能显著降低极化程度。

II

二

Even the most dedicated followers of this manifesto will occasionally say or do something polarizing. Critics will inevitably point it out: “ You ask us not to polarize, but you do it yourself. You’re a hypocrite.”

即使是这份宣言最忠实的追随者，偶尔也会发表或做出一些引发争议的言论或行为。批评者必然会指出这一点：“你要求我们不要制造争议，但你自己却在这样做。你真是个伪君子。”

But hypocrisy is overrated. If only the perfect could call out others, no one would, and the world would quickly descend into mediocrity, chaos, and impunity.

但虚伪被过分夸大了。如果只有完美的人才能指出他人的错误，那就没有人会这么做了，世界很快就会陷入平庸、混乱和有罪不罚的境地。

The only path to mutual improvement is to allow the imperfect to call out others.

实现共同进步的唯一途径是允许不完美的人指出他人的不足。

III

三

Polarization is a coordination problem. When we encounter something polarizing, we feel compelled to respond in kind. But if everyone simultaneously stopped engaging in polarizing behavior, that compulsion would vanish.

极化是一种协调问题。当我们遇到引发极化的事情时，我们会感到不得不以同样的方式回应。但如果每个人都同时停止参与引发极化的行为，这种冲动就会消失。

Committing to this goal even when others are out of sync is the only way to start coordination.

即使其他人步调不一致，也要坚持这个目标，这是开始协调的唯一途径。

您可以在以下网址找到这份宣言的可分享PDF版本：

Luca- Dellanna.com / posts/ depolarization

Luca-Dellanna.com/ posts/ depolarization

1 By “polarization is always mutual,” I do not mean it is symmetric. I mean that polarization on one side fuels polarization on the other.

1. 我所说的“极化总是相互的”，并不是指它是对称的。我的意思是，一方的极化会加剧另一方的极化。

When side A’s polarization provokes polarization in side B, which then reinforces polarization in A, a vicious cycle emerges.

当 A 方的极化引发 B 方的极化，而 B 方的极化又反过来加强 A 方的极化时，就会形成恶性循环。

As with all vicious cycles, even if it is technically possible to identify who started it, or to determine that one side is more responsible than the other, such analysis is rarely useful and may even worsen the problem: the side deemed less responsible might take this as justification for treating the other side more harshly, which only deepens polarization.

与所有恶性循环一样，即使从技术上讲有可能确定是谁挑起了这个循环，或者确定一方比另一方负有更大的责任，这种分析也很少有用，甚至可能会使问题恶化：被认为责任较小的一方可能会以此为由，对另一方采取更严厉的措施，这只会加深两极分化。

The only way out is to stop asking who is to blame and start focusing on how to end mutual polarization.

唯一的出路是停止追究谁的责任，开始关注如何结束相互对立。

21

AN OUTSIDE PERSPECTIVE

局外人的视角

F rom a citizen’s perspective, politics may look like a zero-sum game: party A vs. party B . For a supporter of party A , what matters is the difference in strength between the two parties: ( A – B ). But from the outside, this view is absurd. What matters is not ( A – B ); it’s ( A + B ): how strong and functional a country is, regardless of the color of the president’s tie.

从普通民众的角度来看，政治似乎是一场零和博弈：A党对B党。对于A党的支持者来说，重要的是两党实力的差距：(A - B)。但从旁观者的角度来看，这种观点是荒谬的。重要的不是(A - B)，而是(A + B)：一个国家的实力和运转状况，与总统的领带颜色无关。

As an Italian , for instance, when I hear that Americans have elected a widely criticized president, I do not think, “ What were Republicans thinking?” or “ What were Democrats thinking?” Instead , I wonder, “ What were Americans thinking?” ( Of course, I expect Americans to think the same about Italians and our own questionable leaders.)

例如，作为一个意大利人，当我听说美国人选出了一位备受争议的总统时，我不会想“共和党人当时是怎么想的？”或者“民主党人当时是怎么想的？”相反，我会想“美国人当时是怎么想的？”（当然，我也预料美国人对意大利人和我们自己那些有争议的领导人也会有同样的看法。）

This is not about blaming anyone; the point is precisely to move beyond blame. Whether or not blame is deserved, it is rarely constructive. A better approach is to take an outside perspective and ask, “ What could have led our country as a whole to elect such an inept president?” This question reveals deeper causes than “the other party is stupid.” For example, it might show that extreme polarization led both parties to run inept candidates. Or it might show that a poor quality of the discourse left most voters making decisions with only partial information.

这并非要指责任何人；关键恰恰在于超越指责。无论是否应该指责，指责都鲜有建设性意义。更好的方法是从局外人的视角出发，提出这样的问题：“究竟是什么原因导致我们国家整体选出了这样一位无能的总统？”这个问题揭示了比“对方政党愚蠢”更深层次的原因。例如，它可能表明，极端的两极分化导致两党都推出了不称职的候选人。或者，它可能表明，糟糕的舆论环境使得大多数选民只能在信息不全的情况下做出决定。

The foreign adversary perspective

外国敌对势力的视角

One of the most powerful rules of thumb for good policymaking is:

制定良好政策最有效的经验法则之一是：

“Never pass a policy that our foreign adversaries would applaud.”

“永远不要通过任何会让外国敌对势力鼓掌的政策。”

Examples of such policies include:

此类政策的例子包括：

  • Policies that weaken our economy, such as price and rent controls, excessive taxes, and heavy bureaucracy.
    削弱我国经济的政策，例如价格和租金管制、过高的税收和臃肿的官僚机构。
  • Policies that cause malinvestment, such as poorly designed subsidies, incentives, and job market distortions.
    导致投资不当的政策，例如设计不合理的补贴、激励措施和就业市场扭曲。
  • Policies that increase polarization or erode legitimacy, such as lax law enforcement, diversity measures that go beyond gender- and race-blindness, and mail-in voting (some of these policies are discussed in Part III of this book) .
    一些政策会加剧两极分化或削弱合法性，例如执法不严、不考虑性别和种族的多元化措施以及邮寄投票（本书第三部分将讨论其中一些政策）。

I could list more, but the point is that “never pass a policy our foreign adversaries would applaud” is an effective rule of thumb for spotting harmful proposals, especially those with good intentions but bad effects. As Charlie Munger would say, “ Invert , always invert.”

我还可以列举更多，但重点是，“永远不要通过任何会让外国敌对势力欢呼的政策”是识别有害提案的有效经验法则，尤其适用于那些出发点良好但后果严重的提案。正如查理·芒格所说，“反其道而行之，永远要反其道而行之。”

Moreover, this rule of thumb can help us design better laws. Take immigration: the question is not whether to allow it at all, but to what extent and how to choose who can stay. Then , it’s useful to ask, “ How would our adversaries design an immigration policy to weaken us?” The answer might include allowing more immigrants than we can integrate, not vetting them carefully, and using a lottery system instead of prioritizing whom to accept. These insights suggest that a good policy would do the opposite: allow only as many immigrants as we can integrate, vet them carefully, and prioritize those who add the most value or integrate more easily.

此外，这条经验法则可以帮助我们制定更好的法律。以移民为例：问题不在于是否允许移民，而在于允许移民的程度以及如何选择哪些人可以留下。那么，我们可以思考：“我们的对手会如何制定移民政策来削弱我们？”答案可能包括允许的移民数量超过我们能够融合的数量，不对他们进行严格的审查，以及采用抽签制度而不是优先考虑哪些人可以留下。这些见解表明，好的政策应该反其道而行之：只允许我们能够融合的移民数量，对他们进行严格的审查，并优先考虑那些能够带来最大价值或更容易融入社会的人。

In summary, a powerful way to spot harmful or poorly designed policies is to ask which ones our foreign adversaries would applaud. By imagining how they might weaken us, we can craft laws with the opposite, strengthening features.

总之，识别有害或设计不合理的政策的一个有效方法是问问我们的外国对手会赞赏哪些政策。通过设想这些政策可能会如何削弱我们，我们可以制定出具有相反、增强自身实力的法律。

# ↩

CONCLUSIONS OF PART II

第二部分结论

T here was a time when politics was about finding common ground. “ You and I disagree on many things, but let’s first find out what we agree on and work together on that.” “ I want this, and you want that. Let’s find a win-win compromise.” “ Instead of being red vs. blue, it’s all citizens against poverty, crime, and war.”

曾几何时，政治的本质在于寻求共识。“你我有很多分歧，但我们先找出共同点，然后携手努力。”“我想要这个，你想要那个。让我们找到一个双赢的折衷方案。”“与其说是红蓝之争，不如说是全体公民共同对抗贫困、犯罪和战争。”

Conversely, nowadays, it seems politics is about destroying common ground. “ You and I agree on many things, but I will not work with you until you accept all of my positions.”

相反，如今的政治似乎变成了破坏共识。“你我有很多共识，但除非你接受我的所有立场，否则我不会与你合作。”

People approach politics as if it were a zero-sum game, but it can be a negative-sum game. Without compromise and cooperation among those who disagree, the country and its people suffer. Worse still, the more a country stagnates, the more it falls behind its adversaries, increasing the chances of war or abuse.

人们看待政治往往将其视为零和博弈，但它也可能是一场负和博弈。如果持不同意见者之间缺乏妥协与合作，国家和人民都将遭受损失。更糟糕的是，一个国家越是停滞不前，就越会落后于其对手，从而增加战争或暴力冲突的风险。

* * *

I expect most readers of this book to have been lucky enough to live in a territory that hasn’t experienced war in the last seventy years. This is not because the world is becoming intrinsically more peaceful (it’s not)⁠ 1 but rather because some countries are prosperous enough to deter enemies from invading, democratic enough to avoid starting wars with their neighbors on a whim of their leader, and trade-focused enough to have more to gain from peace than war. However , the world may become less peaceful if these countries become unstable, elect the wrong leaders, or stop seeing positive-sum games as the most effective way to grow.

我预计本书的大多数读者都幸运地生活在过去七十年未曾经历过战争的地区。这并非因为世界本质上变得更加和平（事实并非如此），而是因为一些国家足够繁荣，足以震慑敌人入侵；足够民主，不会因领导人的一时兴起而与邻国开战；并且足够注重贸易，从和平中获益远大于战争。然而，如果这些国家变得不稳定，选出错误的领导人，或者不再将互利共赢视为最有效的增长方式，那么世界和平的局面可能会发生变化。

It is, therefore, of paramount importance not to take our prosperity for granted but to discuss politics and the economy with the seriousness they deserve.

因此，至关重要的是，我们不应将繁荣视为理所当然，而应以应有的严肃态度讨论政治和经济问题。

Seriousness is like car brakes: brakes are not meant to slow you down, but to enable you to go fast. Similarly , seriousness is not to make our lives cautious and slow, but to allow us to live them to their fullest.

严肃就像汽车刹车：刹车不是为了让你减速，而是为了让你加速。同样，严肃也不是为了让我们的生活变得谨慎缓慢，而是为了让我们能够尽情享受生活。

We do not want our lives to be entirely serious, but we must be serious when it matters so that we can be joyous the rest of the time.

我们不希望生活完全严肃，但我们必须在重要的事情上认真对待，这样我们才能在其他时间感到快乐。

1 “The Decline of Violent Conflicts: What Do the Data Really Say?” by Pasquale Cirillo and Nassim Nicholas Taleb, 2016.

1 “暴力冲突的减少：数据究竟说了什么？”，作者：Pasquale Cirillo 和 Nassim Nicholas Taleb，2016 年。

INTERLUDE

插曲

DEMOGRAPHIC CHALLENGES

人口挑战

B efore moving to Part II , let’s address the demographic challenges faced by first-world countries: declining fertility rates, an aging population, immigration, and AI -driven job automation. This section examines these issues and proposes possible solutions.

在进入第二部分之前，我们先来探讨一下发达国家面临的人口挑战：生育率下降、人口老龄化、移民以及人工智能驱动的工作自动化。本节将分析这些问题并提出可能的解决方案。

The problem with low fertility rates

低生育率的问题

I’m writing this book in 2025. Low fertility rates and aging populations have already entered public discourse, and yet, most people still do not grasp how serious this problem is.

我写这本书的时候是2025年。低生育率和人口老龄化已经成为公众讨论的话题，然而，大多数人仍然没有意识到这个问题有多么严重。

The US fertility rate is 1.66. This means that each pair of adults has 1.66 children, or on average 0.83 children per person: a 17% population decrease per generation. Repeating the calculation for another generation gives 0.83 × 0.83 = 0.69 children per person: a 31% drop over two generations, net of immigration.

美国的生育率为1.66。这意味着每对成年人平均生育1.66个孩子，或平均每人0.83个孩子：每代人口减少17%。重复计算，再过一代，每人将有0.83 × 0.83 = 0.69个孩子：两代人口减少31%（已扣除移民因素）。

Europe looks even worse: with a fertility rate of 1.46, each person will have only 0.53 grandchildren. And my home country, Italy , fares even worse. Its fertility rate of 1.18 implies a 65% population decline over two generations if nothing changes!

欧洲的情况更糟：生育率仅为1.46，这意味着每个人平均只能有0.53个孙辈。而我的祖国意大利的情况更糟。其生育率仅为1.18，这意味着如果现状不改变，两代人的时间里人口将减少65%！

But why is low fertility a problem?

但为什么低生育率会成为一个问题呢？

Isn’t a smaller population better, with more resources per person and less pollution?

人口越少，人均资源越多，污染越少，难道不是越好吗？

Not really.

并不真地。

First of all, the transition years will be highly problematic. If current projections hold, within two decades, each Italian retiree will be supported by 40% fewer working-age adults. This means already-high taxes would have to rise further (if that is even possible without causing an exodus and crippling the economy), or pensions and elder healthcare would need to be cut in half, or public services for everyone would face deeper funding shortages. None of these outcomes is attractive.⁠ 1

首先，过渡时期将充满挑战。如果目前的预测成真，二十年后，意大利每位退休人员将由减少40%的劳动年龄人口供养。这意味着本已高企的税收将不得不进一步提高（即便提高税收不会导致人口外流和经济衰退），或者养老金和老年医疗保健支出将不得不削减一半，或者面向所有人的公共服务将面临更严重的资金短缺。所有这些结果都令人担忧。

Moreover, if the Western world’s population shrinks much faster than the rest of the world, it could destabilize the geopolitical balance and even lead to conflict.

此外，如果西方世界的人口减少速度远超世界其他地区，可能会破坏地缘政治平衡，甚至导致冲突。

In both cases, the problem is not the change itself but the speed at which it happens, especially compared with most people’s expectations. Also , what worries me the most is that we could be preparing for the coming shock, but we are not.

无论哪种情况，问题都不在于变化本身，而在于变化发生的速度，尤其与大多数人的预期相比。此外，最令我担忧的是，我们本可以为即将到来的冲击做好准备，但我们并没有。

Some people believe there are alternatives to solving this problem other than restoring fertility rates, but I am skeptical. One is to increase productivity through robotics and automation so much that an aging population can still be supported despite a shrinking workforce. That would be ideal, and while I believe we may eventually reach that point, I am not sure it will happen fast enough to avoid the shocks described above. In addition, for readers in countries other than the US , China , and a few others, the question is not just whether the technology will exist, but whether their country will have the internal know-how, energy, and resources to build and use it cheaply enough.

有些人认为除了提高生育率之外，还有其他方法可以解决这个问题，但我对此持怀疑态度。一种方法是通过机器人和自动化大幅提高生产力，从而在劳动力萎缩的情况下也能养活老龄化人口。这当然是理想情况，虽然我相信我们最终可能会达到这个目标，但我并不确定它能否以足够快的速度实现，从而避免上述冲击。此外，对于美国、中国和其他少数几个国家以外的读者来说，问题不仅在于这项技术是否存在，还在于他们的国家是否拥有足够的内部技术、精力和资源，以足够低的成本开发和使用这项技术。

The other proposed alternative is to increase immigration, but this would require rates far above current levels, which already seem higher than our countries can absorb. This reinforces the importance of raising fertility rates as much as possible through organic means.

另一种提议的替代方案是增加移民，但这需要远高于目前的移民率，而目前的移民率似乎已经超过了我们国家的吸收能力。这更加凸显了通过自然方式尽可能提高生育率的重要性。

Increasing fertility rates

生育率上升

Contrary to common belief, low wages and poverty are not the main cause of declining fertility. If they were, European and American families would have more children than, say, African ones. This explains, by the way, why financial subsidies for parents have a limited effect.⁠ 2

与普遍认知相反，低工资和贫困并非生育率下降的主要原因。如果真是如此，欧洲和美国的家庭应该比非洲家庭生育更多子女。顺便一提，这也解释了为什么对父母的经济补贴效果有限。

Instead, low fertility rates likely stem from cultural and societal trends. Longer and more expensive education means young adults find and marry a partner later in life, when conception is harder. Additionally , our culture seems to celebrate successful careers more than starting a family. Or , more accurately, it expects adults to achieve both while neglecting to mention that having children becomes harder with age.

相反，低生育率很可能源于文化和社会趋势。教育时间更长、费用更高，意味着年轻人会在人生后期才找到伴侣并结婚，而此时受孕难度更大。此外，我们的文化似乎更推崇事业成功而非组建家庭。或者更准确地说，它期望成年人两者兼得，却忽略了随着年龄增长生育难度会增加这一事实。

Therefore, I suggest that raising fertility rates requires redefining the life trajectory expected of young adults, from:

因此，我认为提高生育率需要重新定义年轻人的生活轨迹，从：

“18-24 years old: study,

“18-24岁：研究，

24-33: work hard,

24-33岁：努力工作，

34+: parent and goodbye aspirations.”

34岁以上：为人父母和告别的愿望。”

To:

到：

"17-20 years old: study,

“17-20岁：研究，

20-24: work hard,

20-24岁：努力工作，

24-34: parent,

24-34岁：父母，

35+: career in your skill prime.” ⁠ 3 ⁠ , 4

35岁以上：正值技能巅峰的职业生涯。”⁠ 3 ⁠ , 4

Of course, the ages are only indicative and should not be interpreted as a “one-size-fits-all” path. For example, one does not stop being a parent after ten years. Still , the point remains: if we want higher fertility rates, we must redefine the default life trajectory so that having children happens earlier and without halting professional ambitions.

当然，这些年龄仅供参考，不应被视为“一刀切”的准则。例如，一个人不会在十年后就停止为人父母。然而，关键在于：如果我们想要更高的生育率，就必须重新定义默认的人生轨迹，让生育更早发生，同时又不影响职业抱负。

We should also consider ways to elevate parents’ status. I will not discuss how to do this, as it is highly culture-specific, but the goal is to ensure that young adults do not feel they are putting aside their ambitions when they have children, but instead feel like they are fulfilling them.

我们也应该考虑如何提升父母的地位。具体如何做到这一点，我不打算详述，因为这与文化差异很大，但目标是确保年轻人在为人父母后，不会觉得是在放弃自己的抱负，而是觉得他们正在实现自己的抱负。

Immigration

移民

Most discussion about immigration boils down to one group shouting that immigration is good and another that it’s bad. This is as absurd as a company debating whether hiring is good or bad. Hiring is only as good as the candidates you interview, your selection and onboarding processes, and your ability to quickly remove those you regret having hired. The same applies to immigration.

关于移民的大多数讨论最终都归结为一方高喊移民好，另一方高喊移民坏。这就像一家公司争论招聘是好是坏一样荒谬。招聘的好坏取决于你面试的候选人、你的筛选和入职流程，以及你能否迅速解雇那些你后悔招的人。移民问题也是如此。

It starts with selection. An immigration process that accepts everyone is bound to produce worse outcomes than a more selective one, especially when it comes to values. Accepting immigrants without screening for values and ensuring compatibility with the host population is nonsensical. ( Of course, people can lie, but people also lie during oaths and job interviews, yet we still do them, because they are still at least partially effective.)

一切始于筛选。一个来者不拒的移民过程必然会比一个更有选择性的过程产生更糟糕的结果，尤其是在价值观方面。如果不对移民的价值观进行筛选，也不确保他们与东道国居民的契合度，就接纳他们，这简直是荒谬的。（当然，人们会撒谎，但人们在宣誓和求职面试中也会撒谎，然而我们仍然保留这些程序，因为它们至少在一定程度上仍然有效。）

Selection is particularly important for asylum seekers. By definition, they tend to come from countries with a relatively high proportion of toxic or dysfunctional individuals; that is why they fled. Therefore , these are precisely the immigrants who require the most careful screening.

对寻求庇护者而言，甄别尤为重要。顾名思义，他们往往来自社会弊病或问题人群比例较高的国家；这正是他们逃离家园的原因。因此，这些移民群体恰恰需要最严格的筛选。

Once admitted, how easy is it for immigrants to become productive citizens? What does their onboarding look like, if there is one at all?

一旦获得移民身份，移民融入社会有多容易？他们融入社会的过程是怎样的？如果有的话。

Finally, just as no company hires only perfect employees, no country can accept only ideal immigrants. Some criminals and disruptive individuals will slip through. How are they handled? Are they swiftly punished, imprisoned, or expelled, or are they allowed to shame other immigrants and polarize the native population?

最后，正如没有公司会只雇用完美的员工一样，也没有哪个国家能只接纳理想的移民。总会有一些罪犯和扰乱社会秩序的人混进来。这些人该如何处理？是迅速受到惩罚、监禁或驱逐，还是任由他们羞辱其他移民，并加剧本地居民的社会分裂？

All of this is amplified by whether citizens and immigrants alike embrace the principles discussed in the “ Friends and Foes ” chapter (in particular, whether they are willing to call out the bad apples within their group), and whether the quality of the discourse on immigration remains high or degenerates into destructive polarization.

所有这一切都取决于公民和移民是否都接受“朋友和敌人”一章中讨论的原则（特别是他们是否愿意指出自己群体中的害群之马），以及关于移民的讨论质量是否保持高水平，还是恶化为破坏性的两极分化。

Improving immigration begins with seeing it not as a fixed concept, but as a process that can be made as good or bad as we choose.

改善移民政策首先要将其视为一个过程，而不是一个固定的概念，我们可以选择让它变得好或坏。

Pensions

养老金

Worsening demographics will severely affect the quality of life of future retirees. Contrary to common belief, most Western workers’ pension contributions are not saved for their own retirement but are used to pay current retirees. As the ratio of workers to pensioners declines, either pensions must shrink or public services will lose funding.

人口结构恶化将严重影响未来退休人员的生活质量。与普遍认知相反，大多数西方劳动者的养老金缴款并非用于自身退休，而是用于支付当前退休人员的福利。随着劳动者与退休人员比例的下降，养老金要么缩水，要么公共服务资金短缺。

(Are retirees “owed” their current pensions? They were promised them, yet that promise may have been unfair, placing an excessive burden on future generations. It’s not a fair promise if it results in newer generations having to pay a much higher share of their income to cover pension public spending than what previous generations had to pay.)

（退休人员“应该”拿到他们目前的养老金吗？他们当初确实被承诺过，但这个承诺可能并不公平，给后代造成了过重的负担。如果这意味着新一代人需要拿出比前几代人高得多的收入比例来支付养老金公共支出，那么这个承诺就是不公平的。）

Moreover, many plan retirement by estimating how their net worth will complement pension income, which is wise, but often based on inflated asset prices. Few consider that housing values can drop as populations decline. That happened recently in my city, Turin : despite being one of Italy’s top economies, house prices have fallen about 30% from their 2012 peak,⁠ 5 largely due to a shrinking population.⁠ 6 Retirees may therefore overestimate their capital.

此外，许多人在规划退休时会估算自己的净资产如何补充养老金收入，这固然明智，但往往基于过高的资产价格。很少有人考虑到，随着人口减少，房价也会下跌。这种情况最近就发生在我所在的城市都灵：尽管都灵是意大利的主要经济体之一，但房价已从2012年的峰值下跌了约30%，这主要是由于人口减少。因此，退休人员可能会高估自己的资产。

Finally, purchasing power depends not only on wealth but also on prices. And healthcare, a major retirement expense, depends on the ratio of elderly patients to healthcare workers, which is worsening with demographics.

最后，购买力不仅取决于财富，还取决于物价。而医疗保健作为一项主要的退休支出，又取决于老年患者与医护人员的比例，而随着人口结构的变化，这一比例正在恶化。

All of this is not only a problem for retirees. The more money goes to pensions, the higher the taxes for workers and the less funding for public services.

这一切不仅仅是退休人员的问题。养老金支出越多，劳动者的税收就越高，公共服务的资金就越少。

To prevent that, pensions, especially above the minimum, should be tied to total GDP rather than per capita GDP . This may seem harsh, but the alternative, soaring pension costs as a percentage of GDP that erode healthcare and public services for the poorest seniors, is harsher still.

为避免这种情况，养老金，尤其是高于最低标准的养老金，应与GDP总量挂钩，而非与人均GDP挂钩。这或许听起来有些苛刻，但另一种选择——养老金支出占GDP比例飙升，进而削弱最贫困老年人的医疗保健和公共服务——则更为糟糕。

Of course, that is not the only lever to improve the outlook. As discussed throughout this book, the first two should be increasing productivity and reducing waste and opportunity costs.

当然，这并非改善前景的唯一途径。正如本书后续章节所述，前两个途径应该是提高生产率、减少浪费和机会成本。

Job automation

工作自动化

I’m writing these lines in 2025, and fully self-driving taxi services remain prohibited almost everywhere, except in a handful of cities.

我写下这些文字时是 2025 年，而除了少数几个城市之外，完全自动驾驶出租车服务在几乎所有地方仍然被禁止。

The reason is not safety (these vehicles are significantly safer than human drivers), but rather that existing taxi drivers fear losing their jobs. This position is understandable from their point of view, but should society help them protect those jobs?

原因并非安全问题（这些车辆比人类驾驶员安全得多），而是现有出租车司机担心失去工作。从他们的角度来看，这种担忧可以理解，但社会是否应该帮助他们保住工作呢？

It depends. In countries with high unemployment, one could argue that society is better off with those people driving taxis than sitting at home, even if robots could do it more cheaply. However , in countries with low unemployment, protecting jobs from automation is counterproductive.

这要视情况而定。在失业率高的国家，有人可能会认为，即使机器人能以更低的成本完成工作，但让这些人开出租车总比让他们待在家里要好，这样对社会更有利。然而，在失业率低的国家，保护工作岗位免受自动化侵害反而会适得其反。

To see why, let us return to our fictional countries, Moralia and Pragmatia . ( But before that, let me clarify that deciding not to protect the jobs does not mean abandoning the workers; those who lose their jobs should be supported during their transition.)

为了理解个中缘由，让我们回到虚构的国家莫拉利亚和普拉格玛提亚。（但在此之前，我想澄清一点：决定不保住工作岗位并不意味着抛弃工人；那些失业的人应该在过渡期间得到支持。）

Moralia decides to protect taxi drivers and makes self-driving taxis illegal. As a result, none of its taxi drivers lose their jobs.

莫拉利亚决定保护出租车司机，并宣布自动驾驶出租车非法。结果，该国没有一名出租车司机因此失业。

Pragmatia, on the other hand, allows self-driving taxis. As these spread to more cities, taxi drivers gradually lose their jobs. However , after a few months of unemployment subsidies, most find new employment (remember, we are considering a situation with low unemployment).

另一方面，Pragmatia允许自动驾驶出租车运营。随着自动驾驶出租车在更多城市普及，出租车司机逐渐失业。然而，在领取几个月的失业补贴后，大多数人都能找到新的工作（请记住，我们讨论的是低失业率的情况）。

Who fares better? Both countries have the same number of taxi services, but Pragmatia gains two advantages: first, taxi rides are cheaper, allowing more citizens to afford them; and second, Pragmatia produces more goods and services in the sectors where former taxi drivers now work, making those goods and services more affordable.

谁的处境更好？两国出租车服务的数量相同，但普拉格马蒂亚拥有两项优势：首先，出租车费用更低，更多公民能够负担得起；其次，普拉格马蒂亚在原出租车司机所在的行业生产了更多商品和服务，使这些商品和服务更加实惠。

There is also another factor to consider. This example focused on a single job category, but automation affects much more than that. So , let us add a second job category (accountants) to the previous example to see how this changes the picture.

还有另一个因素需要考虑。这个例子只关注了一个职位类别，但自动化的影响远不止于此。所以，让我们在之前的例子中加入第二个职位类别（会计），看看情况会如何变化。

Moralia decides to protect both taxi drivers and accountants, banning the use of artificial intelligence in accounting. As a result, accounting remains just as costly as before.

莫拉利亚决定同时保护出租车司机和会计师的利益，禁止在会计领域使用人工智能。因此，会计成本依然居高不下。

Pragmatia, conversely, allows AI software to reduce accounting costs. This benefits citizens, who spend less time and money on their tax declarations, and companies, which now have lower accounting expenses. Part of these savings is passed on to consumers through cheaper goods and services. More importantly, Pragmatia’s exports become more competitive, leading foreign buyers to prefer Pragmatian products over Moralian ones. As a result, jobs shift from Moralia to Pragmatia : former Pragmatian accountants find new employment, while many Moralians lose theirs, even outside accounting.

相反，Pragmatia 利用人工智能软件降低会计成本。这不仅使公民受益（他们无需花费大量时间和金钱进行纳税申报），也使企业受益（它们的会计费用降低）。部分节省下来的成本会以更低的价格回馈给消费者。更重要的是，Pragmatia 的出口竞争力增强，促使外国买家更倾向于选择 Pragmatia 的产品而非 Moralia 的产品。因此，工作岗位从 Moralia 流向 Pragmatia：原 Pragmatia 的会计师找到了新的工作，而许多 Moralia 的会计师则失去了工作，甚至在会计行业之外也失去了工作。

This highlights a crucial point: governments must explain to their citizens that the real risk is not losing jobs to automation, but to countries that embrace it (or to countries with cheaper labor⁠ 7 ).

这凸显了一个关键点：各国政府必须向其公民解释，真正的风险不是因自动化而失去工作，而是工作岗位流失到拥抱自动化的国家（或劳动力成本更低的国家）。

Likewise, managers should remind their teams that the threat is not losing jobs to automation itself, but to competitors who adopt it first.

同样，管理者应该提醒他们的团队，真正的威胁不是自动化本身造成的失业，而是那些率先采用自动化技术的竞争对手造成的失业。

(It goes without saying that the adoption of robots and artificial intelligence should not be lawless but subject to reasonable accountability, legal, privacy, safety, etc. standards.)

（毋庸置疑，机器人和人工智能的应用不应不受法律约束，而应遵循合理的问责、法律、隐私、安全等标准。）

1 Another problem is that the fewer children a country has, the fewer “parent-friendly” places, events, and infrastructure exist, which discourages future parents and creates a downward spiral.

另一个问题是，一个国家的孩子越少，适合父母的地方、活动和基础设施就越少，这会打击未来父母的积极性，并造成恶性循环。

Consider how the recent increase in the canine population has led to more dog-friendly restaurants, pet shops, and pet sitters, making dog owners’ lives easier. If the dog population declined, these facilities would likely shrink too, making ownership harder. Why wouldn’t the same happen with babies and children’s infrastructure?

想想看，近年来犬类数量的增长催生了更多对狗狗友好的餐厅、宠物店和宠物保姆，让狗主人的生活更加便利。如果犬类数量下降，这些设施也可能随之减少，养狗变得更加困难。为什么婴儿和儿童的基础设施就不会出现同样的情况呢？

2 “[Hungary] spends 5% of GDP on trying to raise birth rates, but increases have leveled off,” wrote the Financial Times in its 2024-08-19 article “Why Hungary’s lavish family subsidies failed to spur a baby boom.”

《金融时报》在 2024 年 8 月 19 日发表的文章《为什么匈牙利慷慨的家庭补贴未能刺激婴儿潮》中写道：“匈牙利将 5% 的 GDP 用于提高出生率，但出生率的增长已经趋于平缓。”

The country’s statistical service reports that the fertility rate rose from 1.23 to 1.59 between 2011 and 2020, but then leveled off to about 1.5 and decreased to 1.36 in the first half of 2024.

该国统计部门报告称，2011 年至 2020 年间，生育率从 1.23 上升至 1.59，但随后稳定在 1.5 左右，并在 2024 年上半年下降至 1.36。

3 “But Luca, you’re 37 and do not have children yet. Isn’t it hypocritical of you to call for people to have children earlier while you have none?”

3 “但是卢卡，你都37岁了还没有孩子。你自己没有孩子，却呼吁人们早点生孩子，这难道不是虚伪吗？”

I don’t think so. First of all, as I mentioned elsewhere in this book, hypocrisy is overrated: if we only allow the perfect to call out others, no one would call out anyone, and we would descend into mediocrity. What matters is not whether I have children, but whether I genuinely believe having them is important, and whether I did my best or close to my best in that direction.

我不这么认为。首先，正如我在本书其他章节提到的，虚伪被过分夸大了：如果我们只允许完美的人去指责他人，那么就没有人会去指责任何人，我们最终会沦为平庸。重要的不是我是否有孩子，而是我是否真心相信拥有孩子是重要的，以及我是否为此尽了全力，或者至少接近了全力。

Secondly, the problem I call out is precisely half of the reason I haven’t had children yet (the other half has been a series of medical problems, including cancer, which basically put child-making on pause for several years – I’m fine now, thankfully ).

其次，我指出的问题正是我至今没有孩子的原因之一（另一半原因是一系列健康问题，包括癌症，这基本上使我暂停生育计划好几年——谢天谢地，我现在没事了）。

4 Is this timeline unrealistic? How can young adults afford a house at 24? I agree that, under current conditions, it is unrealistic. But things would change if we implemented the ideas discussed in this book, so that, for instance, housing became more abundant and young adults could afford to start families earlier.

4. 这个时间表不现实吗？年轻人24岁就能买得起房吗？我同意，在目前的条件下，这不现实。但如果我们实施本书中讨论的理念，情况就会有所改变，例如，住房供应更加充足，年轻人就能更早地组建家庭。

5 Source: “Evoluzione del prezzo delle case in vendita, Torino provincia,” Idealista.it, published in September 2025.

5 资料来源：“都灵省待售房屋价格的演变”，Idealista.it，2025 年 9 月发布。

6 Note that housing demand in an aging country starts falling earlier than population data: when an elder gets too old to live alone and either moves in with their family or into a nursing home, the number of occupied houses decreases even though the population remains the same.

6 注意，老龄化国家的住房需求下降的时间早于人口数据下降的时间：当老年人年纪太大无法独自生活，搬去和家人一起住或住进养老院时，即使人口保持不变，有人居住的房屋数量也会减少。

7 On the topic of cheaper labor, it is frustrating to hear claims that Italy’s economy suffered from the euro because it prevented currency devaluation to make exports more competitive through lower labor costs. Among all the factors that influence competitiveness (more productive companies, a more skilled workforce, less bureaucracy, lower energy costs, better processes), it is hard to understand the fascination with devaluation. Why would anyone want to make imports more expensive in a world where nearly everything we buy is at least partly produced abroad? Is gaining market share by lowering one’s purchasing power truly desirable? I don’t think so.

7. 关于降低劳动力成本，有人声称意大利经济因欧元而受损，因为它阻止了货币贬值以降低劳动力成本从而提高出口竞争力，这种说法令人沮丧。在所有影响竞争力的因素中（例如生产效率更高的企业、技能更娴熟的劳动力、更少的官僚主义、更低的能源成本、更优化的流程），很难理解人们为何如此痴迷于货币贬值。在一个几乎所有商品都至少部分产自国外的世界里，为什么有人会希望进口商品价格上涨呢？通过降低购买力来获取市场份额真的可取吗？我认为并非如此。

PART III
第三部分

UTOPIA AND DYSTOPIA

乌托邦与反乌托邦

As a reminder, “ Utopia ” is a term referring to a society in which everything is perfect, whereas “ Dystopia ” refers to a society marked by widespread suffering or injustice, typically under a totalitarian regime.

需要提醒的是，“乌托邦”指的是一个一切都很完美的社会，而“反乌托邦”指的是一个充斥着普遍苦难或不公正的社会，通常是在极权统治下的社会。

* * *

The worst dystopias often arise from a desire for utopia.

最糟糕的反乌托邦往往源于对乌托邦的渴望。

The stronger the vision of a perfect world, the more one feels that the end justifies the means, and the more likely they are to use a totalitarian approach.

对完美世界的憧憬越强烈，就越觉得结果可以证明手段的正当性，也就越有可能采取极权主义手段。

This is not a reason to abandon our drive to improve the world, but a reminder to follow moral and practical guidelines that help ensure our efforts move us closer to utopia rather than dystopia.

这并不是让我们放弃改善世界的理由，而是提醒我们要遵循道德和实践准则，以确保我们的努力使我们更接近乌托邦而不是反乌托邦。

We will begin by discussing Late Bureaucracies and Late Democracies , two common precursors to dystopia. Next , we will examine Communism and Capitalism . Then , we will explore non-political sources of systemic risk that could cause widespread suffering. Finally , we will consider the ultimate question: do we want our utopia to be shaped by choice or coercion?

我们将首先探讨晚期官僚主义和晚期民主主义，这是反乌托邦的两种常见先兆。接下来，我们将考察共产主义和资本主义。然后，我们将探讨可能导致普遍苦难的非政治性系统性风险来源。最后，我们将思考一个终极问题：我们希望我们的乌托邦是由选择还是强制塑造的？

22

LATE BUREAUCRACIES

晚期官僚机构

V enture capitalist Nathan Beinach recently recounted the ordeal of founding a startup in Germany . He wrote: “ Twelve hours and counting, a notary reads every single word of Series A docs in German out loud in front of founders. In person.”⁠ 1

风险投资家内森·贝纳赫 (Nathan Beinach) 最近讲述了他在德国创办一家初创公司的艰辛经历。他写道：“整整十二个小时，一位公证员当着创始人的面，用德语逐字逐句地朗读A轮融资文件。全程当面进行。”

He continued (emphasis his): “ EIGHTY SIX THOUSAND EUROS . That’s how much this German notary ordeal taxed (sorry, cost) a startup to complete their financing. Oh , and lawyer fees are not included.”⁠ 2

他继续说道（重点为他所加）：“八万六千欧元。这就是这家初创公司为了完成融资，在德国公证处经历的这场磨难所花费的金额（抱歉，是成本）。哦，对了，律师费还不包括在内。”

This horror story is a warning about what I like to call a Late Bureaucracy ,⁠ 3 a dystopian society where bureaucratic systems have evolved beyond administration into a self-perpetuating maze of procedures, forms, and regulations.

这个恐怖故事是对所谓“晚期官僚主义”的警告，这是一个反乌托邦社会，其中官僚体系已经超越了行政管理，演变成一个自我延续的程序、表格和规章制度的迷宫。

Like all dystopias, Late Bureaucracies arise from two dangerous patterns: good intentions gone wrong and a disconnect between rule-makers and rule-followers.

像所有反乌托邦一样，晚期官僚主义源于两种危险的模式：好心办坏事，以及规则制定者和规则遵守者之间的脱节。

Understanding these patterns is crucial to preventing our institutions from sliding into dysfunction.

了解这些模式对于防止我们的机构陷入功能失调至关重要。

The problem with good intentions

好心办坏事

“The road to hell is paved with good intentions,” the saying goes, but that is not quite right. The road to hell is paved with an initial good intention, followed by a deliberate ignorance of facts and evidence showing that one’s course of action is wrong.

俗话说“通往地狱的路是由善意铺成的”，但这种说法并不完全正确。通往地狱的路是由最初的善意铺成的，随后是对事实和证据的故意无视，而这些事实和证据表明，自己的行为是错误的。

A well-intended person would formulate a hypothesis, test it, observe the results, and adjust accordingly. Yet many bureaucrats skip the last two steps. They create rules without checking whether they work, rarely admit mistakes, and even when they do, they do not examine what led them astray.

一个真正有良知的人会提出假设，进行检验，观察结果，并据此做出调整。然而，许多官僚却忽略了最后两步。他们制定规则却不去检验其有效性，很少承认错误，即便承认了，也不去探究究竟是什么导致了错误。

We spend years of our children’s precious school time teaching them history, but we fail to teach them that good intentions alone do not prevent harm. What matters is results, not intentions. Creating rules without monitoring their real-world impact is not only inefficient but also irresponsible.

我们花费孩子们宝贵的求学时光数年时间教他们历史，却忽略了告诉他们，光有良好的意愿并不能避免伤害。重要的是结果，而不是意愿。制定规则却不去监测其在现实世界中的影响，不仅效率低下，而且是不负责任的。

The next time we embark on a journey toward Utopia , we should first and foremost establish a system to observe how policies perform in the real world and recalibrate quickly if problems arise.

下次我们踏上通往乌托邦的旅程时，首先应该建立一套系统来观察政策在现实世界中的表现，并在出现问题时迅速进行调整。

Failing to do so is a fast path to Dystopia .

否则，将迅速走向反乌托邦。

A pathological detachment from reality

对现实的病态脱离

In Late Bureaucracies , officials obsess over procedural correctness while losing sight of real outcomes. Citizens accept well-intentioned policies regardless of their effects. Politicians often remain insulated from the costs of bureaucracy, either because the rules do not apply to them or because they can offset these costs with expensive professional help (lawyers, accountants, etc.) that ordinary citizens cannot afford.

在官僚体制后期，官员们过分注重程序上的严谨，却忽视了实际结果。民众接受那些出发点良好的政策，却不考虑其实际效果。政客们往往能够免受官僚体制成本的影响，要么是因为规则对他们无效，要么是因为他们可以通过聘请普通民众无力承担的昂贵专业人士（律师、会计师等）来抵消这些成本。

Nassim Nicholas Taleb captures this perfectly, defining bureaucracy as a “construction by which a person is conveniently separated from the consequences of his or her actions.”⁠ 4

纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布对此做了精辟的概括，他将官僚主义定义为“一种使人能够方便地与其行为后果分离的机制”。

How do we fix this disconnect? The solution comes in two parts.

我们该如何解决这种脱节问题？解决方案包含两部分。

First, bureaucrats must have real skin in the game. As Taleb argues, mere incentives are not enough, since they do not protect us from incompetence or conflicts of interest. We also need systems that quickly remove those who create harmful policies from positions where they can make more of them.

首先，官僚机构必须真正承担责任。正如塔勒布所言，仅仅依靠激励机制是不够的，因为它无法保护我们免受无能或利益冲突的影响。我们还需要建立相应的制度，迅速将那些制定有害政策的人从能够继续推行此类政策的岗位上撤换下来。

Second, bureaucrats must experience their own rules firsthand. For example:

其次，官僚们必须亲身体验自己制定的规则。例如：

  • Imagine lawmakers were required to use public healthcare. Who wouldn’t agree that this would lead to better public hospitals? This might seem unrealistic, but is it really? In my 2019 book Best Practices for Operational Excellence , I recount how, in its early days, the DuPont company drastically reduced explosions in its gunpowder factories by requiring that all new machines be operated for a few minutes by top management. And , of course, this solution worked where everything else had failed!
    试想一下，如果立法者被要求使用公共医疗保健系统，谁会不认为这会带来更好的公立医院呢？这听起来或许不切实际，但事实果真如此吗？在我2019年出版的《卓越运营最佳实践》一书中，我讲述了杜邦公司早期如何通过要求所有新机器都必须由高层管理人员操作几分钟，从而大幅降低了火药厂的爆炸事故。当然，这个方法在其他所有方法都失败的情况下奏效了！
  • Imagine lawmakers having to meet face-to-face with ordinary citizens weekly to hear their complaints. Surely this would have a stronger impact than merely reading grievances in newspapers. ( If this seems unrealistic, consider that Singapore’s Parliament Members practice it. Sure , it’s a small country, but your city and province are unlikely to be much bigger; why don’t their elected representatives do that, too?)
    想象一下，如果立法者每周都要与普通民众面对面交流，倾听他们的诉求，这肯定比仅仅在报纸上阅读民众的抱怨更有效果。（如果这听起来不切实际，不妨想想新加坡的国会议员们就是这么做的。诚然，新加坡是个小国，但你的城市和省份的规模也不太可能比它大多少；为什么他们的民选代表不也这样做呢？）
  • Imagine high-ranking bureaucrats having to visit companies to see how their rules affect workers. Are processes followed or gamed? Are they easy or difficult to follow? For this to be effective, observations must be firsthand, not filtered through assistants or reports.
    试想一下，如果高级官员必须亲自走访企业，了解规章制度对员工的影响，会是怎样一番景象？流程是否得到严格执行？是否存在钻空子的情况？流程是否易于理解或难以执行？为了确保考察的有效性，必须进行第一手观察，而不能通过助理或报告进行过滤。

Reducing complexity

降低复杂性

Of course, modern societies are inherently complex, and this necessitates a certain level of legislative complexity to govern effectively. However , excessive complexity creates fertile ground for Late Bureaucracies . The more complex the environment, the more rules bureaucrats create to manage it, which in turn generates even more complexity. This vicious cycle can only be broken by actively keeping things simple.

当然，现代社会本质上是复杂的，这就需要一定程度的立法复杂性才能有效治理。然而，过度的复杂性会为官僚主义的滋生创造温床。环境越复杂，官僚们为了管理它而制定的规则就越多，而这反过来又会造成更大的复杂性。只有积极地简化程序，才能打破这种恶性循环。

This is not easy. Bureaucrats often resist simplification because complexity makes them indispensable. The bigger obstacle, however, is short-term thinking. Adding “just one more rule” may solve today’s problem, but creates tomorrow’s nightmare.⁠ 5 ⁠ , 6

这并非易事。官僚们往往抵制简化，因为复杂性让他们显得不可或缺。然而，更大的障碍在于短视思维。增加“一条规则”或许能解决眼前的难题，却会埋下明日的祸根。

# ↩

Chapter summary

章节概要

Bureaucracies do not become dystopian overnight. They decay gradually through the accumulation of well-intentioned but poorly monitored rules. When bureaucrats can create rules without facing their consequences, and when complexity breeds more complexity without regular pruning, the conditions are perfect for a Late Bureaucracy to take root.

官僚机构并非一夜之间就变成反乌托邦式的。它们会随着大量初衷良好但监管不力的规则的累积而逐渐衰败。当官僚们可以制定规则而无需承担后果，当复杂性滋生出更多复杂性而又缺乏定期的精简时，晚期官僚机构的滋生便水到渠成。

The solution lies in three key principles: monitoring the real-world impact of rules, ensuring bureaucrats have skin in the game, and actively combating complexity. Singapore’s practice of regular face-to-face meetings between Parliament Members and citizens shows that even in a complex modern world, we can maintain a human connection between rule-makers and those affected by their rules. Without such measures, we risk creating systems that, despite good intentions, ultimately harm the people they are meant to serve.

解决方案在于三个关键原则：监测规则在现实世界中的影响、确保官员切身利益攸关，以及积极应对复杂性。新加坡议员与公民定期举行面对面会晤的做法表明，即使在复杂的现代社会，我们仍然可以在规则制定者和受规则影响者之间保持人与人之间的联系。如果没有这些措施，我们就有可能建立起一些制度，这些制度即便出发点是好的，最终也会损害其服务对象——人民的利益。

3 我受到 Flo Crivello 的启发，使用了“晚期民主”一词，这与更熟悉的术语“晚期资本主义”相呼应。

4 Source: “Skin In The Game,” Nassim Nicholas Taleb, 2017.

4 资料来源：“Skin In The Game”，纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布，2017 年。

5 Mark Twain once wrote, “I didn't have time to write you a short letter, so I wrote you a long one.” Similarly, we often settle for complex policies because we feel we lack the time to craft simple ones.

5 马克·吐温曾写道：“我没时间给你写封短信，所以就给你写了封长信。” 同样，我们常常因为觉得没有时间制定简单的政策，而选择制定复杂的政策。

6. 这种心态源于一种错误的信念，即充分利用每一天就能确保我们充分利用一年的时间。但实际上，要想在一年中获得最大的收益，我们有时必须采取一些短期内看似效率低下，但从长远来看却至关重要的行动，才能达到更高的水平。
