23

DEMOCRACIES AND AUTOCRACIES

民主政体与专制政体

I n school, we are taught that democracies are better than dictatorships. But there’s little attention paid to the fact that many dictatorships actually began as democracies. Look at Nazi Germany , Chile in the 1970s, or, more recently, Venezuela . Each of these countries once held free elections and protected democratic rights,⁠ 1 until they didn’t.

学校里，我们被教导说民主比独裁好。但很少有人注意到，许多独裁政权实际上都是从民主国家起步的。看看纳粹德国、20世纪70年代的智利，或者最近的委内瑞拉。这些国家都曾举行过自由选举，保护过民主权利，直到后来才改变了这一切。

We cannot take democracy for granted. We must learn to spot warning signs early: when media manipulation and political violence become normalized, or when governments pass laws, such as censorship, that undermine democracy while claiming to protect it.

我们不能把民主视为理所当然。我们必须学会及早发现预警信号：当媒体操纵和政治暴力变得常态化，或者当政府通过诸如审查制度之类的法律，声称要保护民主却实际上破坏民主时。

As the saying goes, electing an autocrat is often a mistake you can make only once: there will be no more elections afterward. It is therefore crucial to recognize these signs not after democracy has collapsed, but in the intermediate stage: when it is in a pre-autocratic state.

正如俗语所说，选举独裁者往往是只能犯一次的错误：之后就不会再有选举了。因此，至关重要的是，要在民主崩溃的中间阶段，也就是在民主走向独裁的萌芽阶段，识别出这些迹象，而不是等到民主崩溃之后。

This chapter focuses on the all-important question of how to identify when democracy is in a pre-autocratic condition and how to reverse its trajectory before it’s too late.

本章重点讨论一个至关重要的问题：如何识别民主何时处于专制前状态，以及如何在为时过晚之前扭转其发展轨迹。

Pre-autocracies do not look like autocracies

前专制政体看起来不像专制政体

Looking for obvious signs of dictatorship to spot a failing democracy is like trying to diagnose cancer only at its final stages. Pre -autocratic countries still look like democracies: they hold elections, follow constitutions, and maintain independent courts and media. Contrary to popular expectation, tomorrow’s autocrats rarely arrive in military uniforms; more often, they look like ordinary citizens. ( For example, Stalin only started wearing his uniform after his rise to power.)

试图通过寻找明显的独裁迹象来判断一个民主国家是否正在走向衰落，就好比试图在癌症晚期才进行诊断一样。专制统治之前的国家看起来仍然像民主国家：它们举行选举，遵守宪法，并维持独立的法院和媒体。与人们普遍的预期相反，未来的独裁者很少身着军装；他们往往看起来像普通公民。（例如，斯大林是在掌权之后才开始穿军装的。）

The real key to identifying pre-autocracies is spotting subtle but consequential departures from democratic norms : changes that society gradually accepts as normal. These violations target four essential pillars: fair elections with real choice, independent and truth-seeking journalism, equal application of the law, and the shared belief that the ends never justify the means.

识别前专制政体的真正关键在于发现那些微妙却影响深远的偏离民主规范的行为：这些变化会被社会逐渐接受为常态。这些偏离针对的是四大支柱：真正公平的选举和选择、独立且追求真相的新闻报道、法律面前人人平等，以及“目的绝不能为手段辩护”这一共同信念。

Let’s examine each pillar and how it can begin to erode.

让我们逐一分析每个支柱，以及它们是如何开始瓦解的。

Many democracies transition to pre-autocracies when, to prevent the rise of a wannabe dictator, they start using methods such as censorship that make it easier to rise to power for wannabe dictators #2, #3, etc.

许多民主国家为了防止独裁者崛起，开始使用审查制度等手段，这使得独裁者更容易获得权力，从而向准独裁国家过渡。

# ↩

Elections in pre-autocracies

专制政体之前的选举

At first glance, the line between democracy and autocracy seems clear: does a country hold free and fair elections, or does it not? In reality, it’s more complicated.

乍一看，民主与专制之间的界限似乎很清晰：一个国家是否举行自由公正的选举？实际上，情况要复杂得多。

Some regimes have learned they don’t need to stuff ballot boxes to stay in power. Instead , they use subtler tactics, such as holding elections while controlling what voters know about leaders’ competence and performance, or rewarding friendly journalists with access while sidelining critics.

有些政权已经明白，他们无需操纵选票就能维持统治。相反，他们会采取更为隐蔽的策略，例如在举行选举的同时控制选民对领导人能力和政绩的了解，或者给予亲信记者采访机会，同时排挤批评者。

Even more deceptive are systems where power rests not in a single ruler but in an entrenched political class. These are particularly hard to spot because they preserve the outward appearance of democratic institutions (free elections and independent media) while citizens can choose only between candidates, but not the pool of candidates.

更具欺骗性的是那些权力并非掌握在单一统治者手中，而是掌握在根深蒂固的政治阶层手中的制度。这类制度尤其难以识别，因为它们表面上维持着民主制度的假象（自由选举和独立媒体），而公民只能在候选人之间进行选择，却无法选择所有候选人。

So, when we evaluate a democracy's health, we shouldn’t just ask whether elections are still free and fair, but also whether citizens receive high-quality factual information about candidates and whether outsiders are de facto allowed to get elected.

因此，当我们评估一个民主国家的健康状况时，我们不仅应该问选举是否仍然自由公正，还应该问公民是否能获得有关候选人的高质量事实信息，以及是否实际上允许局外人当选。

On this last point, we cannot just examine what the law says on paper; we must also watch what happens in practice. Many pre-autocratic systems maintain pristine democratic laws while creating invisible barriers that effectively block political newcomers. They do not ban outsiders outright but simply ensure they never gain real traction. For example, in Italian politics, there is a word, ricattabilità (which translates as “blackmailable”), used to indicate that established political parties required new entrants to have skeletons in the closet, making them controllable. Honest candidates faced systematic exclusion from parties, media coverage, and political life itself.

关于最后一点，我们不能仅仅审视法律条文，还必须观察其实际运作情况。许多前专制体制表面上维护着民主法律，实则暗藏玄机，有效地阻碍了政治新人的涌入。这些体制并非直接禁止外来者，而是确保他们永远无法真正获得影响力。例如，在意大利政坛，有一个词“ricattabilità”（意为“可勒索的”），用来指代老牌政党要求新候选人必须有不可告人的秘密，以便于控制。诚实的候选人则面临着被政党、媒体乃至整个政治生活系统性排斥的命运。

Journalism in pre-autocracies

专制政体之前的媒体

In many autocracies, governments control the press through two primary mechanisms: direct ownership of media outlets and the persecution of dissenting voices. This might tempt us to conclude that journalistic independence alone is a reliable indicator of democratic health. Such reasoning, however, is dangerously simplistic.

在许多专制政体中，政府通过两种主要机制控制新闻媒体：直接拥有媒体机构和迫害异议人士。这或许会让我们得出这样的结论：新闻独立性本身就是民主健康状况的可靠指标。然而，这种推理过于简单化，存在危险。

Even in seemingly open societies, governments can exert influence over the press. Consider how selective access shapes coverage: when officials grant interviews primarily to sympathetic journalists, they create a system that both incentivizes favorable coverage and ensures their message dominates public discourse. Critical voices, denied equal access, struggle to present alternative perspectives, and either fade into irrelevance or drift from independence to partisanship.

即使在看似开放的社会中，政府也能对媒体施加影响。想想选择性采访如何影响报道：当官员主要接受与其立场相近的记者采访时，他们就建立了一种既鼓励有利于自身的报道，又确保其自身信息主导公共舆论的体系。批评的声音被剥夺了平等的采访机会，难以提出不同的观点，最终要么被边缘化，要么从独立立场滑向党派立场。

The path toward autocracy, however, doesn’t always begin with government pressure. Often , journalists themselves compromise their essential role. This occurs when newsrooms prioritize sensationalism over substance, choosing to cover celebrity scandals rather than investigate policy decisions that affect millions, or when journalists allow political ideology to overshadow their commitment to factual reporting.

然而，通往专制的道路并非总是始于政府施压。很多时候，记者自身也会损害其至关重要的职责。这种情况发生在新闻编辑室为了追求耸人听闻的效果而牺牲实质内容，选择报道名人丑闻而非调查影响数百万人的政策决策时；或者当记者让政治意识形态凌驾于其对事实报道的承诺之上时。

On this last point, I do not mean that journalists cannot present political opinions. After all, who doesn’t have strong views about policy and governance? But these beliefs must never supersede their primary obligation to truth. Professional journalism requires presenting verified facts before discussing opinions. When this doesn’t happen, and societies discuss opinions before agreeing on facts, polarization rises, and democracies start to erode.

关于最后一点，我并非认为记者不能表达政治观点。毕竟，谁没有对政策和治理的强烈看法呢？但这些观点绝不能凌驾于他们对真相的首要责任之上。专业新闻工作要求在讨论观点之前先呈现经过核实的事实。如果做不到这一点，社会在尚未就事实达成共识之前就讨论观点，那么社会两极分化就会加剧，民主制度也会开始瓦解。

The point is that legal press freedom is necessary but not sufficient to show that we are still in a democracy. We must also consider whether journalists are effectively free to hold dissenting opinions without losing access and, perhaps more importantly, whether they seek truth rather than serve political ideas.

关键在于，合法的新闻自由固然必要，但并不足以证明我们仍然生活在民主社会中。我们还必须考虑记者是否能够真正自由地持有不同意见而不失去采访机会，或许更重要的是，他们是否追求真相而非服务于政治理念。

Democracies require more than free elections. They also require journalists to fulfill their duty of factually informing the population.

民主制度需要的不仅仅是自由选举，还需要记者履行其职责，向民众提供真实的信息。

The rule of law in pre-autocracies

专制政体之前的法治

The classic image of an autocrat is someone who rules by force and ignores laws at will. This might lead us to a dangerous conclusion: as long as leaders follow the law, we are safe from autocracy.

人们对独裁者的经典印象是：他们依靠武力统治，随意践踏法律。这可能会导致一个危险的结论：只要领导人遵守法律，我们就能免受独裁统治的侵害。

But many autocrats have learned a clever trick: why break laws when you can simply reshape them to serve your purposes? That’s why we need to monitor not only whether governments obey existing laws but also what new laws they create.

但许多独裁者都学会了一个巧妙的伎俩：既然可以随意修改法律以达到自己的目的，何必直接违法呢？因此，我们不仅需要监督政府是否遵守现有法律，还需要监督它们制定了哪些新法律。

The most obvious red flag is legislation that treats different groups of citizens differently. In their most extreme form, autocracies might pass laws directly targeting ethnic or religious groups. However , pre-autocratic systems often take a more socially acceptable approach. They suspend basic rights for “enemies of democracy,” look the other way during riots or lynchings, censor the intolerant, or pass laws that favor specific ethnic or racial groups in the name of social equity.

最明显的危险信号是区别对待不同公民群体的立法。在最极端的情况下，专制政权可能会通过法律直接针对特定族裔或宗教群体。然而，前专制政权往往采取一种更易被社会接受的方式。它们会暂停“民主敌人”的基本权利，对骚乱或私刑视而不见，审查不宽容的言论，或者以社会公平的名义通过有利于特定族裔或种族群体的法律。

These measures often start with good intentions, aiming to protect vulnerable groups or fight genuine threats to society. The immediate results might even be positive. But each exception to equal treatment under the law, even when made for noble reasons, chips away at a fundamental democratic principle: that the law should treat everyone the same.

这些措施往往出于好意，旨在保护弱势群体或应对对社会的真正威胁。短期效果甚至可能是积极的。但每一项对法律面前人人平等的例外，即便出于崇高的理由，都会削弱一项基本的民主原则：法律应当平等对待所有人。

This erosion of democratic values is precisely what makes it easier for an autocracy to emerge and is, therefore, a hallmark of pre-autocracies. True democracies never compromise democratic values, not even when fighting an enemy of democracy.

民主价值观的这种侵蚀恰恰为专制政体的出现创造了条件，因此也是专制政体出现之前的标志。真正的民主政体绝不会妥协民主价值观，即使是在对抗民主的敌人时也是如此。

Remember: we preserve our rights by guaranteeing them to our enemies.

记住：我们通过保障敌人的权利来维护我们自己的权利。

# ↩

But what about the Paradox of Tolerance?

但是，宽容悖论又该如何解释呢？

When a society extends tolerance to the intolerant, doesn’t it risk enabling their dominance? It depends. If the world were neatly divided into heroes and villains, and we could easily identify the “bad guys” and be certain the “good guys” would always remain good, the solution would be simple: fight the bad guys by any means necessary. But our reality is messier. Wolves hide among sheep, and today’s defenders of democracy might become tomorrow’s threats to it. Giving any group extraordinary powers, even with the best intentions, creates tools that could later be used against democracy itself. As I often say, “ First , we had a problem. So , we used censorship. Now , we have two problems.”

当一个社会对不宽容者采取宽容态度时，难道不会助长他们的统治吗？这要视情况而定。如果世界泾渭分明地分为英雄和恶棍，我们可以轻易识别“坏人”，并且确信“好人”永远都是好人，那么解决办法就很简单：不惜一切代价打击坏人。但我们的现实远比这复杂。狼藏在羊群中，今天的民主捍卫者可能成为明天的民主威胁。赋予任何群体超乎寻常的权力，即便出于善意，也会创造出日后可能被用来对抗民主本身的工具。正如我常说的，“起初，我们遇到了一个问题。于是，我们采取了审查制度。现在，我们面临两个问题。”

Perhaps more importantly, we do not need censorship to fight the enemies of democracy. History shows that most autocrats revealed their true nature by committing crimes long before seizing power. Had societies enforced existing laws against these tangible offenses, many dictators would have been stopped in their tracks.

或许更重要的是，我们无需审查制度来对抗民主的敌人。历史表明，大多数独裁者在夺取政权之前很久就通过犯罪暴露了其真面目。如果当时的社会能够有效执行针对这些实际犯罪行为的法律，许多独裁者早就被制止了。

The same logic applies to hate speech. Many who spread hatred have also committed violence or vandalism. By properly prosecuting these actual crimes, we could address the problem without compromising democratic principles. If this principle seems not to apply to cases like the Rwandan genocide incited by RTLM radio, whose staff had no prior criminal record, it’s because we’re not looking far enough back in time. Had the perpetrators of the violence in the previous decades been swiftly and publicly held accountable, the culture of impunity that allowed ethnic hatred to flourish might have weakened, and the ideological conditions that gave rise to RTLM might never have matured.

同样的逻辑也适用于仇恨言论。许多散播仇恨的人也犯有暴力或破坏行为。通过对这些实际犯罪行为进行适当的起诉，我们可以在不损害民主原则的前提下解决问题。如果这一原则似乎不适用于像卢旺达国家广播电视台（RTLM）煽动的种族灭绝这样的案例（该电视台的员工此前并无犯罪记录），那是因为我们追溯的时间不够长。如果过去几十年里的暴力犯罪者能够被迅速且公开地追究责任，那么助长种族仇恨的有罪不罚文化或许就会削弱，而催生RTLM的意识形态条件或许也就不会出现。

The point is, censorship is necessary only when violence and corruption are not prosecuted. In fact, this is the second hallmark of pre-autocracies: a degraded capacity to fight violence and corruption. The predictable result is widespread exasperation, leading to a demand for other, less democratic ways to fight crime. Where crime and corruption flourish unchecked, they create perfect conditions for would-be autocrats to present themselves as saviors who will “restore order” by any means necessary.

关键在于，只有当暴力和腐败行为得不到惩处时，审查制度才显得必要。事实上，这正是前专制政体的第二个显著特征：打击暴力和腐败的能力下降。其结果可想而知，民众普遍感到愤怒，转而寻求其他不那么民主的打击犯罪手段。在犯罪和腐败肆意横行、不受约束的地方，就为那些潜在的独裁者创造了绝佳的条件，让他们可以把自己塑造成救世主，不惜一切代价“恢复秩序”。

Legitimacy and pre-autocracies

合法性与前专制时期

I’m writing these lines in October 2024. As of this date, the United States still has a voting system in which mail-in ballots and electronic voting machines make electoral fraud plausibly possible.

我写下这些文字时是 2024 年 10 月。截至目前，美国的投票制度仍然采用邮寄选票和电子投票机，这使得选举舞弊成为可能。

Note that I didn’t say there has been fraud. I said there is a plausible possibility , regardless of whether such fraud has occurred. Even if nothing foul has happened, this plausible possibility is fertile ground for doubts. Similarly , whether these doubts are planted by politically motivated actors sowing division is irrelevant: as long as doubt is plausible, there will be discontent, friction, and instability. For democracy to thrive, elections need to be not just fair but also visibly and undeniably fair. The system needs to be so transparent and secure that claims of fraud sound absurd.

请注意，我并没有说已经发生了舞弊。我说的是存在这种可能性，无论舞弊是否真的发生。即使没有发生任何不正当行为，这种可能性本身也足以滋生疑虑。同样，这些疑虑是否是出于政治动机、旨在制造分裂的势力所散播的也无关紧要：只要疑虑存在，就会有不满、摩擦和不稳定。为了使民主制度蓬勃发展，选举不仅要公平，而且要公平得有目共睹、无可辩驳。制度必须足够透明和安全，以至于任何关于舞弊的指控都显得荒谬可笑。

This points to a critical pattern: while functioning democracies have elections beyond reproach, and outright autocracies often engage in obvious fraud, fair but low-legitimacy elections are a red flag for pre-autocracies (which doesn’t mean the system is already corrupt, but that it has become easier prey for wannabe totalitarians).

这表明了一种关键模式：虽然运转良好的民主国家拥有无可指摘的选举，而彻头彻尾的专制国家经常进行明显的舞弊，但公平但合法性低的选举对于即将成为专制国家的政权来说是一个危险信号（这并不意味着该制度已经腐败，而是意味着它更容易成为那些想要成为极权主义者的人的猎物）。

Hence, if we want to preserve democracy, we need to raise our standards for election security. It’s not enough that there is no evidence of fraud: we need systems that make fraud nearly impossible to pull off. This means taking a hard look at several vulnerable practices.

因此，如果我们想要维护民主，就必须提高选举安全标准。仅仅没有舞弊证据是不够的：我们需要建立一套几乎不可能实施舞弊的系统。这意味着我们需要认真审视一些存在漏洞的做法。

First, electronic voting machines. Even if these devices have never been hacked, their very nature, a single point of failure that’s difficult to verify, creates doubt. Moreover , when the stakes are high enough, even expensive hacking attempts become worth the investment. Instead , we should prefer methods that are harder to tamper with at scale, such as paper ballots submitted in person.

首先是电子投票机。即使这些设备从未被黑客攻击过，但它们本身的单点故障特性（难以核实）也令人担忧。此外，当事关重大时，即使代价高昂的黑客攻击也值得投入。因此，我们应该优先选择更难大规模篡改的方法，例如现场提交的纸质选票。

Second, no ID requirement for voting. This isn’t just about making fraud harder; it’s about public confidence. When a government resists implementing basic verification measures that most citizens expect, it naturally raises questions. Think of it this way: if you were designing a system to be trustworthy, wouldn’t you include ID checks?

其次，投票无需出示身份证件。这不仅仅是为了防止舞弊，更关乎公众信任。当政府拒绝实施大多数公民期望的基本核查措施时，自然会引发质疑。不妨这样想：如果你要设计一个值得信赖的系统，难道不会加入身份验证吗？

Third, mail-in ballots. Not only are they more vulnerable to large-scale tampering than in-person voting, but they also open the door to coercion. When people vote from home, nothing stops an abusive spouse, aggressive activist, or local mafioso from “helping” them fill out their ballot. Some states mitigate this risk by offering ways to cancel a coerced ballot, but many voters do not know about this option, feel too intimidated to use it, or do not care enough.

第三，邮寄选票。邮寄选票不仅比现场投票更容易受到大规模篡改，而且还为胁迫打开了方便之门。当人们在家投票时，没有任何措施可以阻止虐待配偶、激进分子或当地黑手党成员“帮助”他们填写选票。一些州通过提供取消被胁迫选票的途径来降低这种风险，但许多选民不知道有这种选择，或者因为害怕而不敢使用，或者根本不在乎。

Finally, online voting poses similar risks. Even if cryptographers made digital ballots impossible to hack, we still face the risk of coercion outlined above. The privacy of the voting booth isn’t just a tradition; it’s a crucial safeguard that protects voters from pressure and intimidation.

最后，网络投票也存在类似的风险。即使密码学家使电子选票无法被破解，我们仍然面临上文所述的胁迫风险。投票站的私密性不仅仅是一种传统，它更是一项至关重要的保障措施，能够保护选民免受压力和恐吓。

In other words, when we design election systems, we need to think not just about convenience but also about creating a voting process so secure and transparent that neither fraud nor even claims of fraud are plausible.

换句话说，我们在设计选举制度时，不仅要考虑便利性，还要考虑如何创建一个安全透明的投票过程，使得舞弊甚至舞弊指控都不可能成立。

Chapter summary

章节概要

Democratic systems often erode gradually through subtle changes that can be hard to spot until it’s too late. This chapter has outlined four critical areas where democracy’s foundations can begin to crack:

民主制度往往会通过一些不易察觉的细微变化逐渐瓦解，这些变化往往在为时已晚之前难以被发现。本章概述了民主根基可能开始出现裂痕的四个关键领域：

First , elections must do more than just count votes accurately: they need to be visibly and undeniably legitimate, and they must allow citizens to choose not only between candidates but also the candidates themselves.

首先，选举不能仅仅只是准确地统计选票：它必须具有显而易见的合法性和无可辩驳的合法性，并且必须允许公民不仅在候选人之间进行选择，而且在候选人本身之间进行选择。

Second , press freedom requires more than the absence of censorship. Modern threats to independent journalism often involve subtle pressure, selective access to power, the blurring of facts and opinion, and the choice of some newsrooms to prioritize sensationalism over substance.

其次，新闻自由不仅仅意味着没有审查制度。如今，对独立新闻业的威胁往往包括隐蔽的压力、选择性地获取权力、模糊事实与观点之间的界限，以及一些新闻机构为了追求耸人听闻而牺牲实质内容。

Third , the rule of law must apply equally to everyone. While it’s tempting to suspend legal protections for those we see as threats to democracy, this creates dangerous precedents. A society that compromises on consistent treatment, even for seemingly good reasons, weakens the very principles that protect democracy itself.

第三，法治必须平等适用于所有人。虽然暂停对那些被视为民主威胁者的法律保护看似诱人，但这会开创危险的先例。一个社会如果为了看似合理的理由而在对待所有人方面做出妥协，就会削弱维系民主本身的原则。

Finally , fighting corruption and violence is not just about maintaining order; it’s about preventing the conditions that allow autocrats to rise. When societies fail to prosecute actual crimes effectively, frustration often causes them to turn to censorship and other anti-democratic measures.

最后，打击腐败和暴力不仅仅是维护秩序，更重要的是防止独裁者崛起的土壤形成。当社会无法有效惩处犯罪行为时，挫败感往往会导致其转向审查制度和其他反民主措施。

Democracy is not something that, once achieved, it’s automatically kept forever. We must actively maintain it by protecting its core principles: legitimate elections, truthful journalism, equal treatment under the law, and effective prosecution of real crimes. When we compromise on these fundamentals, even with good intentions, we risk starting down the path toward autocracy.

民主并非一蹴而就，一旦实现便可永久维系。我们必须积极维护民主，捍卫其核心原则：合法选举、真实新闻、法律面前人人平等以及对真正犯罪行为的有效惩处。即便出于善意，一旦我们在这些基本原则上妥协，也可能导致我们走上专制之路。

If you cannot tolerate hearing falsehoods, then the day you are wrong, you will not tolerate hearing the truth.

SAMUEL FITOUSSI

如果你无法容忍谎言，那么当你犯错的那一天，你也将无法容忍真相。——塞缪尔·菲图西

No system is perfect; the choice is between the kind that weeds out errors over time and the one that lets them fester.

PER BYLUND

没有哪个系统是完美的；选择在于选择一种能随着时间推移不断淘汰错误的系统，还是选择一种任由错误滋生蔓延的系统。——佩尔·比伦德

1 Were they perfect democracies? Of course not, otherwise, they would not have degenerated into autocracies. This is precisely the point of this chapter: that many countries seem like functioning democracies until hindsight reveals they weren’t really. Hence, the need to be able to spot red flags without relying on hindsight.

1. 它们都是完美的民主国家吗？当然不是，否则它们就不会蜕变为专制国家。这正是本章的重点：许多国家表面上看起来是运转良好的民主国家，但事后看来却并非如此。因此，我们需要能够在不依赖事后诸葛亮的情况下识别出危险信号。

24

COMMUNISM AND CAPITALISM

共产主义与资本主义

W hen we label countries as “socialist” or “capitalist,” we overlook that most modern economies do not fully fit either model.

当我们给一个国家贴上“社会主义”或“资本主义”的标签时，我们忽略了大多数现代经济体并不完全符合任何一种模式。

For example, Denmark is often called “socialist,” but by socialism’s standard definition of a country whose businesses are publicly owned, it is not. Private citizens and companies own most Danish businesses, which makes it a capitalistic country; what sets Denmark apart are its extensive social programs.

例如，丹麦常被称为“社会主义国家”，但按照社会主义的标准定义——即企业公有制国家——丹麦并非社会主义国家。丹麦的大部分企业由私人公民和公司所有，这使它成为一个资本主义国家；丹麦的独特之处在于其广泛的社会福利项目。

The United States , seen as the champion of capitalism, spends over $18,000 per public school student and devotes 21% of its federal budget to Social Security . Even the most “capitalist” nation engages in significant social spending.

美国被视为资本主义的捍卫者，其公立学校学生人均支出超过18000美元，并将联邦预算的21%用于社会保障。即使是最“资本主义”的国家，也存在大量的社会支出。

Switzerland blurs public and private programs: everyone buys private health insurance, low-income citizens are subsidized, and insurers compete freely.

瑞士模糊了公共和私人项目的界限：每个人都购买私人医疗保险，低收入公民获得补贴，保险公司之间自由竞争。

Singapore appears as a free-market paradise, yet ~80% of its citizens live in public housing, and the government plays a major role in planning.

新加坡看似自由市场的天堂，但其约 80% 的公民居住在公共住房中，政府在规划中扮演着重要角色。

These examples show that asking “ Is this country socialist or capitalist?” misses the point. In this chapter, we will explore better questions.

这些例子表明，问“这个国家是社会主义国家还是资本主义国家？”这个问题并没有抓住重点。本章我们将探讨更好的问题。

Does a country respect price signals?

一个国家是否尊重价格信号？

I’m writing in January 2025, just after a devastating fire destroyed the Pacific Palisades neighborhood in Los Angeles . What’s remarkable isn’t only the fire itself but what happened months earlier: insurance companies had largely pulled out of that area, with insurer State Farm alone dropping 69.4% of its homeowner policies in that zip code.

我写这篇文章时是2025年1月，就在一场毁灭性的大火摧毁了洛杉矶太平洋帕利塞德社区之后不久。令人震惊的不仅是这场大火本身，还有几个月前发生的事情：保险公司大多撤出了该地区，仅州立农场保险公司就取消了该邮政编码区域内69.4%的房屋保险业务。

Why? California’s government limited insurers’ annual rate increases. As fire risks rose, insurers couldn’t adjust prices to match the real danger. Unable to charge sustainable rates, they stopped offering coverage. Had the government paid attention to price signals,⁠ 1 it could have anticipated the risk and increased prevention efforts. Instead , it treated rising prices as a problem to suppress and got caught unprepared.

为什么？加州政府限制了保险公司每年的保费涨幅。随着火灾风险的上升，保险公司无法调整价格以适应实际风险。由于无法收取可持续的保费，他们停止了承保。如果政府关注价格信号，就能预见风险并加大预防力度。然而，政府却将价格上涨视为需要压制的问题，结果措手不及。

This example suggests that the key difference between successful and struggling economies may not be who owns the means of production, but whether they respect price signals. Singapore illustrates this: despite heavy government involvement, it pays significant attention to market prices, helping maintain remarkable prosperity.

这个例子表明，成功经济体和困境经济体之间的关键区别可能不在于谁拥有生产资料，而在于它们是否尊重价格信号。新加坡就是一个很好的例子：尽管政府干预力度很大，但它非常重视市场价格，从而保持了显著的繁荣。

Asking “ How much does a country respect price signals?” is a more useful lens than “socialist vs. capitalist.”

比起“社会主义与资本主义”，提出“一个国家对价格信号的尊重程度如何？”这个问题更有用。

Does a country ask the right questions, and does it discuss them genuinely?

一个国家是否提出了正确的问题，并且是否真诚地讨论了这些问题？

Many people believe capitalism outperforms communism mainly because of profit incentives: the idea that people work harder when they can earn more. However , capitalism’s true strength lies in its ability to guide people toward more productive work.

许多人认为资本主义优于共产主义的主要原因是利润激励机制：人们在收入越高，工作效率就越高。然而，资本主义真正的优势在于它能够引导人们从事更高效的工作。

After all, communist economies had plenty of hard workers, too. Factory employees often worked longer hours than their Western counterparts, and their scientists and engineers were highly skilled. What they lacked wasn’t effort or talent but a system that efficiently matched people’s skills with society’s needs. Central planners often assigned people and resources poorly, leaving talent stuck in unproductive jobs.

毕竟，共产主义经济体也拥有大量勤劳的劳动力。工厂工人的工作时间通常比西方同行更长，他们的科学家和工程师也技艺精湛。他们缺乏的并非努力或才能，而是一个能够有效将人们的技能与社会需求相匹配的体系。中央计划者常常对人力和资源分配不当，导致人才被困在低效的工作岗位上。

Capitalism, despite its flaws, uses wages and opportunities to signal what use of people, tools, and land can create the most value. An engineer who might have maintained outdated machinery in a state-run factory can instead design new products in a growing industry.

尽管资本主义存在缺陷，但它仍然利用工资和机会来表明如何最大程度地利用人力、工具和土地来创造价值。一位原本可能在国营工厂维护过时机器的工程师，现在却可以在蓬勃发展的行业中设计新产品。

This redirection of talent drives prosperity. When people move freely to more valuable work, everyone benefits: workers earn more, consumers get better products at lower prices, and society grows richer. The profit incentive matters not much because it makes people work harder, but rather because it helps show us where our work is needed most.

人才的重新分配推动了繁荣。当人们可以自由地从事更有价值的工作时，每个人都会受益：工人收入增加，消费者能以更低的价格买到更好的产品，社会也变得更加富裕。利润激励之所以重要，并非因为它能促使人们更加努力地工作，而是因为它能帮助我们找到最需要我们付出努力的地方。

Most countries do not talk enough about allocating land, labor, and tools to their most productive uses and the opportunity costs of doing so. That’s a shame because countries become more prosperous when they have open and genuine discussions about productivity and poorer when they don’t.

大多数国家很少讨论如何将土地、劳动力和工具分配到最高效的用途，以及这样做的机会成本。这很可惜，因为当国家就生产力问题展开公开真诚的讨论时，它们会变得更加繁荣；反之，则会导致贫困。

Are rules designed or discovered?

规则是设计出来的还是后天形成的？

Another reason capitalism historically outperformed communism is that communism focused on designing economic rules, while capitalism focused on discovering them.

资本主义在历史上优于共产主义的另一个原因是，共产主义注重设计经济规则，而资本主义注重发现经济规则。

Of course, it’s not as clear-cut as that: communist systems also discovered some rules, and capitalist governments spend plenty of time designing rules. Still , free markets gave capitalism an extra tool to uncover the economy’s underlying rules, giving it an edge in navigating the system.

当然，事情并非如此简单：共产主义制度也发现了一些规律，资本主义政府也花费大量时间制定规则。尽管如此，自由市场仍然为资本主义提供了一种额外的工具，使其能够揭示经济的潜在规律，从而在驾驭经济体系方面占据优势。

Is the country productive enough?

这个国家的生产力足够高吗？

After World War II , East Germany’s social services lagged behind West Germany’s , not because it cared less about welfare (it arguably cared more) but because its economic system generated less wealth to redistribute, and redistributed it less efficiently.

二战后，东德的社会服务落后于西德，这并非因为东德对福利不够重视（可以说东德更重视福利），而是因为东德的经济体系创造的财富较少，可供再分配的财富也较少，而且再分配的效率也较低。

Similarly, modern China improved its welfare not by becoming more socialist (it did the opposite) but by adopting market reforms that boosted productivity.

同样，现代中国改善人民福祉的方式不是变得更加社会主义（恰恰相反），而是通过推行市场改革来提高生产力。

As we saw in the “ Abundance Equation ” chapter, a country must be productive enough to generate surplus for redistribution, public services, and a strong social net. Productivity matters more for welfare than who owns the means of production.

正如我们在“富足方程式”一章中所看到的，一个国家必须拥有足够的生产力才能创造盈余，用于再分配、公共服务和健全的社会保障体系。生产力对福利的影响远大于生产资料的所有权。

Thus, a country can be capitalist with a strong social net or communist with a weak one. If we want robust redistribution and public services, the focus should be on productivity, not ideology.

因此，一个国家可以是拥有强大社会保障体系的资本主义国家，也可以是社会保障体系薄弱的共产主义国家。如果我们想要健全的财富再分配和公共服务，重点应该放在生产力上，而不是意识形态上。

Is the rule of law consistently enforced?

法治是否得到始终如一的执行？

A brief look at history teaches us that every economic system has good and bad actors. What truly protects people’s rights and well-being isn’t whether an economy is “capitalist” or “socialist,” but whether it has a strong rule of law. Without reliable enforcement, even the best-designed system can become a tool for exploitation.

简要回顾历史便可知，任何经济体系中都存在善恶两方。真正保障人民权利和福祉的，并非经济体制是“资本主义”还是“社会主义”，而是其是否拥有健全的法治。若缺乏可靠的执法，即使是设计最精良的体系也可能沦为剥削的工具。

I have many friends working in Health , Safety , and Environment consulting, and the stories they tell me reveal a huge gap between regulations and reality. The problem is not the lack of laws (we have plenty) but the lack of consistent enforcement. Fines alone are insufficient because they rarely affect managers personally. Stronger measures, like debarments, both incentivize compliance and prevent repeat offenses.

我有很多朋友从事健康、安全和环境咨询工作，他们讲述的故事揭示了法规与现实之间存在的巨大差距。问题不在于缺乏法律（我们已经有很多法律了），而在于缺乏一致的执行。仅仅罚款是不够的，因为罚款很少会对管理人员造成直接影响。更强有力的措施，例如取消资格，既能激励企业遵守规定，又能防止再次违规。

The same applies to labor rights. Some “capitalist” countries have robust, consistently enforced worker protections, while some “socialist” countries have poor conditions despite laws on the books. The key factor is consistent enforcement, not ideology.

劳动权利也是如此。一些“资本主义”国家拥有健全且始终如一地执行的劳动者保护制度，而一些“社会主义”国家尽管有相关法律条文，劳动者的生活状况却很差。关键在于法律的持续执行，而非意识形态。

When evaluating economic systems, we should focus as much on how rules are enforced as on what they say.

在评估经济体系时，我们应该像关注规则的内容一样关注规则是如何执行的。

# ↩

Is competition strong?

竞争激烈吗？

As a thought experiment, imagine a company discovers a way to produce TVs that saves $40 per unit. Who benefits from this cost reduction, the company or the customers?

不妨做个思想实验：假设一家公司发现了一种生产电视机的方法，每台电视机可以节省 40 美元。那么，成本降低的受益者是公司还是消费者？

It depends. In a market with strong competition, companies must pass most savings to customers through lower prices. If they don’t, a competitor will do it first and take their customers. Conversely , in markets with weak competition, companies can keep most of the savings as extra profit, such as with prescription drugs still under patent protection.

这要视情况而定。在竞争激烈的市场中，公司必须将大部分节省的成本通过降低价格让利给消费者。否则，竞争对手就会抢先一步，抢走他们的客户。相反，在竞争较弱的市场中，公司可以将大部分节省的成本作为额外利润保留下来，例如仍在专利保护期内的处方药。

This principle explains why many governments work hard to prevent monopolies and protect private-sector competition. Yet they often forget about competition in public services. They run healthcare, education, and transportation as pseudo-monopolies or grant privileges to public hospitals and schools.

这一原则解释了为什么许多政府努力防止垄断，保护私营部门的竞争。然而，他们却常常忽略公共服务领域的竞争。他们以准垄断的方式运营医疗、教育和交通运输，或者给予公立医院和学校特权。

Competition in the public sector does not require privatization. A country could let public hospitals compete with each other, giving patients a choice and encouraging better service. Public schools could compete for students, teachers, and funding. In both cases, hospitals and schools would remain public and free. Competition is not about private versus public ownership but about being willing to allocate resources based on merit and create incentives for continuous improvement.

公共部门的竞争并不一定意味着私有化。一个国家可以允许公立医院之间展开竞争，让患者有更多选择，从而促进服务质量的提升。公立学校也可以竞争生源、师资和资金。在这两种情况下，医院和学校都将保持公立和免费。竞争并非关乎私有制与公有制的对立，而是关乎是否愿意根据绩效分配资源，并激励持续改进。

Contrary to common belief, these incentives do not have to be financial. From my experience leading an NGO where all staff were volunteers, what mattered was an internal meritocracy and a hierarchy of status aligned with contribution. Achieving this without financial incentives requires Direct Observations (managing where the work actually takes place⁠ 2 ) and removing the most dysfunctional individuals. Contrast this with many public schools, where principals rarely observe teachers teaching, if at all, and the worst teachers cannot be easily dismissed.

与普遍认知相反，这些激励措施并非一定要是经济上的。根据我领导一家所有员工都是志愿者的非政府组织的经验，真正重要的是内部的精英管理制度和与贡献挂钩的地位等级。要在不依赖经济激励的情况下实现这一点，需要进行直接观察（即管理实际工作发生的场所）并清除最不称职的员工。相比之下，许多公立学校的校长很少（甚至根本不）观察教师的教学，而且最差的教师也难以被解雇。

The point is that competition is vital, but does not require privatization. It requires valuing meritocracy and enabling transparency.

关键在于，竞争至关重要，但这并不意味着要实行私有化。它需要重视精英制度并实现透明化。

Communism, Capitalism, and Authoritarianism

共产主义、资本主义和威权主义

This chapter began by reflecting on how reality is often more complex than labels. Many communist countries have a private sector, and many capitalist countries have large government-owned industries.

本章首先探讨了现实往往比标签更为复杂。许多共产主义国家拥有私营部门，而许多资本主义国家也拥有庞大的国有企业。

Similarly, I do not believe capitalism is inherently good or evil. It has the potential for both, and much depends on whether the population elects competent leaders who uphold meritocracy, enforce the rule of law, and prevent abuse.

同样，我不认为资本主义本身是善或恶的。它既有可能带来善，也可能带来恶，很大程度上取决于民众能否选出称职的领导人，这些领导人能够维护精英统治、执行法治并防止滥用权力。

Conversely, I believe communism is inherently dangerous, as it has historically led to authoritarianism whenever implemented on a scale larger than a small village.

相反，我认为共产主义本质上是危险的，因为历史上，只要其规模大于一个小村庄，它就会导致专制主义。

I can already hear the objection: “ But Luca , real communism has not been tried yet. There can be communism without authoritarianism!” If that were true, everyone desiring communism would already be living in communes. Nothing stops anyone from quitting their nine-to-five and joining one. The fact that most people do not do it suggests that what they truly want requires everyone else to live under communism, too, which inevitably requires authoritarian measures.⁠ 3 ⁠ , 4

我仿佛已经听到反对的声音了：“但是卢卡，真正的共产主义还没有被实践过。共产主义也可以不伴有专制！”如果真是这样，所有渴望共产主义的人早就都住进公社了。没有人能阻止任何人辞掉朝九晚五的工作，加入公社。大多数人没有这样做，这表明他们真正想要的，是让所有人都生活在共产主义之下，而这必然需要专制措施。

# ↩

Chapter Summary

章节概要

When we move past the oversimplified labels of “capitalism” and “socialism,” we see what really makes economies work: their ability to generate wealth through productivity and through their respect for the signals prices provide, their commitment to fair law enforcement, and their willingness to harness competition, whether in the private or public sector.

当我们超越“资本主义”和“社会主义”这些过于简单的标签时，我们就能看到经济真正运作的要素：通过生产力创造财富的能力，以及对价格信号的尊重；致力于公平执法；以及利用竞争的意愿，无论是在私营部门还是公共部门。

This perspective explains why countries like Singapore and some Nordic nations thrive with very different approaches: they all respect these fundamental principles while adapting them to their circumstances. It also shows why policies that ignore these principles, such as California’s insurance price controls, often create more problems than they solve.

这种观点解释了为什么像新加坡和一些北欧国家这样的国家在采取截然不同的方法的情况下也能蓬勃发展：它们都尊重这些基本原则，同时又根据自身情况进行调整。这也解释了为什么忽视这些原则的政策，例如加州的保险价格管制，往往会带来更多的问题而不是解决问题。

The key is to care less about political systems and more about understanding and applying these core principles effectively.⁠ 5

关键在于减少对政治制度的关注，更多地理解并有效运用这些核心原则。

1 My point here is not that higher premiums would have prevented the wildfire, but that higher premiums would have signaled that prevention efforts were insufficient.

1 我的观点不是说更高的保费就能阻止野火，而是说更高的保费会表明预防措施不足。

2 A Direct Observation occurs when leaders spend time where work happens or where customers are served, directly speaking with employees. This helps leaders spot issues that reports and meetings cannot reveal.

2. 直接观察是指领导者花时间到工作场所或客户服务场所，直接与员工交谈。这有助于领导者发现报告和会议无法揭示的问题。

I describe them in detail in my 2019 book, “Best Practices for Operational Excellence.”

我在 2019 年出版的《卓越运营的最佳实践》一书中详细描述了它们。

3 On a similar note, I enjoy Chris Freiman’s quote: “If worker-owned firms are more efficient, they needn’t be mandated. If worker-owned firms are less efficient, they shouldn’t be mandated.”

3. 类似地，我很欣赏克里斯·弗雷曼的这句话：“如果工人所有制企业效率更高，就不必强制推行；如果工人所有制企业效率更低，就不应该强制推行。”

4 I cannot write about communism and capitalism without addressing a pet peeve of mine: that the main argument for communism is often financial equality.

4 如果不谈谈我最讨厌的事情，我就无法谈论共产主义和资本主义：共产主义的主要论点往往是经济平等。

I understand why money is emphasized, given communism’s poor historical record on freedom and civil rights. Still, it is striking that communist supporters who claim to value more than wealth often ignore civil liberties and instead focus on wealth while comparing communism and capitalism.

我理解为什么人们会如此强调金钱，毕竟共产主义在自由和公民权利方面有着糟糕的历史记录。然而，令人惊讶的是，那些声称重视的不仅仅是财富的共产主义支持者，在比较共产主义和资本主义时，往往忽视公民自由，反而将重点放在财富上。

One thing I respect about many supporters of communism is their dislike of fascism and other right-wing authoritarian movements. I just wish they opposed all authoritarianism, including far-left variants.

我敬佩许多共产主义支持者的一点是，他们厌恶法西斯主义和其他右翼威权运动。我只是希望他们反对一切形式的威权主义，包括极左翼的威权主义。

Since communism and fascism have been two of the deadliest ideologies in history, I propose renaming them “Red Authoritarians” and “Black Authoritarians” to remind us never to support a dictator simply because they frame themselves as champions of a noble-sounding ideology.

鉴于共产主义和法西斯主义是历史上最致命的两种意识形态，我建议将它们重新命名为“红色独裁者”和“黑色独裁者”，以提醒我们永远不要仅仅因为独裁者把自己包装成某种听起来高尚的意识形态的捍卫者就支持他们。

5 That said, capitalism has an advantage in the form of self-correcting mechanisms, such as bankruptcies, which help ensure participants follow these principles. But socialist governments could incorporate similar mechanisms as well. Nothing says that a socialist government must have exactly one bank; its government could own more than one and have them compete.

5 也就是说，资本主义的优势在于其自我纠正机制，例如破产制度，这有助于确保参与者遵守这些原则。但社会主义政府也可以引入类似的机制。并没有规定社会主义政府必须只有一家银行；政府可以拥有多家银行，并让它们相互竞争。

25

SYSTEMIC RISKS

系统性风险

O ur world faces two kinds of systemic risks. The first arises from harmful actions, such as polluting regions to the point of making them uninhabitable, or accidentally releasing a deadly virus. But there is a second, more subtle kind of risk that comes from doing nothing at all. This chapter explores this paradox through four critical challenges of our time.

我们的世界面临两种系统性风险。第一种风险源于有害行为，例如污染环境使其变得不适宜居住，或意外释放致命病毒。但还有第二种风险，更为隐蔽，它源于我们什么都不做。本章将通过探讨我们这个时代面临的四大关键挑战来剖析这一悖论。

The AI Dilemma: When Regulations Are Not Enough

人工智能困境：监管不足以解决问题

When we think about the dangers of artificial intelligence, we often picture armies of Terminator robots. But while Hollywood imagines conscious machines turning against their creators, we face a far more likely and immediate threat: the risk that foreign adversaries will use AI to gain an economic or military advantage while we lag behind.

当我们想到人工智能的危险时，脑海中常常浮现出终结者机器人大军的画面。然而，尽管好莱坞描绘的是拥有意识的机器反抗其创造者的场景，我们却面临着一个更现实、更紧迫的威胁：外国敌对势力利用人工智能获取经济或军事优势，而我们却落后于人。

Think of it as a new arms race, but instead of nuclear weapons, we’re dealing with a technology that could revolutionize everything from military strategy to economic production. If we fall behind in this race, we won’t face Terminator robots but irrelevance on the world stage, and the relative loss of prosperity and independence that comes with it.

不妨把它看作一场新的军备竞赛，但这次的对手不是核武器，而是一种可能彻底改变从军事战略到经济生产等方方面面的技术。如果我们在这场竞赛中落后，我们面临的不是终结者机器人，而是世界舞台上的边缘化，以及随之而来的繁荣和独立性的相对丧失。

This creates a thorny dilemma. If AI were being developed only in our country, we could regulate it heavily or ban it outright. But that’s not the world we live in. Restricting AI development at home is useless if other nations develop it anyway. ( Would international treaties help? Only if there’s not even a single defector, which is extremely unlikely, especially since a data center is much harder to spot than, say, an uranium enrichment facility.)

这就造成了一个棘手的难题。如果人工智能只在我国研发，我们可以对其进行严格监管甚至彻底禁止。但现实并非如此。如果其他国家仍然在研发，那么限制本国的人工智能研发就毫无意义。（国际条约会有帮助吗？只有在没有一个叛逃者的情况下才有效，但这几乎不可能，尤其考虑到数据中心比铀浓缩设施等设施更难被发现。）

Similarly, some experts suggest focusing on developing “safe AI .” While this sounds sensible, it won’t help much if others are developing AI with fewer restrictions. Similarly , banning “unsafe” AI might feel right, but unless we can enforce such a ban worldwide (and we can’t), we’re only handicapping ourselves while others race ahead.

同样，一些专家建议专注于开发“安全人工智能”。这听起来合情合理，但如果其他人开发的限制更少的人工智能，那么这种做法就无济于事。同样，禁止“不安全”人工智能或许感觉是对的，但除非我们能够在全球范围内强制执行这种禁令（而我们做不到），否则我们只会阻碍自己前进，而其他人则抢占先机。

The real solution is to acknowledge that AI development is inevitable. Under that assumption, the natural next step is to build a society ready for it. We need a population that’s robust, adaptable, and principled enough to thrive in a world where AI is as common as electricity. This isn’t something we can achieve through simple top-down regulations, which are fragile to countries defecting or researchers facing conflicts of interest. Instead , we must strengthen our formal and informal educational systems and foster a culture that can harness AI’s benefits while managing its risks. ( What should be taught? Among others, the principles outlined earlier in this book, and in particular, those around iterated games.)

真正的解决之道在于承认人工智能的发展势不可挡。基于此，下一步自然是构建一个能够适应人工智能发展的社会。我们需要一个足够强大、适应力强且恪守原则的群体，才能在人工智能像电力一样普及的世界中蓬勃发展。这并非简单的自上而下的监管就能实现的，因为这种监管方式很容易受到国家倒戈或研究人员利益冲突的影响。相反，我们必须加强正规和非正规教育体系，并培育一种能够充分利用人工智能优势并管控其风险的文化。（应该教授什么？除其他内容外，本书前面概述的原则，特别是关于迭代博弈的原则。）

We must build a society and culture that’s both able to progress strongly, so as not to fall behind less-considerate cultures, and able to swiftly and decisively pull the plug on specific dangerous projects and dangerous actors, if and when the time comes to it, instead of being endlessly divided on what needs to be done.

我们必须建设一个既能强劲进步、不落后于那些考虑不周的文化，又能在时机成熟时迅速果断地叫停某些危险项目和危险行为者的社会和文化，而不是在需要做什么的问题上无休止地争论不休。

While AI risk might seem like a technical problem requiring technical solutions, it’s actually a cultural and geopolitical problem requiring cultural and geopolitical solutions.

虽然人工智能风险看似是一个需要技术解决方案的技术问题，但实际上它是一个需要文化和地缘政治解决方案的文化和地缘政治问题。

We cannot regulate our way out of this challenge any more than we could have regulated our way out of the Industrial Revolution . Instead , we need to build a culture and society with enough common sense to thrive in an AI -powered world.

我们无法通过监管来应对这一挑战，就像我们无法通过监管来应对工业革命一样。相反，我们需要构建一种拥有足够常识的文化和社会，以便在人工智能驱动的世界中蓬勃发展。

# ↩

Climate: When Good Intentions Are Not Enough

气候：当良好的意愿不足以应对气候变化

We all share the dream of clean air and pristine wilderness. But , just like the AI challenges I covered earlier, we cannot solve environmental problems simply by writing new laws. If we implement strict environmental regulations while other countries don’t, we risk driving our industries overseas. This not only costs us jobs and makes goods more expensive, but also shifts production to places with even fewer environmental protections. As a result, global pollution may actually increase.

我们都渴望拥有洁净的空气和原始的自然风光。但是，正如我之前提到的AI挑战一样，我们不能仅仅通过制定新的法律来解决环境问题。如果我们实施严格的环境法规，而其他国家却不这样做，我们就有可能将产业转移到海外。这不仅会导致失业和商品价格上涨，还会将生产转移到环境保护力度更弱的地方。结果，全球污染实际上可能会加剧。

Of course, this doesn’t mean we should do nothing. Instead , we need to be smart about where and how we act, carefully weighing benefits and opportunity costs.

当然，这并不意味着我们应该无所作为。相反，我们需要明智地选择行动的地点和方式，仔细权衡收益和机会成本。

Take vehicle pollution, for example. Targeting the oldest, largest, and most frequently used vehicles, those responsible for the lion’s share of pollution, delivers most of the environmental benefits at a fraction of the cost of forcing everyone to buy a new electric car tomorrow.

以汽车污染为例。针对车龄最长、体积最大、使用最频繁的车辆（这些车辆是污染的主要来源），可以带来大部分环境效益，而成本却远低于强迫所有人明天就购买一辆新的电动汽车。

Moreover, clean technology is expensive. Solar panels, nuclear plants, and electric cars all require a surplus of wealth and productivity to develop, build, and buy. If excessive regulation hurts the economy, investments in a cleaner environment will be among the first to be cut. Hence , if we want to maximize environmental investments over time, we must ensure they’re economically sustainable (at the net of subsidies, of course).

此外，清洁技术成本高昂。太阳能电池板、核电站和电动汽车的研发、建设和购买都需要大量的财富和生产力。如果过度监管损害经济，那么对清洁环境的投资将首当其冲被削减。因此，如果我们想长期最大限度地发挥环境投资的作用，就必须确保这些投资在经济上是可持续的（当然，要扣除补贴）。

The lesson here echoes what we learned about AI . Systemic risks aren’t just technical or regulatory problems. They’re complex puzzles involving economics, politics, and human behavior. Finding effective solutions requires balancing competing needs and confronting false dichotomies and uncomfortable truths.

这与我们之前在人工智能领域学到的经验不谋而合。系统性风险不仅仅是技术或监管问题，它们是涉及经济、政治和人类行为的复杂难题。找到有效的解决方案需要平衡各种相互冲突的需求，并直面错误的二元对立和令人不安的真相。

# ↩

War and Peace: When Treaties Are Not Enough

战争与和平：当条约不足以解决问题时

“Peace is something systemic, not contractual,” wrote Nassim Nicholas Taleb , and history proved him right time and time again. Winning a war through brutal tactics or ending it with a hasty treaty without solving the problem from which the conflict started provides only a temporary truce.

纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布曾写道：“和平是一种系统性问题，而非契约问题。”历史一次又一次地证明了他的观点。通过残酷的战术赢得战争，或者在没有解决冲突根源问题的情况下匆忙签订条约结束战争，都只能带来暂时的休战。

Real peace needs genuine friendship and respect between ordinary citizens, not just smiling photos of presidents shaking hands. It also requires trade relationships that benefit both sides. When countries depend on each other for prosperity, they think twice before reaching for weapons. Look at Europe after World War II : former enemies became close allies largely because their economies became deeply intertwined.

真正的和平需要普通民众之间真诚的友谊和尊重，而不仅仅是总统们握手的合影。它还需要互惠互利的贸易关系。当国家彼此依赖才能繁荣发展时，它们在动用武力之前就会三思而后行。看看二战后的欧洲：昔日的敌人变成了亲密的盟友，很大程度上是因为它们的经济联系日益紧密。

Citizens and politicians alike should respect the principles we discussed in the “ Friends and Foes ” chapter. If , instead, they seek peace through polarizing methods, the peace they find won’t last long, and the aftermath will be more painful.

公民和政治家都应该尊重我们在“朋友与敌人”一章中讨论的原则。如果他们反而通过分裂的方式寻求和平，那么他们所获得的和平不会长久，而且后果会更加痛苦。

Again, the lesson is that while narrow solutions can temporarily mitigate systemic risks, systemic solutions are required for long-lasting prosperity.

这再次表明，虽然狭隘的解决方案可以暂时缓解系统性风险，但要实现长久的繁荣，需要系统性的解决方案。

Pandemic Preparedness: When Masks and Vaccines Are Not Enough

疫情防范：当口罩和疫苗不足以应对疫情时

If COVID -19 taught us anything, it’s that having the right tools is not enough: we also need people willing to use them. A vaccine in a warehouse does nothing to stop a pandemic. Masks work only if people wear them. And quarantines help only if citizens respect them.

新冠疫情教会了我们什么，那就是拥有合适的工具还不够：我们还需要愿意使用这些工具的人。仓库里的疫苗并不能阻止疫情蔓延。口罩只有在人们佩戴时才有效。隔离措施只有在民众遵守的情况下才有效。

This means public health experts need to be more than brilliant scientists; they must also be trusted communicators who can explain complex ideas clearly and address people’s questions directly instead of brushing them off with a “trust us.”

这意味着公共卫生专家不仅需要是杰出的科学家；他们还必须是值得信赖的沟通者，能够清晰地解释复杂的概念，并直接回答人们的问题，而不是用“相信我们”来敷衍了事。

Another lesson of the 2020 pandemic is that ignoring the spread of a virus only works if the illness is truly inconsequential; otherwise, it only allows the problem to grow, increasing the likelihood of more drastic solutions. As I’m fond of saying, problems grow to the size required for us to acknowledge them. The best way to avoid draconian solutions such as lockdowns and vaccine mandates is to prevent the very conditions that might lead the population to adopt them.

2020 年疫情带来的另一个教训是，忽视病毒传播只有在疾病真的无关紧要的情况下才有效；否则，只会让问题愈演愈烈，增加采取更严厉措施的可能性。正如我常说的，问题会发展到我们不得不正视的地步。避免采取封锁和强制接种疫苗等严厉措施的最佳方法是，从源头上预防可能导致民众采取这些措施的因素。

Again, systemic problems require systemic solutions (and a good dose of long-term thinking).

再次强调，系统性问题需要系统性解决方案（以及大量的长远思考）。

Building a Resilient Future

构建具有韧性的未来

A society that relies solely on regulations to manage systemic risks is fragile.

一个仅仅依靠监管来管理系统性风险的社会是脆弱的。

The previous four scenario analyses showed that true resilience also requires that:

前四项情景分析表明，真正的韧性还需要：

  • Leaders understand the complex interplay between technology, economics, geopolitics, and human behavior.
    领导者了解技术、经济、地缘政治和人类行为之间复杂的相互作用。
  • Citizens reward competent politicians and journalists over populist ones.
    民众更青睐有能力的政治家和记者，而不是民粹主义者。
  • The economy is solid enough to resist crises and has enough surplus to guarantee sustained investments in the future.
    经济结构稳健，足以抵御危机，并拥有足够的盈余来保证未来的持续投资。
  • The population is willing to adapt at the early signs of a new crisis (or, even better, before that!) and is focused enough to solve problems structurally rather than superficially.
    民众愿意在新危机的早期迹象出现时（或者更好的是，在危机出现之前！）就做出调整，并且足够专注，能够从结构上而不是表面上解决问题。
  • There is enough trust between the government and citizens to enable collective action when needed.
    政府与公民之间有足够的信任，可以在需要时采取集体行动。

The challenges our world faces are not just technical problems waiting for technical solutions (though, of course, technology plays an important and necessary role). Instead , they are complex puzzles that require us to balance competing needs, understand human nature, and think beyond quick fixes.

我们世界面临的挑战并非仅仅是等待技术解决方案的技术问题（当然，技术扮演着重要且必要的角色）。相反，它们是复杂的难题，需要我们平衡各种相互冲突的需求，理解人性，并跳出速效解决方案的局限进行思考。

The path to a more resilient future passes through acknowledging that there is no getting away with neglecting the importance of competence and trust.

通往更具韧性的未来之路，在于认识到忽视能力和信任的重要性是行不通的。

26

CHOICE AND COERCION

选择与胁迫

L et’s make a thought experiment. What would a utopia (a perfect world) look like to you? Think about its laws and policies. What rights would citizens have? What obligations?

我们来做一个思想实验。在你看来，乌托邦（一个完美的世界）会是什么样子？想想它的法律和政策。公民会拥有哪些权利？又会承担哪些义务？

Take a moment to answer these questions before reading on.

请花点时间回答以下问题，然后再继续阅读。

Do you think everyone would agree with your vision? Or would some citizens reject the rights and obligations you devised? How would you deal with dissent? And what if they still disagreed despite that?

你认为所有人都会同意你的设想吗？或者会有一些公民反对你制定的权利和义务？你会如何处理异议？如果他们即便如此仍然不同意呢？

Does your utopia feel like a utopia to them, or more like a dystopia, especially after taking into account how you will deal with dissent?

在他们眼中，你的乌托邦是乌托邦，还是反乌托邦？尤其是在考虑到你将如何处理异议之后？

This thought experiment highlights a fundamental problem: everyone imagines an ideal world differently.

这个思想实验凸显了一个根本问题：每个人对理想世界的想象都不同。

Your personal utopia might be someone else’s dystopia.

你眼中的乌托邦，可能是别人眼中的反乌托邦。

Therefore, we should shift our vision of utopia from something centered on what looks perfect to us to something centered on enabling everyone to pursue their own vision of a good life, constrained only by basic rules that prevent harm to others

因此，我们应该转变对乌托邦的理解，不再以我们认为完美的事物为中心，而是以让每个人都能追求自己理想中的美好生活为中心，仅受防止伤害他人的基本规则约束。

The Coercion Paradox

强制悖论

Almost by definition, a utopia is a place where citizens do not feel coerced. Yet , coercion comes from many sources: government, criminals, poverty, addiction, and other misfortunes. There is no world without coercion, only worlds with more or less of it.

几乎从定义上讲，乌托邦就是一个公民不会感到受到胁迫的地方。然而，胁迫的来源多种多样：政府、犯罪分子、贫困、成瘾以及其他不幸事件。没有一个世界完全没有胁迫，只有胁迫程度不同的世界。

Our goal, therefore, should not be to fully eliminate coercion (which is impossible) but to minimize it through careful trade-offs. Sometimes , a small amount of legitimate coercion, such as law enforcement, is needed to prevent much larger forms of illegitimate coercion. The key is to treat coercion as a necessary evil to be minimized, not as a tool for creating a perfect world. Here are four principles to follow:

因此，我们的目标不应该是彻底消除强制（这是不可能的），而是通过谨慎的权衡取舍来最大限度地减少强制。有时，少量合法的强制手段，例如执法，是防止更大规模的非法强制的必要之举。关键在于将强制视为一种必须尽量减少的必要之恶，而不是将其视为创造完美世界的工具。以下是四个需要遵循的原则：

1. Enforce the most important laws first. It feels tyrannical to enforce minor laws while major ones go unchecked. Moreover , tackling serious crimes often reduces the need to pursue lesser ones. For example, as we saw in an earlier chapter, prosecuting vandals and violent offenders reduces the threat posed by hate speech and its frequency.

1. 首先要执行最重要的法律。如果只执行次要的法律而对重大法律视而不见，会显得专制。此外，打击严重犯罪往往能减少追究轻微犯罪的必要性。例如，正如我们在前一章中看到的，起诉破坏公物者和暴力犯罪者可以降低仇恨言论的威胁及其发生频率。

2. Consistency matters more than severity. ⁠ 1 It is more effective and fairer to fine all speeders a little than a few of them a lot. When there is a 10 percent chance of getting caught, punishment feels arbitrary.

2. 一致性比严厉程度更重要。对所有超速者处以少量罚款比对少数超速者处以重罚更有效、更公平。当被抓的概率只有10%时，惩罚就显得随意了。

3. Speed of enforcement matters. Catching a robber years after their first crime delivers justice but risks two problems: they may have committed other crimes in the meantime, and the appearance of impunity can inspire imitators. Quick enforcement prevents both.

3. 执法速度至关重要。在劫匪首次犯罪数年后将其抓获固然伸张正义，但也存在两个风险：一是劫匪可能在此期间犯下其他罪行；二是逍遥法外的假象会助长模仿者的气焰。快速执法可以避免这两个问题。

4. Address root causes, not just symptoms. Laws often treat effects rather than causes. Double parking, for instance, is not only about rule-breaking but also about a shortage of legal parking. The fewer spaces available, the more tyrannical the fines feel. Fixing the shortage prevents most double parking and makes punishment seem fairer.

4. 要解决根本原因，而不仅仅是表面症状。法律往往只关注结果而非原因。例如，双排停车不仅仅是违反规则，还反映了合法停车位的短缺。停车位越少，罚款就越显得苛刻。解决停车位短缺问题可以有效预防大多数双排停车行为，并使处罚显得更加公平。

Just as countries have a moral duty to improve public spending efficiency before raising new taxes, they also have a duty to apply the most important laws quickly, fairly, and consistently before introducing new ones to cover for incompetence or ineffectiveness.

正如各国在提高新税之前有道德义务提高公共支出效率一样，它们也有义务在引入新法律来掩盖无能或低效之前，迅速、公平、一致地执行最重要的法律。

The Scale Problem

尺度问题

“I am a libertarian at the federal level, a Republican at the state level, a Democrat at the local level, and a socialist with family and friends."

NASSIM NICHOLAS TALEB

“在联邦层面，我是自由意志主义者；在州层面，我是共和党人；在地方层面，我是民主党人；但在家人和朋友面前，我却是一个社会主义者。”——纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布

A system that works perfectly in a small community where everyone knows each other might be disastrous in a country of millions.⁠ 2 What works as a utopia at one scale often becomes dystopian at another.

在一个彼此熟识的小社区里完美运行的系统，在一个拥有数百万人口的国家里可能会变成灾难。在一种规模下堪称乌托邦的模式，在另一种规模下往往会变成反乌托邦。

Therefore, we need systems that can function at scale. Two stand out.

因此，我们需要能够大规模运行的系统。其中有两个系统尤为突出。

The first is federalism, which scales by adopting a fractal structure that keeps local units small. Its core principle is that centralization is a necessary evil to be minimized and restricted to functions that truly require it, such as foreign policy.

第一种是联邦制，它通过采用分形结构来实现规模化，使地方单位保持较小的规模。其核心原则是，中央集权是一种必要的恶，应尽可能减少，并限制在真正需要它的功能范围内，例如外交政策。

The second is the market mechanism. Markets are not perfect, but they scale well. They fail in three main ways: excessive government intervention that distorts them, insufficient intervention that lets participants form cartels, and the absence of a rule of law. Thus , markets work best when the government protects citizens’ rights and upholds a strong rule of law while refraining from manipulating or influencing the markets themselves.

第二点是市场机制。市场并非完美无缺，但其规模效应良好。市场失效主要体现在三个方面：政府过度干预导致市场扭曲、干预不足导致市场参与者形成垄断集团，以及法治缺失。因此，当政府在保护公民权利、维护强有力的法治的同时，避免操纵或影响市场本身时，市场机制才能发挥最佳效用。

Markets as Freedom Maximizers

市场作为自由最大化器

Market mechanisms help build prosperity while maximizing freedom. Take employment: society needs certain jobs done, but how do we ensure people do them without coercion? The answer is market-based compensation. If wages are equal, most people would choose the easiest or most prestigious jobs, leaving essential but less appealing work unfilled; but with wages set by demand and supply, we can ensure that all jobs are filled as close as possible to what society needs without any coercion required.

市场机制有助于在最大限度保障自由的同时促进繁荣。以就业为例：社会需要某些工作，但我们如何确保人们在不强迫的情况下从事这些工作呢？答案是基于市场的薪酬体系。如果工资水平相同，大多数人会选择最轻松或最体面的工作，导致那些重要但吸引力较低的工作无人问津；但如果工资由供求关系决定，我们就能确保所有工作岗位都能尽可能地满足社会需求，而无需任何强迫手段。

To clarify this concept, imagine you can choose between two equally paid jobs: an interesting job as a theater actor or a boring job as a tax accountant. You would probably choose acting, and most people would too. This would create an excess of actors and a shortage of tax accountants. One option is to force people into these jobs, but that is neither practical nor compatible with a utopia. A better option is to let wages adjust: tax accountant pay rises until enough people take the job, while actor pay falls until demand balances.⁠ 3

为了阐明这个概念，想象一下，你可以选择两份收入相同的工作：一份是充满乐趣的戏剧演员工作，另一份是枯燥乏味的税务会计工作。你很可能会选择演员，大多数人也会如此。这将导致演员过剩，而税务会计短缺。一种解决办法是强迫人们从事这些工作，但这既不现实，也不符合理想状态。更好的办法是让工资自行调整：税务会计的工资上涨，直到有足够多的人从事这份工作；而演员的工资下降，直到供需平衡。

(Remember that market equilibria are important not only because shortages in essential jobs are harmful, but also because having more people in a job than demand warrants comes with large opportunity costs.)

（请记住，市场均衡之所以重要，不仅是因为基本岗位短缺会造成危害，还因为就业人数超过需求会带来巨大的机会成本。）

At first glance, pay gaps might seem unfair, but that is only if we focus solely on money. Jobs come with hidden rewards and costs that matter just as much as the paycheck. For example, actors often earn less in dollars but gain status, creative fulfillment, and the thrill of performance, whereas tax accountants earn more money but face hidden costs such as stress, tedium, and long hours hunched over spreadsheets. These non-financial factors clearly matter: just look at how many talented people chase acting careers despite low pay.

乍一看，薪酬差距似乎不公平，但这只是因为我们只关注金钱。工作除了薪水之外，还包含其他隐性回报和成本，这些同样重要。例如，演员的收入通常较低，但他们能获得社会地位、创作成就感和表演的刺激；而税务会计师的收入更高，却要承担压力、枯燥乏味的工作以及长时间伏案工作等隐性成本。这些非经济因素显然至关重要：看看有多少才华横溢的人不顾低收入，仍然选择从事演艺事业就知道了。

This is not to say unfair wages never exist. They do, but they usually result from a lack of market-based wages rather than an excess. Some professions, like notaries, have artificially high pay due to regulations limiting entry, while others, like agricultural work, have artificially low pay because regulations restrict mobility and bargaining power.

这并非否认不公平工资的存在。不公平工资确实存在，但通常是由于市场工资水平不足而非过剩造成的。某些职业，例如公证员，由于准入限制而导致工资人为偏高；而另一些职业，例如农业劳动，由于流动性和议价能力受限而导致工资人为偏低。

The point is that forcing equal wages would increase unfairness, since different jobs carry different non-financial costs and rewards.

关键在于，强制同工同酬会加剧不公平现象，因为不同的工作会带来不同的非经济成本和回报。

A truly fair system would instead remove barriers that prevent people from making free and informed career choices: cartels and wage-fixing regulations, artificial limits on professional licenses, and opacity around salaries and advancement opportunities. Reducing these barriers does more for fairness than manipulating wages ever could.

一个真正公平的体系应该消除阻碍人们自由、知情地做出职业选择的障碍：例如垄断集团和工资操纵法规、人为设定的专业执照限制，以及薪资和晋升机会方面的不透明性。减少这些障碍比操纵工资更能促进公平。

Financial and Non-Financial Assets

金融资产和非金融资产

Let’s expand on the idea that wealth should not be measured purely in financial terms.

让我们进一步阐述财富不应该仅仅用金钱来衡量的观点。

Imagine two twins, Alice and Bob , raised the same way and living identical lives until high school graduation. In her 20s, Alice travels, works low-paying but stress-free jobs, and enjoys life. Conversely , Bob spends his 20s studying and working hard. By age 30, Bob appears much wealthier to the tax authorities, pays more taxes, and has less access to federal aid. Yet if we measure wealth more broadly, not just in dollars, Alice also has valuable assets Bob lacks, such as fun experiences, friendships, and personal fulfillment. From this perspective, they might be equally wealthy, just in different ways.⁠ 4 Measuring wealth purely financially overstates inequality.

想象一下，一对双胞胎，爱丽丝和鲍勃，从小接受同样的教育，过着完全相同的生活，直到高中毕业。二十多岁时，爱丽丝四处旅行，从事着收入不高但压力较小的工作，享受着生活。相反，鲍勃则在二十多岁时努力学习和工作。到了三十岁，鲍勃在税务机关眼中显得更加富有，缴纳的税款更多，获得的联邦援助也更少。然而，如果我们更广泛地衡量财富，而不仅仅用金钱来衡量，爱丽丝还拥有鲍勃所缺乏的宝贵资产，例如美好的经历、真挚的友谊和个人的成就感。从这个角度来看，他们或许同样富有，只是财富的体现方式不同。仅仅用金钱来衡量财富会夸大不平等。

This is not to claim that everyone is equally wealthy: clearly, some have more financial and non-financial assets than others, or have benefited from undeserved luck. Instead , my point is that financial inequality does not equal overall inequality, and efforts to eliminate financial inequality can be unfair if they increase total inequality when both financial and non-financial wealth are considered. This happens, for example, in countries where able-bodied people receive generous benefits without working, ending up with slightly lower income but a higher quality of life than their working-class neighbors.

这并非声称人人财富水平相同：显然，有些人比其他人拥有更多的金融和非金融资产，或者受益于不应得的运气。我的观点是，经济不平等并不等同于整体不平等，如果消除经济不平等的努力在考虑金融和非金融财富后反而加剧了整体不平等，那么这些努力就可能是不公平的。例如，在一些国家，身强力壮的人无需工作就能获得丰厚的福利，最终他们的收入略低于工薪阶层邻居，但生活质量却更高，这种情况就时有发生。

Conclusion

结论

The path to utopia does not lie in any single person’s vision of perfection. It requires balancing competing visions while minimizing unnecessary coercion.

通往乌托邦的道路并非在于任何个人对完美的设想。它需要在平衡各种相互冲突的愿景的同时，最大限度地减少不必要的强制措施。

We must accept that the world will never be perfect for everyone. Instead , we should aim for a system where people can freely pursue their vision of a good life, constrained only by basic rules that prevent harm to others.

我们必须接受这样一个事实：世界永远不可能对每个人都完美无缺。相反，我们应该努力构建一个让人们能够自由追求美好生活的体系，而唯一的约束就是防止伤害他人的基本规则。

1 Are “Enforce the most important laws first” and “consistency matters more than severity” at odds? Not at all. Enforce the most important laws first and enforce them consistently.

1. “优先执行最重要的法律”和“一致性比严厉性更重要”相互矛盾吗？完全不矛盾。应该优先执行最重要的法律，并且始终如一地执行。

2 Why can small-scale communism work but not large-scale communism?

2 为什么小规模共产主义可以成功，而大规模共产主义却不行？

Any economic system needs a way to identify who adds value and who does not, so that resources can be directed to the former and freeloaders can be held accountable. Communism handles this through official evaluation: officials assess companies and individuals to decide who deserves what. This can work at small scales, where officials (or community members) personally know the people and products involved, but it fails at larger scales where such knowledge is absent.

任何经济体系都需要一种方法来识别谁创造了价值，谁没有创造价值，以便将资源导向创造价值者，并追究搭便车者的责任。共产主义通过官方评估来解决这个问题：官员对公司和个人进行评估，以决定谁应获得什么。这种方法在小规模范围内可能有效，因为官员（或社区成员）对相关人员和产品非常了解；但在大规模范围内，由于缺乏这种信息，这种方法就失效了。

Capitalism uses a different mechanism: profit. Profit works better as a large-scale measuring stick because it does not require personal knowledge and is harder to fake.

资本主义采用的是不同的机制：利润。利润作为大规模衡量标准更为有效，因为它不需要个人知识，也更难造假。

3 A telling anecdote comes from France, at a retailer called Next. A group of store employees sued the company, claiming it was unfair that they earned less than their warehouse colleagues. They won the trial and received a substantial payment.

3 一个颇具启发性的案例来自法国，一家名为Next的零售商。一群门店员工起诉公司，声称他们的收入低于仓库同事，这很不公平。他们最终胜诉，并获得了一笔可观的赔偿。

One wonders why they did not apply for the higher-paying warehouse positions. This suggests there was likely a good reason why those jobs paid more.

人们不禁要问，他们为什么不申请薪水更高的仓库职位？这表明，那些工作薪水更高很可能是有原因的。

Source: “'We did it!' Next shop workers win equal pay claim,” the BBC, 2024-08-27.

来源：“‘我们做到了！’ Next 商店员工赢得同工同酬诉求”，BBC，2024-08-27。

4 “But Luca, Alice’s wealth is not true wealth; it cannot buy medical treatment if needed.” Yes, but by the same argument, Bob’s wealth cannot buy many of Alice’s experiences either (it can buy a trip, but it cannot buy those experiences that are much easier to have when you’re young, fit, and careless).

4 “但是卢卡，爱丽丝的财富不是真正的财富；如果需要，它买不起医疗。” 是的，但按照同样的逻辑，鲍勃的财富也买不到爱丽丝的许多经历（它可以买得起旅行，但它买不到那些在你年轻、健康、无忧无虑的时候更容易获得的经历）。

# ↩

CONCLUSIONS OF PART III

第三部分结论

T he populations of prosperous countries must not let their guard down. Democracies can quickly slide into autocracies, and strong economies can unravel surprisingly fast.

富裕国家的民众绝不能放松警惕。民主政体可能迅速滑向专制政体，强大的经济体也可能在出人意料的时间内崩溃瓦解。

This often happens when people convince themselves that the current system is failing but adopt an even worse one. For example, problems like poverty and corruption are often blamed on capitalism, yet they also exist in other systems, often more severely. This is not to claim our systems are perfect, but to caution against overestimating how flawed they are compared to alternatives.

这种情况经常发生，人们往往认为现有体制已经失败，却转而接受一个更糟糕的体制。例如，贫困和腐败等问题常常被归咎于资本主义，但这些问题在其他体制中也同样存在，而且往往更为严重。这并非要宣称我们的体制完美无缺，而是要提醒人们不要高估现有体制与其他体制相比的缺陷程度。

To understand this, it is crucial to have a clear and realistic view of how the world has changed over recent decades. The thought experiment on the next page will help with this.

要理解这一点，至关重要的是要对近几十年来世界发生的变化有一个清晰而现实的认识。下一页的思维实验将有助于我们做到这一点。

# ↩

Reversing the arrow of time

逆转时间之箭

Some people believe the world has gotten worse. I disagree. Consider what would happen if the arrow of time were reversed: we would progressively lose technologies, social rights, and access to goods and services that we now take for granted.

有些人认为世界变得更糟了。我不同意。试想一下，如果时间倒流会发生什么：我们会逐渐失去现在习以为常的技术、社会权利以及商品和服务。

Go 20 years back in time, and access to the internet disappears, but only for the bottom half of society. Go 40 years back in time, and we lose mobile phones, cars get less safe and more polluting, and houses get smaller and worse equipped, especially for the poorest half. Go 60 years back in time, and plenty of rights disappear, especially for those at the bottom of society (think about racial segregation). Go back 75 years, and plumbing disappears, but only in the houses of the poorest 30%.⁠ 1 Go back 150 years, and people worked much longer hours (the average US manufacturing worker worked 10 hours a day, 6 days a week), and their life was much shorter (in the US , it was slightly more than 40 years, also due to child mortality).

时光倒流20年，互联网消失了，但仅限于社会底层一半的人口。时光倒流40年，我们失去了手机，汽车变得越来越不安全、污染越来越严重，房屋越来越小、设施越来越简陋，尤其对于最贫困的一半人口而言更是如此。时光倒流60年，许多权利消失了，尤其对于社会底层的人们而言（想想种族隔离）。时光倒流75年，自来水消失了，但仅限于最贫困的30%的人口。时光倒流150年，人们的工作时间更长（美国制造业工人平均每天工作10小时，每周工作6天），寿命也更短（在美国，平均寿命略高于40岁，部分原因是儿童死亡率高）。

So why do some claim the world is getting worse? Sometimes they focus on specific places, like isolated villages left behind when jobs moved elsewhere, ignoring broader society. Other times, expectations have grown faster than the economy: housing prices may have risen, but it’s often because people want larger and better-equipped homes in more desirable locations with more opportunities and services than their grandparents ever had. Still other times, they focus on aspects of life that have worsened, such as weaker familial ties. While I agree with this, these are areas where we have individual choice, whereas areas beyond our control (civil rights, access to healthcare and education, and basic living standards) have generally improved over time. This suggests that those who feel life has worsened over recent decades are likely among the luckiest in the luckiest parts of the world; for the vast majority (basically, everyone except the top strata of society in the wealthiest countries), life has significantly improved over the past few decades.

那么，为什么有些人会说世界正在变糟呢？有时，他们关注的是特定地区，比如工作机会流失后留下的偏远村庄，而忽略了更广泛的社会层面。有时，人们的期望增长速度超过了经济增长速度：房价上涨，但这通常是因为人们想要更大、设施更完善的住宅，位于更理想的地段，拥有比祖辈更多的机会和服务。还有一些时候，他们关注的是生活中某些方面恶化，例如家庭关系的疏远。我同意这种观点，但这些领域是我们个人可以选择的，而我们无法控制的领域（公民权利、医疗和教育资源以及基本生活水平）总体上随着时间的推移而有所改善。这表明，那些感觉近几十年生活变糟的人，很可能是世界上最幸运地区中最幸运的人；对于绝大多数人（基本上，除了最富裕国家的顶层人群之外的所有人）来说，过去几十年生活水平显著提高。

The point is, when we lose sight of how far we’ve come, we risk dismantling the very foundations that made this progress possible. That is why this book argues for improving, not replacing, our existing systems.

关键在于，如果我们忽视了我们已经取得的成就，就有可能动摇支撑这些进步的根基。因此，本书主张改进而非取代我们现有的体系。

1 Source: “Historical Census of Housing Tables: Plumbing,” 1990, the US Census Bureau.

1 资料来源：“历史住房普查表：管道”，1990 年，美国人口普查局。

# ↩

CONCLUSIONS

结论

Prosperity is far more fragile than we like to admit. We should never take it for granted. In fact, complacency is the greatest danger. While we should enjoy the benefits of our current prosperity, we shall never forget what built it: the ingenuity and care that increased productivity, and the discipline to create more than we consume.

繁荣远比我们愿意承认的要脆弱得多。我们绝不应将其视为理所当然。事实上，自满才是最大的危险。我们固然应该享受当前繁荣带来的种种益处，但绝不能忘记它背后的缔造者：是提高生产力的智慧和匠心，以及创造大于消费的自律精神。

Our society drifts toward decline when we:

当我们这样做时，我们的社会就会走向衰落：

  • Allow the government to spend public money carelessly.
    允许政府随意挥霍公共资金。
  • Forget that everyone’s prosperity depends on Average National Productivity .
    别忘了，每个人的繁荣都取决于国民平均生产率。
  • Dismiss market prices as unfair instead of seeing them as vital economic signals.
    将市场价格视为不公平现象而予以否定，而不是将其视为重要的经济信号。
  • Let partisan politics override competent governance.
    让党派政治凌驾于称职的政府之上。
  • Focus on the urgent at the expense of the important.
    优先处理紧急事项而忽略重要事项。

Each of these pitfalls stems from the same root: a failure to take a moment to ask ourselves hard, honest questions. In fact, the recipe for prosperity is precisely to keep the important in mind at all times, despite what may feel urgent in the immediate.

这些陷阱都源于同一个根源：我们未能抽出时间认真地问自己一些尖锐而诚实的问题。事实上，通往成功的秘诀恰恰在于始终牢记真正重要的事情，即便眼前的事情看似紧急。

Better questions

更好的问题

Let’s end this book with the question that started it.

让我们以本书开篇提出的问题来结束这本书吧。

What causes prosperity?

什么因素会带来繁荣？

Is it natural resources? They help, but many resource-rich nations remain poor. Is it capitalism? Is it democracy? These matter, but many capitalistic and democratic countries have seen their wealth decline in recent decades.

是自然资源吗？自然资源固然重要，但许多资源丰富的国家仍然贫穷。是资本主义吗？是民主制度吗？这些固然重要，但许多资本主义和民主国家在近几十年都经历了财富缩水。

In fact, looking at the ups and downs of capitalistic countries probably offers the best answer. In the 20th century, capitalistic countries grew extraordinarily prosperous because they asked themselves better questions and answered them more truthfully.

事实上，考察资本主义国家的兴衰或许能提供最佳答案。20世纪，资本主义国家之所以能取得非凡的繁荣，是因为它们提出了更好的问题，并给出了更真实的答案。

Which jobs add the most value? Where is money better allocated? Where do benefits exceed the costs? These are all excellent prompts that every person and company had to ask, explicitly or implicitly, and to which they received a genuine answer. The results manifested in the form of good decisions that created prosperity.

哪些工作最有价值？资金应该如何更有效地分配？哪些方面的收益大于成本？这些都是每个人和公司都必须思考或隐含地提出的重要问题，而且他们也都得到了真实的答案。最终，这些问题转化为能够创造繁荣的明智决策。

Conversely, in the 21st century, debt and subsidies obfuscated reality in much of the Western World , and complacency and virtue signaling took over. Some countries started asking themselves worse questions and answering them less honestly. The result was stagnation first, and now a trajectory angling towards poverty, whose severity the population doesn’t even feel because unsustainable levels of debt keep the quality of life afloat, for the moment.

相反，在21世纪，债务和补贴掩盖了西方世界大部分地区的现实，自满和虚伪的道德作秀盛行。一些国家开始反思更严峻的问题，却未能坦诚作答。其结果首先是经济停滞，如今则走上了一条通往贫困的道路，而民众却并未感受到贫困的严重性，因为不可持续的债务水平暂时维持了他们的生活质量。

This highlights the root of the problem and its solution. We should return to asking ourselves better questions and answering them more truthfully.

这凸显了问题的根源及其解决方法。我们应该重新审视问题，提出更好的问题，并更诚实地回答这些问题。

Raise the quality of the discourse and prioritize discussing the important over the urgent. Do not reward those who distract or divide us, and let them fade into irrelevance. Focus not on winning the next elections, but on ensuring that the next few governments will be competent.

提升讨论质量，优先讨论重要事项而非紧急事项。不要奖励那些分散我们注意力或分裂我们的人，让他们逐渐被边缘化。重点不应放在赢得下次选举上，而应放在确保未来几届政府能够胜任工作上。

It’s well worth it.

非常值得。

# ↩

EPILOGUE

结语

I n today’s news,⁠ 1 I read that the Swiss canton of Bâle is returning about $235 a month to taxpayers because its public coffers are too full.⁠ 2 This is the way.

在今天的新闻中，我看到瑞士巴伐利亚州每月向纳税人返还约 235 美元，因为其公共财政收入过剩。这就是方法。

I do not believe taxes are inherently greedy, but I do believe it is greedy to spend tax money poorly and then ask for more. Here , the Swiss administration demonstrates competence and reasonableness.

我不认为税收本身是贪婪的，但我认为浪费税款然后还要求更多才是贪婪。在这方面，瑞士政府展现出了能力和合理性。

It all comes down to productivity: in this case, spending productivity. A competent government would rank projects by decreasing efficiency and only fund those that improve life substantially relative to their cost. Any surplus should be returned to taxpayers, who will spend or invest it, not just creating jobs, but crucially, the very jobs they need.

一切最终都归结于效率：在这个例子中，指的是支出效率。一个称职的政府会按照效率递减的原则对项目进行排序，只资助那些能够显著改善民生且成本远低于实际效益的项目。任何盈余都应该返还给纳税人，由他们用于消费或投资，不仅创造就业机会，更重要的是，创造他们真正需要的就业机会。

Over time, society may grow to respect productivity and opportunity costs more deeply. People will realize how much their welfare depends on average societal productivity and will treat the subject with the seriousness it deserves.

随着时间的推移，社会可能会更加深刻地重视生产力和机会成本。人们会意识到自身福祉在多大程度上依赖于社会平均生产力，并会以应有的严肃态度对待这一问题。

Ultimately, the quality of the discourse will determine whether our future is poor or prosperous: how seriously we discuss what matters versus what does not, and whether we do so in good faith.

最终，讨论的质量将决定我们的未来是贫穷还是繁荣：我们讨论重要的事情与不重要的事情的认真程度，以及我们是否出于善意进行讨论。

ABOUT THE AUTHOR

关于作者

LUCA DELLANNA

卢卡·德拉纳

Luca has been supporting senior leaders on risk-, operations-, and people- management as an independent expert for over 12 years.

12 年来，Luca 一直作为独立专家为高层领导提供风险、运营和人员管理方面的支持。

For some clients, he acts as an on-demand advisor to provide expertise in his areas of competence. For others, he conducts short workshops to efficiently increase the managerial capabilities of their leaders. Sometimes , he also conducts short on-site consulting engagements and benchmark audits.

他为部分客户提供按需咨询服务，在其专业领域内提供专业知识。对于其他客户，他则举办短期研讨会，以有效提升其领导者的管理能力。有时，他还会开展短期现场咨询项目和标杆审计。

In addition to his advisory activity, Luca is an external lecturer at an Italian university and frequently speaks at conferences and internal company events. Luca is also the author of eleven books and an independent researcher in economics, behavioral sciences, and public health, and has presented at large conferences and won international research grants.

除了担任顾问外，卢卡还是意大利一所大学的客座讲师，经常在各种会议和公司内部活动中发表演讲。卢卡著有11本书，是一位经济学、行为科学和公共卫生领域的独立研究员，曾在大型会议上发表论文，并获得过国际研究资助。

Trained as an automotive engineer, Luca led large teams and consulted for large multinationals before quitting his corporate job in 2015 to become an independent advisor, researcher, and author. After living in Spain , Germany , and Singapore , he returned to his hometown of Turin ( Italy ).

Winning Long-Term Games

赢得长期比赛

The key to winning long-term games is to stop playing them as a succession of separate short-term games.

赢得长期比赛的关键在于停止将比赛视为一系列独立的短期比赛。

Yet, most people take the opposite approach. Here are three examples:

然而，大多数人却采取相反的做法。以下是三个例子：

  • The manager who sees each interaction with her team as a separate game. Every time she talks to her subordinates, it’s to get things done rather than develop their skills. As a result, she fails to build the long-term assets (a competent team) she needs in order to win her long-term game (a successful career).
    这位管理者将与团队的每一次互动都视为一场独立的游戏。她每次与下属交谈，都是为了完成任务，而不是为了培养他们的技能。结果，她无法建立起赢得长期目标（成功职业生涯）所需的长期资产（一支称职的团队）。
  • The spouse who lies to avoid responsibility. If lying has, say, a 1% chance of being discovered, it is a great short-term tactic (it succeeds 99% of the time) but a terrible long-term strategy (if you lie once a week, you have a 99.5% chance of getting caught over a decade).
    配偶为了逃避责任而撒谎。如果撒谎被发现的概率只有 1%，那么这是一种很好的短期策略（成功率高达 99%），但从长远来看却是一种糟糕的策略（如果你每周撒谎一次，那么十年后你被发现的概率高达 99.5%）。
  • The solopreneur who sends weekly emails to their mailing list and sees each as a separate game. They consume their audience’s trust to generate more sales within a single email instead of building trust to create more sales within a few months.
    有些个体创业者每周都会向邮件列表发送邮件，并将每次发送都视为一场独立的游戏。他们为了在单封邮件中提升销量而消耗受众的信任，而不是通过几个月的时间来建立信任，最终实现销售增长。

These three examples show that approaching long-term games as a succession of separate short-term games is a bad strategy despite working great over short time horizons.

这三个例子表明，尽管在短期内效果很好，但将长期博弈视为一系列独立的短期博弈是一种糟糕的策略。

In “ Winning Long - Term Games ,” Luca guides the reader into designing strategies that not only have a long-term horizon but also leverage the long term to gain an edge against anyone with shorter time horizons and make success all but inevitable.

在《赢得长期博弈》一书中，卢卡指导读者设计策略，这些策略不仅具有长远的眼光，而且还利用长远优势来对抗那些眼光较短的人，从而使成功几乎成为必然。
